A credible pathway requires a defined CT-protocol eligibility check; pre-specified vertebral region of interest and exclusions; protocol- and contrast-aware quantification; scanner-specific quality assurance and calibration monitoring where applicable; external validation in representative populations; and an explicit route from an AI alert to confirmatory testing and treatment evaluation. AI may also enable concurrent vertebral-fracture and body-composition assessment, but clinical utility must be shown through downstream testing, treatment, fracture, workload, equity, and cost outcomes. The near-term priority is therefore not higher retrospective diagnostic performance alone, but reproducible, transparent, and prospectively evaluated integration into radiology workflows.
42881289:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of balloon-occluded transarterial chemoembolization (B-TACE) compared with conventional (cTACE) and drug-eluting-bead transarterial chemoembolization (DEB-TACE) in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted following PRISMA guidelines and registered in PROSPERO. PubMed, Scopus, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched to 8 February 2026 for randomized and observational studies comparing B-TACE with cTACE or DEB-TACE. Tumor response (mRECIST), overall survival, and adverse events were pooled using random-effects models; risk of bias was assessed with established tools.
RESULTS: Nine studies (one randomized, eight observational; 1534 patients) were included. Complete response, objective response, disease control, and progressive disease did not differ significantly between groups, with moderate-to-substantial heterogeneity. Baseline tumors were larger in the balloon-occluded group (mean difference 4.34 mm; 95% CI 1.18- 7.50; p = 0.014). Exploratory study-level analyses suggested greater relative B-TACE effects with larger tumors, particularly for complete response and disease control.Overall survival favored B-TACE in the two studies with extractable hazard ratios (HR 0.41; 95% CI 0.23 to 0.73; p = 0.002). Post-treatment liver enzymes, bilirubin, fever, and post-embolization syndrome did not differ significantly.
CONCLUSION: No statistically significant differences in imaging response or safety were observed between intervention and comparator groups, while B-TACE was associated with a signal toward improved overall survival despite larger baseline tumors. Exploratory findings suggested that larger tumor size may be associated with a greater relative B-TACE effect. Given the limited evidence, these findings require confirmation in randomized controlled trials.
42886241:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: The comparative effects of intravenous thrombolytic agents, endovascular thrombectomy (EVT), and bridging therapy in imaging-selected patients with acute ischemic stroke treated beyond 4.5 hours remain uncertain. We compared these strategies while distinguishing confirmed large-vessel occlusion (LVO) evidence from broader mixed populations.
METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library for randomized trials evaluating reperfusion treatments administered 4.5 to 24 hours after stroke onset or last known well. The primary network included trials requiring confirmed intracranial LVO or basilar artery occlusion (BAO). An anterior-circulation LVO network and an all-available network were examined as sensitivity and exploratory analyses. Bayesian random-effects consistency models estimated odds ratios (ORs) with 95% credible intervals (CrIs). The primary outcome was functional independence, defined as a modified Rankin Scale score of 0 to 2 at 90 days.
RESULTS: Fifteen randomized trials were included, of which 8 contributed to the primary confirmed LVO/BAO network. Compared with placebo or best medical care, EVT significantly improved functional independence (OR, 2.93 [95% CrI, 1.40-6.53]) and excellent functional outcome, defined as mRS 0 to 1 (OR, 2.22 [95% CrI, 1.30-4.11]), reduced 90-day mortality (OR, 0.71 [95% CrI, 0.50-0.98]), and increased trial-defined recanalization or reperfusion at approximately 24 hours (OR, 5.27 [95% CrI, 1.83-16.04]); sICH was also increased (OR, 2.65 [95% CrI, 1.28-5.81]). Compared with EVT, tenecteplase plus EVT showed numerically favorable but statistically inconclusive estimates for functional independence (OR, 1.10 [95% CrI, 0.34-3.52]) and excellent outcome (OR, 1.16 [95% CrI, 0.52-2.64]). Direct pairwise analyses of 2 trials were similarly inconclusive. Tenecteplase alone did not show clear differences from placebo or best medical care. Findings were directionally consistent in the anterior-circulation sensitivity and all-available exploratory networks.
CONCLUSIONS: Among imaging-selected patients with confirmed intracranial LVO or BAO treated 4.5 to 24 hours after onset or last known well, EVT had the most consistent evidence of benefit versus placebo or best medical care. Tenecteplase plus EVT showed favorable but imprecise estimates, and neither network nor direct pairwise analyses established superiority over EVT alone. The incremental benefit of bridging tenecteplase remains uncertain.
42886364: Multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI) has become integral to the detection, localization, risk stratification, and management of prostate cancer. Increasing utilization of prostate MRI in screening, active surveillance, targeted biopsy guidance, and treatment planning has amplified the demand for faster imaging protocols while maintaining high diagnostic quality. Conventional MRI acceleration strategies, including parallel imaging and compressed sensing, improve acquisition efficiency but remain limited by trade-offs involving signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), image sharpness, artifacts, and reconstruction complexity. Deep learning reconstruction (DLR) has emerged as a promising artificial intelligence-based approach for MRI acceleration and image enhancement. Unlike traditional reconstruction methods that rely primarily on predefined mathematical models, DLR uses neural networks to learn image priors and reconstruction features from MRI data. Published studies suggest that DLR may enable accelerated acquisitions while maintaining or, in some settings, improving image quality through denoising, artifact reduction, and improved spatial resolution and lesion conspicuity. However, these effects vary according to the reconstruction algorithm, sequence, acceleration factor, and clinical setting. Variational networks combine physics-based MRI constraints with learned regularization and represent an important framework for DLR. In prostate MRI, available studies have reported substantial reductions in acquisition time for T2-weighted and diffusion-weighted imaging while generally maintaining perceived image quality. Reported benefits include improved lesion conspicuity, reader confidence, and delineation of anatomic structures. Current evidence suggests that DLR generally preserves PI-RADS assessment and diagnostic performance rather than systematically altering lesion categorization; however, evidence demonstrating improvements in diagnostic accuracy or clinical outcomes remains limited. Important limitations include vendor and algorithm dependence, potential reconstruction artifacts, variability in quantitative imaging metrics, limited multicenter validation, and uncertain generalizability across scanners, protocols, and clinical settings. This review summarizes the technical principles underlying DLR, discusses current clinical applications in prostate MRI, highlights representative studies and workflow implications, reviews limitations, and outlines future directions for this rapidly evolving technology.
42886874:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Spontaneous intracranial hypotension (SIH) results from spinal CSF leakage. Epidural blood patch (EBP) is an important first-line treatment. However, pre-EBP, intra-EBP, and post-EBP practice varies widely owing to limited consensus guidance. We aimed to develop expert consensus statements to support clinical decision-making in SIH management, including peri-EBP practices, focusing on patients with spinal longitudinal epidural CSF collection (SLEC) before definitive leak type classification.
METHODS: An international multidisciplinary Delphi process was conducted between January 2024 and July 2025, involving experts in neurology, neurosurgery, radiology, and anesthesiology. Consensus was defined a priori as ≥70% agreement for strong agreement, 60%-69% for partial agreement, and <60% for no consensus, based on a 5-point Likert scale in round 3. Responses were collected anonymously using an online survey platform, with summarized feedback from the previous round provided between rounds.
RESULTS: Fourteen experts were invited, with 10, 9, and 9 participants in rounds 1, 2, and 3, respectively. Before EBP, bed rest was recommended for recent-onset SIH with severe orthostatic headache (88.9%); other conservative methods such as abdominal binder and hydration were considered not mandatory (90%). Semitargeted EBP was recommended as initial management for patients with extradural CSF collections (70%). Dynamic CT myelography was preferred for localization (70%). Post-EBP care was variable, particularly in bed rest duration, with most recommendations (70%) exceeding 12 hours. Definitions of clinical remission (80%) and radiologic remission (90%) were established. Radiologic follow-up after clinical remission was recommended (78%). No consensus was reached on follow-up strategies for persistent symptoms, although "doing nothing" was not recommended. No consensus was reached for persistent extradural CSF despite clinical remission, requiring an individualized approach. Light activity after EBP was recommended within a few days (70%). No consensus was reached on the optimal number of EBPs before invasive leak localization or surgical intervention.
DISCUSSION: This Delphi study outlines expert recommendations and uncertainties for SIH management, including peri-EBP practices. This study incorporated the initial management strategy for patients in whom leak-type classification was incomplete. However, the treatment section primarily focused on the SLEC-positive setting and presumed ventral dural tears; lateral dural tears and CSF-venous fistulas warrant future consensus development.
42887144: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental condition whose timely identification can support earlier intervention. Conventional assessment relies on specialist observation and caregiver reports, motivating research into computer-aided screening using facial and behavioral data. This systematic review examines 171 studies published between 2016 and May 2026. It synthesizes machine learning and deep learning approaches to ASD assessment using static facial images, facial video, eye tracking, and multimodal data containing a facial signal. It also covers large language models, vision-language models, and multimodal large language models applied to ASD assessment, which were not addressed by the previous reviews included in the structured comparison, together with facial-data foundation-model studies in other clinical conditions that offer transferable methods. The review compares datasets, modeling strategies, and evaluation practices, and assesses methodological quality and risk of bias. Reported performance was often promising, but the strength of evidence varied with dataset provenance, diagnostic confirmation, participant independence, and validation design. Static-image studies relied heavily on reused public datasets and image-level partitions, whereas facial-video, eye-tracking, and multimodal studies more often used participant-level cohorts but still provided limited external and prospective validation. Differences in populations, acquisition protocols, prediction targets, and evaluation units prevent direct ranking of reported metrics across studies. Foundation models broaden the field toward behavioral description, diagnostic reasoning, and clinician-readable reporting, although their evidence remains preliminary. Facial-related data therefore show potential for computer-aided ASD screening, but clinical translation depends on clinically verified datasets, participant-independent evaluation, and testing in independent cohorts.
42888543:
BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence (AI) is being developed for image acquisition, quantitative tissue assessment, diagnosis, and clinical prediction in rotator cuff tears. The breadth of this literature and its methodological limitations have not been integrated across the complete care pathway.
METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library from inception to July 5, 2026 for English-language original studies applying AI to rotator cuff-related reconstruction, segmentation or quantitative imaging, diagnosis or classification, anatomical measurement, or prognosis. Two reviewers screened reports and extracted study, data, model, validation, reference standard, and performance characteristics. Diagnostic accuracy studies were assessed with QUADAS-2 and prediction-model studies with PROBAST. Because clinical tasks, modalities, models, reference standards, and reported metrics were not sufficiently comparable, evidence was synthesized narratively rather than pooled statistically.
RESULTS: Sixty-six reports were included: 35 diagnostic accuracy or classification studies, 20 segmentation or quantitative imaging studies, 9 prognosis or outcome prediction studies, 1 Magnetic Resonance Imaging reconstruction or image-optimization study, and 1 exploratory unsupervised-phenotyping study. Applications spanned Magnetic Resonance Imaging, radiography, ultrasound, computed tomography, clinical or multimodal data, motion video, and emerging sensing data. QUADAS-2 classified overall risk-of-bias as high in 27/36 diagnostic studies, unclear in 6/36, and low in 3/36. PROBAST classified all 8/8 completed prediction-model studies as high risk-of-bias; 1 protocol without model results was not rated. Promising internal performance was recurrent, but selection methods, imperfect or incompletely described reference standards, limited external validation, small or selected datasets, and analysis-stage weaknesses constrained clinical inference.
CONCLUSION: AI has proof-of-concept value across rotator cuff imaging and decision support, but the current evidence does not establish routine clinical readiness or replacement of clinician judgment. Prospective multicenter studies, transparent reference standards, independent external validation, calibration and clinical-utility assessment, and standardized task-specific reporting are required.
42892701:
PURPOSE: Diffusion MRI has shown promise for breast cancer screening, lesion characterization, and treatment response monitoring without contrast agents, but further translation is constrained by the gradient performance of conventional systems. The aim of this work is to develop a single-axis high-performance bilateral plug-and-play breast gradient insert to enable strong-gradient diffusion MRI.
METHODS: An in-house breast gradient insert and bed-tabletop was constructed entirely from commercially available materials, providing a cost-effective solution compatible with existing MRI systems. Its wiring pattern was optimized for torque and force balancing, power dissipation, and target field performance. Evaluation included gradient field characterization, peripheral nerve stimulation simulation verification, and temperature and eddy current assessment. The setup was used for imaging of a diffusion phantom based on soy lecithin across a range of b values.
RESULTS: Gradient efficiency ranged from 0.61 to 2.8 mT/m/A, enabling diffusion MRI using local strengths up to 420 mT/m (150 A). No peripheral nerve stimulation was observed during tests on five healthy volunteers. Eddy currents were successfully characterized, revealing a linear first order component with an amplitude of 0.03% of the applied gradient field. Imaging experiments demonstrated the feasibility of acquiring b = 10 000 s/mm2 volumes with a TE of 78 ms, compared with 161 ms when using the scanner gradients (40 mT/m).
CONCLUSION: This work demonstrates a dedicated bilateral breast gradient insert for safe and feasible strong-gradient breast diffusion MRI and represents a first step toward dedicated hardware for breast cancer detection and characterization without contrast agents.
42893682: The Advanced Breast Cancer (ABC) 8th international consensus conference took place on 6-8 November 2025, in Lisbon, and updated the previous ABC international consensus guidelines that are described in this manuscript. These guidelines reflect the work of a large and global consensus panel, comprising healthcare professionals and patients, and provide recommendations on how to best manage patients with advanced breast cancer (inoperable locally advanced or metastatic), of all breast cancer subtypes. The guidelines are based on the best available evidence or on expert opinion when a higher level of evidence is lacking and aim to cover the needs of the person living with ABC, including but also beyond the main therapeutic recommendations. Each guideline is accompanied by the level of evidence (LoE), the grade of recommendation (GoR), and the percentage of consensus reached at the consensus session. Updated diagnostic and treatment algorithms are also provided. These guidelines are endorsed by several international oncology organizations (AGO, AORTIC, ECO, EONS, ESO, ESTRO, EUSOMA, GECO Perú, SUMA, MASCC, French Breast Cancer Guidelines and AMAAC) and have official representation from ASCO, NCCN and ABC-NZ. Inequalities in access to high-quality care have increased in the last decade, both between and within countries, and are a major concern. The ABC guidelines provide guidance on the best available management options for patients living with ABC globally, assuming availability of the recommended therapies. Their adaptation is often needed in resource-constrained settings, and the grading of each recommendation may help in prioritizing access to available options.
42895635: Progressive unilateral calf enlargement is more commonly attributed to vascular, inflammatory, neoplastic, or lymphatic disease than to chronic denervation. We report a 55-year-old female recreational runner with progressive right calf enlargement and long-standing mild low back pain. Lumbar MRI demonstrated multilevel disc herniations, including a right-sided L5-S1 extrusion with compression of the right S1 nerve root. During the initial phase of calf symptoms, calf MRI showed mild asymmetric enlargement of the right posterior compartment with edema-like signal on fluid-sensitive sequences. At later-stage evaluation, 16 months after the initial calf MRI, ultrasound and follow-up calf MRI demonstrated significant interval progression to marked asymmetric enlargement of the right posterior compartment, predominantly involving the medial gastrocnemius and soleus; at a comparable anatomic level, the right soleus cross-sectional area had increased by approximately 58% relative to the prior calf MRI. Ultrasound showed mildly increased echogenicity with preserved fibrillar architecture, without increased color Doppler flow, focal mass, or architectural distortion. MRI confirmed preserved muscle architecture and absence of fatty replacement, consistent with true muscle hypertrophy rather than fatty pseudohypertrophy. Electromyography confirmed chronic right S1 radiculopathy. This case highlights that chronic S1 radiculopathy may present as progressive true calf hypertrophy without fatty replacement and that unilateral calf muscle enlargement with preserved architecture should prompt correlation with lumbar spine MRI and electrodiagnostic findings.
42895857:
INTRODUCTION: Total knee arthroplasty causes substantial postoperative pain. Combined adductor canal and interspace block between the popliteal artery and posterior knee capsule (iPACK) provides motor-sparing analgesia, but its duration is limited. We compared perineural and intravenous dexamethasone as adjuncts to these blocks in older patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty.
METHODS: In this prospective, randomised, quadruple-blind, parallel-group trial, 90 patients aged 65-100 years were allocated equally to receive adductor canal and iPACK blocks with ropivacaine plus perineural dexamethasone 4 mg in total (2 mg per block), intravenous dexamethasone 4 mg, or placebo. The primary outcome was time to first rescue opioid analgesia within 48 h. Secondary outcomes included opioid consumption, pain scores, inflammatory markers, blood glucose, quadriceps strength, and neurological safety.
RESULTS: Time to first rescue opioid analgesia differed between groups (log-rank p < 0.001). Median time (95% CI) was 4.5 (4.5-5.5) h with placebo, 13.9 (12.5-14.7) h with intravenous dexamethasone, and 18.5 (16.5 to not reached) h with perineural dexamethasone. The proportions remaining opioid-free at 48 h were 0%, 23.3%, and 36.7%, respectively. Opioid consumption and pain scores were lower with both dexamethasone routes than with placebo; perineural administration resulted in the lowest opioid consumption and lower pain scores than intravenous administration at later timepoints. Perineural dexamethasone was associated with lower postoperative neutrophil-to-lymphocyte and platelet-to-lymphocyte ratios, whereas intravenous dexamethasone was associated with higher blood glucose. No motor weakness or nerve injury occurred.
DISCUSSION: Perineural dexamethasone prolonged analgesia and reduced opioid requirements more than intravenous dexamethasone, without neurological or motor impairment. The inflammatory-marker findings were exploratory and do not establish independent clinical benefit.
42896192:
BACKGROUND: The Choosing Wisely initiative made recommendations where screening, testing, or treatment may be overused, with caveats around appropriate use. Clinicians are increasingly using large language models (LLMs).
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether commercial LLMs appropriately call for restraint or action from scenarios based on Choosing Wisely recommendations.
DESIGN: Benchmark evaluation. Fifteen Choosing Wisely recommendations were used to develop 225 scenarios (per recommendation, 10 in which restraint was appropriate and 5 in which action was appropriate). Six commercial LLMs (3 runs each) generated 4050 responses to the 225 scenarios, using a prompt from the clinician perspective.
SETTING: Production application programming interfaces of OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google from February to March 2026.
PARTICIPANTS: No human participants were involved.
MEASUREMENTS: Co-primary outcomes were the overuse rate (endorsing action when restraint was appropriate) and the false restraint rate (withholding an appropriate action).
RESULTS: The rate of LLM-recommended overuse was 5.4% (95% CI, 0.6% to 12.2%); LLMs did not recommend overuse in 8 of 15 recommendations. Two recommendations accounted for most LLM-recommended overuse: thyroid ultrasound for an incidental subcentimeter nodule (overuse recommended in 42.8% of LLM responses) and routine electrocardiography in low-risk adults (overuse recommended in 28.3% of LLM responses). The LLMs recommended overuse in 0.6% to 3.3% of responses for the remaining 5 recommendations. False restraint was rare (0.6% [CI, 0.1% to 1.2%]), was absent for 11 of 15 recommendations, and was highest for prostate-specific antigen screening (3.3%).
LIMITATIONS: Single prompts without follow-up; a benchmark rather than real-world use; responses classified by LLM judge with physician adjudication. Findings may not extend to consumer-facing use.
CONCLUSION: The LLMs rarely withheld recommendations for treatment when it was appropriate. Overuse was concentrated in 2 recommendations.
PRIMARY FUNDING SOURCE: None.
42897968:
BACKGROUND: Most thyroid malignancies harbor a limited set of well-characterized mutations driving tumor initiation and determining phenotype. This relatively direct genotype-phenotype association, bringing insights into molecular mechanisms of progression and drug resistance, makes advanced thyroid cancers suitable for genetic-based therapies. Personalized cancer treatment by targeting actionable tumor mutations represents one of the most innovative frontiers in oncology.
SUMMARY: The present narrative review focuses on actionable mutations occurring in thyroid cancers and provides a state-of-the-art overview of genetic-based treatments that have received regulatory approval worldwide. These include two selective RET inhibitors (sRET-Is) (selpercatinib and pralsetinib), three NTRK inhibitors (NTRK-Is) (larotrectinib, entrectinib, and repotrectinib), and two dual BRAF/MEK inhibitor regimens (dabrafenib plus trametinib and encorafenib plus binimetinib). The most significant impact has been observed in the management of RET-mutant medullary thyroid cancer. Selpercatinib, available in many countries, demonstrated superiority over standard multikinase inhibitors (MKIs) in a head-to-head comparison. It currently represents the best first-line treatment option. In BRAFV600E-positive anaplastic thyroid cancer, both dabrafenib plus trametinib and encorafenib plus binimetinib showed efficacy that appeared to exceed that historically observed with standard approaches. However, their approval is currently limited to a few countries. In radioiodine-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC), sRET-Is and NTRK-Is are effective in molecularly selected patients and are approved in many countries. However, their applicability is limited by the low prevalence of the corresponding actionable alterations. In BRAFV600E-positive radioiodine-refractory DTC, dabrafenib plus trametinib has emerged as a useful option after MKI failure, although a tumor-specific approval has been granted only in Europe.
CONCLUSIONS: Precision oncology is increasingly being integrated into the management of advanced thyroid cancer. However, its impact varies widely across different tumor settings, and its real-world use is strongly influenced by country-specific drug regulations.
42899250: Cancer has become one of the major diseases threatening the health of the Chinese population. The incidence of cancer in high-altitude regions of China is equally concerning. However, due to the unique geographical environment, population, and economic factors in high-altitude regions, there is an urgent need for a consensus on cancer prevention and management tailored to real-world clinical practice. To promote and standardize the diagnosis and treatment of cancer in high-altitude regions, under the leadership of the Breast Cancer Expert Committee of the National Cancer Quality Control Center and the Cancer Prevention and Treatment Committee of the Healthy China Research Center, experts in the field of high-altitude medicine were convened to jointly formulate the "Expert Consensus on the Standardized Diagnosis, Treatment, and Management of Cancer in High-Altitude Regions of China." This consensus serves as a reference for clinicians in high-altitude regions.
42899941: Encephalitis is a medical emergency characterized by inflammation of the brain parenchyma due to an infective cause or an immune-mediated process. Autoimmune encephalitis (AE) is characterized by a misdirected immune attack against neuronal structures, resulting in an inflammatory response. Triggers for the development of antibodies are often paraneoplastic or parainfectious. AE may occur in children or adults with symptoms including subacute onset of altered mentation, cognitive issues, drug-resistant epilepsy, movement disorders, and/or autonomic dysfunction. Limbic encephalitis is a common imaging feature of many forms of AE; however, cortical, basal ganglia, diencephalon, brainstem, and cerebellar involvement have been described. This article provides an overview of the general imaging appearances of AE, with a detailed discussion of key patterns encountered with common causes of AE, as well as a review of the relevant differential diagnoses, thus serving as a practical reference for radiologists.
42901239:
BACKGROUND: Early reocclusion after endovascular treatment (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke is underrecognized; its determinants and impact remain poorly defined.
METHODS: Random-effects meta-analysis of early reocclusion after successful EVT (PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library through January 2026). Crude odds ratios (ORs) were pooled and certainty rated with GRADE. Post hoc sensitivity analyses included only same-site reocclusion definitions.
RESULTS: Ten studies (3,381 patients) were included; 244 (7.2%) reoccluded. Reocclusion was associated with lower 90-day functional independence (OR 0.25, 95% CI 0.17-0.38) and higher mortality (OR 1.86, 1.29-2.68), both moderate certainty. Reocclusion was more frequent with large-artery atherosclerosis (OR 2.24, 1.41-3.55; same-site 3.04, 1.73-5.33) and less frequent with cardioembolism (OR 0.40, 0.28-0.57) and atrial fibrillation (OR 0.39, 0.26-0.59), mutually confounded associations reflecting one embolic-versus-atherothrombotic axis. Prestroke antiplatelet therapy (OR 0.43, 0.28-0.67) lost significance under the same-site definition (0.60, 0.31-1.16). Exploratory data (two cohorts) linked eTICI 2c-3 reperfusion with less reocclusion (OR 0.44, 0.28-0.69). No study reported when etiology was adjudicated; the atherosclerosis association may be partly outcome-induced.
CONCLUSIONS: Early reocclusion is uncommon but carries a substantial prognostic penalty. Its determinants appear to lie in the vascular substrate rather than thrombectomy technique; prospective studies with uniform same-site definitions and systematic follow-up imaging are needed.
42901389: Temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) is a network disorder extending beyond the structurally defined epileptogenic zone. Resting-state functional MRI (rsfMRI) may provide information on brain network alterations relevant to seizure outcome and cognitive risk after epilepsy surgery. We reviewed rsfMRI studies in TLE surgical cohorts to evaluate postoperative network changes, preoperative predictors of seizure outcome, and associations between functional connectivity and cognition. This systematic review followed PRISMA guidelines and was registered in PROSPERO. Fifteen studies were included, comprising 474 TLE patients who underwent resective epilepsy surgery and had at least 1 year of follow-up. Studies were reviewed for patient population, surgery, rsfMRI methodology, networks or regions, outcome definition, postoperative network changes, and cognitive assessments. Despite heterogeneity in patient selection, surgery, rsfMRI analysis, and outcome definition, studies consistently reported reduced DMN-related connectivity in TLE compared with healthy controls. Postoperative functional connectivity in seizure-free patients shifted toward healthy control patterns in few studies. Preoperative rsfMRI-based prediction models showed promising accuracy for predicting seizure outcome but were generally developed in small cohorts and lacked external validation. Evidence relating rsfMRI to cognition was limited, but implicated thalamic and ascending reticular activating system connectivity in visuospatial attention. RsfMRI is a promising research biomarker for network-level risk stratification in TLE surgery, particularly for seizure outcome prediction and postoperative network reorganization. Current evidence remains insufficient for clinical implementation. Future studies require larger homogeneous multicenter cohorts, standardized acquisition and preprocessing, consistent outcome definitions, systematic postoperative rsfMRI, neuropsychological assessment, and external validation of prediction models.
42901399:
BACKGROUND: Previous studies have reported gray matter volume (GMV) deficits in different illness stages of depression; however, whether patients at different stages show shared or distinct GMV abnormality patterns has not been systematically characterized.
METHODS: We conducted a quantitative voxel-wise meta-analysis of whole-brain voxel-based morphometry studies in individuals with subthreshold depression (STD), first-episode drug-naïve depression (FEND), and long-term major depressive disorder (MDD). Separate, pooled and comparative meta-analyses were performed using the seed-based d mapping (SDM) toolbox. Meta-regression analyses were conducted to explore age- and disease-related alterations in depression.
RESULTS: Twelve studies including 467 individuals with STD, 19 studies including 854 patients with FEND, and 14 studies including 525 patients with long-term depression were included. Compared with controls, STD and FEND exhibited mixed patterns of GMV increases and decreases predominantly involving key emotional and default mode network regions. In contrast, long-term MDD showed consolidated GMV reductions confined to the paracingulate gyrus and left middle temporal gyrus extending to insula. Direct comparisons across stages confirmed that GMV alterations in prefrontal and temporal regions showed progressive divergence from early to chronic depression. Meta-regression analyses revealed stage-specific associations between clinical characteristics and GMV changes.
CONCLUSIONS: This meta-analysis reveals stage-specific GMV abnormalities across depression. GMV changes shift from mixed alterations in early stages to purely atrophic reductions in chronic MDD, supporting a progressive model. Fronto-limbic deficits at the subthreshold stage may serve as early vulnerability markers, while GMV consolidation in long-term MDD underscores the importance of early intervention.
42901727:
BACKGROUND: The efficacy of middle meningeal artery embolization (MMAE) for chronic subdural hematoma (cSDH) has heightened interest in imaging biomarkers that may reflect neomembrane activity, predict recurrence, and identify patients most likely to benefit from treatment. Characterization of hematoma internal architecture, referred to as the imaging phenotype, may provide indirect information regarding the biological activity and maturation of the neomembrane. However, imaging phenotype has not been incorporated into randomized trials or validated treatment-selection algorithms, and standardized definitions and reporting remain lacking.
METHODS: The American Society of Functional Neuroradiology Clinical Practice Committee developed this State of Practice statement through expert consensus and review of the available literature.
KEY MESSAGE: Noncontrast CT (NCCT) remains the primary imaging modality for cSDH assessment. Hematoma burden should be characterized by maximum thickness measured perpendicular to the inner table, midline shift, and, when appropriate, volume. Volume may be estimated using the ABC/2 formula, whereas segmentation is more accurate for irregular, crescentic, or multiloculated collections when available. Internal architecture should be described using the Nakaguchi framework of homogeneous, laminar, separated, and trabecular phenotypes, with mixed or transitional features explicitly reported. Advanced techniques, including dual-energy CT, photon-counting CT, MRI, and arterial spin labeling, may provide information regarding membrane activity but are supported by limited, largely single-center evidence and currently have a problem-solving rather than routine role. Standardized reporting and prospective validation are needed before imaging phenotype or advanced-imaging biomarkers can guide treatment selection.
42905151:
PURPOSE: GE has recently developed Sonic DL MRI acceleration technology. We wished to (1) quantify scanner time reduction compared to the AIR Recon DL already in clinical use at our institution and (2) preliminarily evaluate any change in diagnostic findings between these methods.
METHODS: A total of 30 outpatients undergoing routine shoulder MRI for shoulder pain were recruited. Each underwent routine AIR Recon DL and Sonic DL exams containing the same sequences. Three subspecialized musculoskeletal radiologists assessed image quality, graded pathology, and reported diagnostic confidence in a blinded fashion. Differences in image quality and confidence were compared using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests.
RESULTS: Sonic DL reduced nominal acquisition time 38.7% compared to AIR Recon DL (6 min 15 s versus 10 min 12 s). Artifact was considered slightly worse on the routine examination (3.20 versus 3.37, P = 0.039); there was no significant difference in image quality, sharpness, or signal-to-noise ratio between routine and Sonic DL accelerated exams (P 0.171-0.861). Inter-reader agreement was broadly similar between routine-routine and routine-Sonic DL comparisons (median agreement 0.867 and 0.839, respectively). Within-reader analysis identified subacromial/subdeltoid bursitis and supraspinatus tendon tears more frequently on the routine protocol than on Sonic DL (P 0.049 and P 0.006, respectively).
CONCLUSION: Sonic DL enabled a 38.7% reduction in nominal shoulder MRI acquisition time with broadly comparable image quality and inter-reader agreement in this pilot cohort. Diagnostic equivalence was not established; subacromial/subdeltoid bursitis and supraspinatus tears were potentially less conspicuous on Sonic DL. A larger powered validation study would be needed to fully evaluate diagnostic performance.
42906371:
BACKGROUND: Adenomyosis has been shown to reduce live birth rates and increase the risk of pregnancy loss. The diagnosis is often established by ultrasonographic assessment using the revised Morphological Uterus Sonographic Assessment (MUSA) criteria. However, the reproductive impact of specific sonographic features remains unclear. A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted to investigate whether individual ultrasonographic adenomyosis features influence pregnancy outcomes in women with infertility or pregnancy loss.
METHODS: We searched MEDLINE (PubMed), Embase, Cochrane Library (CENTRAL), Web of Science, Scopus, and Google Scholar (most recent 200 records) from inception to May 11th, 2026. Observational and interventional studies reporting specific ultrasonographic features of adenomyosis in women with infertility and/or pregnancy loss were included. Primary outcomes were clinical pregnancy, live birth, and pregnancy loss. Two reviewers independently extracted data and assessed risk of bias using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal tools, as appropriate by study design. Meta-analyses were performed using random-effects models, with common-effects models applied where appropriate; remaining evidence was synthesised narratively. Certainty of evidence was assessed by GRADE. The protocol was registered on PROSPERO (CRD420251077005).
FINDINGS: Of 2322 records screened, 29 studies comprising 19,510 patients (7569 with adenomyosis) were included. Diffuse adenomyosis was associated with lower odds of live birth compared with no adenomyosis (OR 0.52, 95% CI 0.34-0.79; I2 = 63%), as well as internal adenomyosis compared with no adenomyosis (OR 0.49 95% CI 0.42-0.57 I2 = 0%). Narrative synthesis suggested poorer reproductive outcomes with adenomyosis features located near the endometrium and with larger uterine volume. The overall certainty was low or very low for 20 out of 21 outcomes, and moderate for one, primarily driven by imprecision and indirectness related to variation in diagnostic criteria across studies.
INTERPRETATION: Reproductive outcomes in adenomyosis vary according to specific ultrasonographic features, supporting feature-based reporting beyond a binary diagnosis. Substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity, including inconsistent ultrasonographic diagnostic criteria, variable application of MUSA definitions, and differences in fertility treatment protocols, warrants cautious interpretation of pooled estimates. Standardised definitions and reporting of adenomyosis features are needed to improve evidence synthesis and clinical translation.
FUNDING: The Novo Nordisk Foundation and the Danish Research Council.
42906641: The rapid expansion of minimally invasive, endoscopic, percutaneous, and implant-based spine interventions has outpaced standardized training requirements. This statement provides recommendations based on current training pathways, contemporary practice, and expert consensus, with patient safety as the guiding principle. These recommendations are not intended to define or restrict scope of practice; credentialing decisions remain the responsibility of institutions and governing bodies. Formal surgical spine training currently occurs through orthopaedic surgery residency with spine fellowship or neurological surgery residency with or without spine fellowship. These pathways include substantial supervised operative experience and ACGME residency case minimums. Anesthesiology, physical medicine and rehabilitation, radiology, and pain medicine pathways provide procedural training but do not include operative spine training, and nationally recognized training pathways for these specialties do not have minimum required case volumes across the spectrum of advanced spine interventions. Minimum case numbers, where established, are only one component of competency and should be considered alongside appropriate education, supervised experience, and demonstrated competency. Training and credentialing should reflect procedural complexity, anatomy at risk, biomechanical alteration, and potential complications. A surgical intervention treats structural spinal anatomy and meaningfully alters biomechanics or directly visualizes and decompresses the spinal cord and/or nerve roots. Based on current training pathways, spinal fusion or permanent stabilization, direct spinal cord and/or nerve root decompression, lateral sacroiliac fusion, vertebral augmentation with structural vertebral implants beyond cement or bone graft, and spinal cord stimulation paddle lead placement should be performed by physicians with formal surgical spine training. Other nonstructural interventions, including basivertebral nerve ablation, percutaneous neuromodulation, cement or bone-graft vertebral augmentation, and endoscopic branch neurectomy, should require structured procedure-specific education, supervised experience, appropriate minimum case numbers, and competency assessment. Educational courses should complement rather than replace structured clinical experience. This statement encourages prospective registries for emerging technologies to evaluate outcomes, complications, reinterventions, durability, subsequent surgical consequences, and inform training standards. Transparent informed consent and documented complication-management arrangements established before the procedure in every practice setting, including physician offices, are essential.
42908095:
OBJECTIVES: To identify preoperative factors associated with ablation zone resorption after microwave ablation (MWA) in patients with solitary T1aN0M0 papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC), and to explore their association with energy density.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study enrolled patients with solitary T1aN0M0 PTC who underwent MWA in our institution between September 2013 and January 2021. Ablation zone volume was measured at 1, 3, 6, 12, and 24 months post-ablation, and annually thereafter. Cox proportional hazards regression was performed to identify independent factors associated with ablation zone resorption. Kaplan-Meier analysis compared cumulative resorption rates among subgroups. Energy density was compared across subgroups.
RESULTS: A total of 296 patients were included, with an overall complete resorption rate of 73.6%. Multivariable Cox analysis identified baseline lesion volume (HR per IQR: 0.788, 95% CI: 0.678-0.917, p = 0.002) and microcalcification (HR: 0.669, 95% CI: 0.508-0.881, p = 0.004) as independent factors associated with delayed ablation zone resorption. Both factors were significantly correlated with energy density: the large-volume group (>52.1 mm³) received lower energy density than the small-volume group (≤52.1 mm³) (median 18.3 vs. 60.5 J/mm³, p < 0.001), and energy density was also lower in the microcalcification group than in those without (median 25.6 vs. 35.2 J/mm³, p = 0.030).
CONCLUSION: MWA is an effective and safe treatment for solitary T1aN0M0 PTC. Baseline lesion volume and microcalcification are independent factors associated with delayed ablation zone resorption, and their correlation with energy density provides a rationale for optimizing energy delivery strategies to facilitate resorption.
42908960:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative thyrotropin (TSH)-directed levothyroxine is used to reduce recurrence risk in selected patients with differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC), but treatment-related adverse effects may vary based on patient susceptibility and treatment exposure. Contemporary guidelines increasingly require balancing anticipated oncologic benefit against potential harm. This scoping review synthesizes patient-, treatment-, and disease-related factors associated with adverse effects of postoperative TSH-directed levothyroxine therapy in adults with DTC.
METHODS: This scoping review was reported following PRISMA-ScR guidelines and prospectively registered on the Open Science Framework. MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched from January 1, 2011, to February 24, 2026. Eligible studies reported associations between patient-, treatment-, or disease-related factors and adverse effects among adults with DTC receiving postoperative TSH-directed levothyroxine therapy. Data were summarized descriptively and synthesized narratively, with stratification according to TSH exposure definition.
RESULTS: Of 7361 records screened, 35 studies including 11,819 patients were included. Skeletal outcomes were most frequently reported (51.4%), followed by cardiometabolic (40.0%), neuropsychological (11.4%), reproductive (2.9%), and muscular outcomes (2.9%). TSH exposure definitions varied substantially: 18 studies evaluated subnormal TSH, 2 low-normal TSH, 8 mixed categories spanning subnormal and low-normal TSH, 4 continuous biochemical/treatment measures, and 3 unclear exposures. Greater suppression intensity was the most consistently reported treatment-related factor associated with adverse skeletal outcomes, particularly in studies evaluating subnormal TSH. Longer treatment duration was associated with skeletal harm in selected studies. Postmenopausal status emerged as a relatively consistent patient-level factor, whereas associations with age and body mass index were variable. Evidence for cardiometabolic, neuropsychological, reproductive, and muscular outcomes was less extensive and less consistent, and disease-related factors were infrequently examined. Only two studies conducted prediction/discrimination analyses, both involving skeletal outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: Evidence on adverse effects associated with TSH-directed levothyroxine therapy in DTC is most consistent for skeletal outcomes and predominantly derives from studies evaluating subnormal TSH exposure. The available literature provides limited evidence for clinically applicable prediction of toxicity or cumulative treatment burden. Future longitudinal studies should better characterize the intensity and persistence of biochemical exposure and develop outcome-specific prediction models integrating baseline susceptibility, organ vulnerability, and longitudinal treatment exposure to support individualized TSH management.
42910416: Intraoperative management of a patient undergoing cardiac surgery requires continuous and independent interventions by multiple healthcare professionals, including surgeons, anesthesiologists, and perfusionists, among others. Although each clinician performs tasks based on their training and accepted techniques, guidelines, and protocols, an action by one member of the team can have immediate consequences for other team members. Aortic surgery adds a level of complexity, with the need for interventions such as single-lung ventilation, systemic cooling (and subsequent rewarming), and myocardial, cerebral, and visceral protection. Much has been made of the utility of the multidisciplinary team. This scientific statement is intended to approach the patient undergoing aortic surgery from 3 different viewpoints: that of the surgeon, the anesthesiologist, and the perfusionist. This scientific statement is not intended to provide an exhaustive summary of approaches to aortic surgery but rather to illustrate the specific concerns that each member of the team may have.
42910430:
BACKGROUND: Endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) outperforms best medical treatment (BMT) for basilar artery occlusion (BAO), but the influence of stroke cause on the time sensitivity of EVT remains unclear. We hypothesized nonatherosclerotic BAO would require earlier EVT, whereas atherosclerotic BAO-with chronic stenosis and more robust collaterals-would retain EVT benefit in extended windows. We conducted a post hoc 3-way interaction analysis of the ATTENTION trial (Trial of Endovascular Treatment of Acute Basilar Artery Occlusion) to explore cause-specific EVT time patterns.
METHODS: Using randomized ATTENTION trial data (36 Chinese centers, 2021-2022), patients were stratified by onset-to-puncture time (<6 versus ≥6 hours) and TOAST (Trial of ORG 10172 in Acute Stroke Treatment) cause (atherosclerotic: large-artery atherosclerosis; nonatherosclerotic: cardioembolism/undetermined/other causes). The primary outcome was 90-day favorable functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale score 0-3), with relative risk as the primary estimand; the 3-way interaction was tested via joint Wald test. A weighted 1-hour interval odds ratio trend analysis served as an exploratory tool, with multivariable regression adjusting for confounders.
RESULTS: Among 340 patients (226 EVT+BMT, 114 BMT), for onset-to-puncture time <6 hours, patients with nonatherosclerotic BAO who received EVT achieved a significantly higher favorable outcome rate (46.7% versus 20.4%; relative risk, 2.29 [95% CI, 1.25-4.18]; P=0.007); the atherosclerotic group showed numerical outcome benefit (40.4% versus 26.1%, P=0.259). For onset-to-puncture time ≥6 hours, the numerical benefit in the atherosclerotic group increased from 14.3% to 30.6% (56.9% versus 26.3%; P=0.199), accompanied by ordinal modified Rankin Scale score improvement (common odds ratio, 3.30 [95% CI, 1.13-9.62]; P=0.029) and National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score reduction; the benefit in the nonatherosclerotic group decreased from 26.3% to 17.8% with loss of significance (39.5% versus 21.7%, P=0.341). The treatment time×cause interaction was not significant (P=0.662). The weighted 1-hour interval odds ratio trend analysis identified a provisional 5.3-hour reference point in nonatherosclerotic BAO.
CONCLUSIONS: Compared with nonatherosclerotic BAO, atherosclerotic BAO appears less time-sensitive, potentially retaining EVT responsiveness over longer windows. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation.
REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT04751708.
42911849: Spontaneous intracranial hypotension is a frequently debilitating condition that is most commonly caused by loss of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) from the spine. The most frequently occurring types of spontaneous spinal CSF leaks that cause spontaneous intracranial hypotension are ventral dural tears, lateral dural tears, and CSF venous fistulas, but other leak types are recognized including sacral dural tears or fistulas into vascular malformations. Localization and characterization of spinal CSF leaks with CT myelography facilitates subsequent targeted treatment. A tailored approach based on the suspected leak type as determined at MRI of the spine is necessary to maximize the likelihood of a diagnostic study. The authors focus primarily on advanced CT myelographic techniques for leaks from dural tears and CSF venous fistulas. The importance of optimal patient positioning, typical and atypical appearances of the different leak types, and artifacts that can mimic a CSF leak are considered. ©RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article. See the invited commentary by Madhavan in this issue.
42912575:
BACKGROUND: Hyperkinetic biliary dyskinesia, defined as a gallbladder ejection fraction (EF) ≥80% on cholecystokinin (CCK)-stimulated hepatobiliary iminodiacetic acid scans in the setting of biliary-type pain, has been increasingly recognized as a potential functional gallbladder disorder. The clinical significance of this entity and the role of cholecystectomy remain uncertain.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies reporting outcomes in patients with CCK-hepatobiliary iminodiacetic acid EF ≥80% who underwent cholecystectomy due to non-acute biliary-type pain. Primary outcomes included mean EF, rates of symptom resolution and improvement following cholecystectomy, and prevalence of chronic cholecystitis on pathology. Secondary outcomes included normal histology rates and symptom reproduction with CCK stimulation. All statistical analyses were conducted in R (version 4.5.0) using a random-effects model to obtain pooled estimates.
RESULTS: A total of 14 retrospective studies, including 686 patients, were analyzed. The pooled mean gallbladder EF was 90.27% (95% CI: 88.73-91.80, I 2 = 86.6%). Symptom resolution occurred in 83.1% (95% CI: 76.7-89.4, I 2 = 76.8%), and symptom improvement in 91.6% (95% CI: 89.0-94.2, I 2 = 29.7%) of patients following cholecystectomy. Histopathologic analysis revealed chronic cholecystitis in 85.1% (95% CI: 76.9-93.4, I 2 = 90.6%) of surgical specimens, while normal gallbladder histology was rare, observed in only 9.9% (95% CI: 4.6-15.2, I 2 = 83.7%). The pooled risk ratio indicated a 6.70-fold higher likelihood of chronic cholecystitis compared with normal histology (95% CI: 3.69-12.17, I 2 = 65.2%, P = 0.0022). Functional reproduction of symptoms during CCK stimulation was frequent, with a pooled rate of 78.3% (95% CI: 70.4-86.3, I 2 = 35.6%). Egger regression test suggested potential publication bias for the normal histology outcome ( P = 0.0223), but not for symptom resolution ( P = 0.1589).
CONCLUSIONS: This meta-analysis suggests that a high gallbladder EF in the setting of biliary-type pain could represent clinically relevant hyperkinetic biliary dyskinesia rather than normal physiology. Cholecystectomy appears to provide meaningful symptom relief in appropriately selected patients, and pathologic findings frequently indicate underlying chronic inflammation. Further studies are needed to establish clear diagnostic cutoffs and guide management.
42912579:
PURPOSE: This study was designed to investigate the detection rate and tumor uptake of 18 F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI PET/CT in newly diagnosed high-risk prostate cancer (PCa), compared with 68 Ga-PSMA-11 and 18 F-FDG PET/CT.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This study enrolled 48 patients with biopsy-diagnosed, treatment-naive high-risk PCa who underwent 18 F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI, 68 Ga-PSMA-11, and 18 F-FDG PET/CT between April and December 2024. A head-to-head comparison of detection rate and tumor uptake was performed among the 3 tracers. In addition, 18 F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI and 68 Ga-PSMA-11 dual-tracer PET was used to characterize the imaging phenotypes of each lesion and interlesional heterogeneity.
RESULTS: A total of 477 lesions were detected by the 3 PET tracers. 68 Ga-PSMA-11 exhibited the highest overall detection rate (96.4%), followed by 18 F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI (81.1%) and 18 F-FDG (66.0%). A total of 17 68 Ga-PSMA-11-negative lesions were identified in 8 patients, all of which were detected by 18 F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI, whereas only 12 were detected by 18 F-FDG. Combined 68 Ga-PSMA-11 and 18 F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI PET identified all lesions detected by triple-tracer PET. Based on relative tracer dominance of dual-tracer PET, patients were classified as PSMA-dominant (n=23), FAPI-dominant (n=5), or mixed phenotype (n=20). The mixed phenotype with marked interlesional heterogeneity might be associated with more advanced clinical characteristics, with a higher proportion of metastatic disease and a greater metastatic burden.
CONCLUSIONS: 18 F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI is a promising PET tracer for newly diagnosed high-risk PCa. It may improve the detection rate of 68 Ga-PSMA-11-negative lesions and provide complementary information that could reflect interlesional heterogeneity. The clinical value of combining 18 F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI and 68 Ga-PSMA-11 PET requires further validation in larger prospective cohorts.
42912580: Neuroblastoma (NB) is the most common extracranial solid malignancy of childhood, arising from neural crest cells of the sympathetic nervous system. Metastatic spread most frequently involves the bone marrow, bones, lymph nodes, and liver, whereas soft-tissue, central nervous system, and pulmonary metastases are less common. Unusual sites of recurrence may present a significant diagnostic challenge. We report a rare case of thymic relapse of NB presenting as an anterior mediastinal mass with intense uptake on 123 I-meta-iodobenzylguanidine ( 123 I-mIBG) scintigraphy. This case highlights an uncommon pattern of NB recurrence and the value of 123 I-mIBG imaging in its detection.
42912642: A 5-year-old boy underwent 18 F-FDG PET/CT before the histopathologic diagnosis of neuroblastoma, revealing a metabolically active left adrenal primary tumor with metastases to the liver. Following resection and chemotherapy, sequential 68 Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT and 18 F-MFBG demonstrated tracer-specific uptake patterns: 18 F-MFBG identified a solitary hepatic metastasis undetected by 68 Ga-DOTATATE. This case underscores the complementary diagnostic value of multimodal molecular imaging in pediatric neuroblastoma response assessment.
42912643: A 13-year-old boy underwent FDG PET/CT to evaluate fever of unknown origin, which demonstrated extensive abnormal activity around joints of all 4 extremities and probable myopericarditis. Subsequent rheumatologic evaluation, including cardiac auscultation and echocardiography, identification of subcutaneous nodules, and elevated antistreptolysin O titers, established the diagnosis of acute rheumatic fever (ARF). Symmetrical polyarthritis with enthesitis-myotendinitis is an uncommon manifestation of ARF.
42912647: Solitary ectopic insulinomas without concurrent pancreatic or gastrointestinal lesions are exceedingly rare. We report the 18 F-NOTA-exendin-4 PET/CT findings of a solitary ectopic insulinoma in a 68-year-old woman with a 10-year history of recurrent hypoglycemic syncope. Endogenous hyperinsulinemia was confirmed, but conventional imaging and laparoscopic pancreatic exploration were negative. PET/CT revealed a solitary intense focus in the para-abdominal aortic region. Surgical resection confirmed a solitary ectopic insulinoma, and postoperative hypoglycemia resolved. This case highlights the value of 18 F-NOTA-exendin-4 PET/CT in identifying occult solitary ectopic insulinomas when conventional imaging and surgical exploration are unrevealing, enabling curative resection.
42912648: Bladder diverticula are predisposed to developing intradiverticular bladder tumors. We describe FDG PET/CT findings in a case of intradiverticular bladder cancer. At FDG PET/CT (62 min), the intradiverticular bladder cancer appeared as an exophytic lesion with similar density to the urine in the bladder‌ and intense activity mimicking a bladder diverticulum. At delayed pelvic FDG PET/CT (275 min), the tumor showed higher density and activity than the urine in the bladder, consistent with malignancy. This case indicates that delayed pelvic FDG PET/CT may be necessary for detecting possible intradiverticular bladder cancer in patient with bladder diverticulum.
42912649: A 71-year-old woman with a 5-week history of right-sided abdominal pain was initially suspected of hepatobiliary disorders. Upper abdominal ultrasound and MRI revealed unremarkable hepatobiliary findings. Although no hepatobiliary lesions were identified, MRI incidentally detected an ascending colon mass highly suspicious for malignancy. The patient underwent FDG PET/CT for differential diagnosis and preoperative staging. PET/CT with 3D CT reconstruction demonstrated a linear hyperdense foreign body within the ascending colon wall, causing focal bowel wall thickening with intense FDG avidity. These imaging findings were consistent with a foreign body-induced inflammatory granuloma, a diagnosis ultimately confirmed by colonoscopy and biopsy.
42912667: Urethral involvement in IgG4-related disease is rare. We describe FDG PET/CT and delayed pelvic PET/MRI findings in a woman with IgG4-related disease presenting as urethral wall thickening with obstructive urinary symptoms. FDG PET/CT and delayed pelvic PET/MRI showed significant circumferential thickening of the urethral wall with intense diffuse activity (SUV max , 13) and multiple hypermetabolic lymph nodes in pelvic, retroperitoneal, mediastinal, pulmonary hilar, and axillary regions. This case indicates that IgG4-related urethral disease should be included in the differential diagnosis of FDG-avid urethral or periurethral lesions.
42913278: Low-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (LGSOC) is a rare epithelial malignancy characterized by frequent mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathway alterations, hormone receptor expression, relative resistance to cytotoxic chemotherapy, and a prolonged, relapsing clinical course. Since publication of the 2023 international expert consensus, significant advances have reshaped the management of both newly diagnosed and recurrent disease. The 2026 LGSOC Consensus Conference convened an international multidisciplinary panel of experts in the field to review emerging evidence and update recommendations across pathology, molecular testing, translational biology, frontline and recurrent treatment, imaging, treatment-associated toxicity, regulatory strategy, patient advocacy, and future research priorities. Recommendations were informed by contemporary clinical evidence, multidisciplinary discussion, and patient perspectives. The updated consensus incorporates practice-changing data from NRG-GY019 supporting chemotherapy-containing postoperative therapy as the current reference approach for stage II-IV disease while recognizing selected circumstances in which endocrine monotherapy may represent individualized de-escalation. It also integrates recent advances in recurrent disease, including the US Food and Drug Administration's accelerated approval of avutometinib in combination with defactinib for KRAS-mutated LGSOC, emerging evidence supporting endocrine therapy combined with CDK4/6 inhibition, and refined guidance for biomarker-directed treatment selection, imaging assessment, toxicity management, and patient-centered survivorship. The panel emphasizes treatment-specific biomarker interpretation, multidisciplinary care, central pathology review for clinical trials, and the continued need for prospective studies addressing treatment sequencing, predictive biomarkers, and quality-of-life outcomes. This updated international consensus provides an evidence-based framework for the diagnosis and management of LGSOC while identifying priorities for future clinical research and drug development.
42914619:
BACKGROUND: Embryo selection is one of the most critical determinants of success in in vitro fertilization (IVF). Conventional approaches based on static morphological grading and time-lapse imaging (TLI) remain subjective and show only modest predictive accuracy. Artificial intelligence (AI) tools, including deep learning-based platforms such as iDAScore and KIDScore, have emerged as potentially more standardized alternatives, yet their true clinical impact on per-transfer outcomes remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVES: To determine whether AI-assisted embryo selection offers measurable clinical advantages over conventional morphology-based methods in IVF.
SEARCH STRATEGY: A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted by searching four electronic databases (PubMed, Scopus, Embase, and the Cochrane Library) from January 2013 to April 2024.
SELECTION CRITERIA: Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and observational cohort studies evaluating AI-assisted embryo selection versus conventional morphology in IVF cycles without preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (PGT-A), reporting at least one of clinical pregnancy rate (CPR), implantation rate (IR), or live birth rate (LBR).
DATA COLLECTION AND ANALYSIS: Two reviewers independently screened records and extracted data. Study quality was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool for the RCT and the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale for observational studies. Where arm-level data were available, risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were pooled using a random-effects model.
RESULTS: Ten studies were included. Only two reported arm-level outcomes suitable for meta-analysis. The pooled estimate showed no significant difference in clinical pregnancy rate between AI-assisted and morphology-based selection (RR = 0.99, 95% CI 0.87-1.12; I2 = 26.5%), with no statistically significant difference between the two methods. The remaining eight studies reported predictive performance metrics with area under the receiver operating characteristic curve values of 0.85-0.96, though these did not consistently translate into improved per-cycle outcomes. Implantation and live birth rates were inconsistently reported and could not be pooled.
CONCLUSION: AI-based embryo scoring showed no statistically significant difference compared with conventional morphology for per-transfer clinical pregnancy rate, with potential advantages in standardization and inter-observer consistency. However, superiority remains unconfirmed and key patient-centered outcomes including cumulative live birth rate, miscarriage rate, and time-to-pregnancy were not reported in available studies. Larger multicenter RCTs with standardized outcome reporting are required.
42914680: Bereavement is among life's most stressful events, and a minority of mourners develop prolonged and disabling grief. Biological markers have been proposed as signals of this risk, but no systematic review has examined them across bereaved family members or asked how well bereaved parents (parents who have lost a child) are represented. We systematically reviewed observational studies linking a cortisol/HPA-axis, inflammatory/immune, or cardiovascular/autonomic biomarker to a validated measure of coping or grief in bereaved family members of any age or relationship to the deceased (PROSPERO CRD420261446539). Five databases were searched, with citation searching of a related review. Eighteen studies met inclusion criteria across the three domains. More severe grief was linked to blunted or flatter diurnal cortisol in three of five cortisol studies. Bereavement and greater grief were linked to raised inflammatory markers (IL-6, IL-1RA, and related cytokines), although five of seven inflammatory studies appear to come from one research programme, and one study found divergent Type I interferon gene transcription in complicated relative to uncomplicated grief. Cardiovascular and autonomic findings were mixed and depended on moderators such as coping style and childhood adversity. Some cortisol associations weakened with time since loss, so they may not be stable markers of grief severity. Only one participant across all 18 studies was an identifiable bereaved parent. Biological markers show domain-specific associations with grief, but the evidence is exploratory, and bereaved parents are largely absent from it. They should be a priority for future prospective work.
42918308: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) encompasses diverse behavioral, cognitive, and neural profiles that vary widely across individuals. Because diagnosis remains predominantly behavior-based, clinically meaningful within-spectrum differences are often missed. Recent advances in neuroimaging analysis have created opportunities for the identification of distinct neural profiles within ASD. These new avenues provide ways to examine intra-ASD heterogeneity directly, identifying person-specific brain-behavior patterns that group-level comparisons fail to capture. The present systematic review focused on neuroimaging methods (i.e., resting-state fMRI; rs-fMRI, cortical morphology) that emphasized heterogeneity-informed outcomes based on normative modeling, data-driven subtyping, clustering analysis and similar analytic choices. For rs-fMRI, findings showed that differences in connectivity within the default mode and salience networks were linked to social-communication and language impairments, with subtype-specific patterns emerging across samples. In cortical thickness and surface area, studies identified distinct developmental trajectories and individual deviation profiles, with prefrontal and temporal regions often tied to repetitive behaviors and social-communication difficulties. Voxel-based analyses revealed subgroup-specific gray matter alterations, including cerebellar and cortical differences, that aligned with variation in repetitive behaviors and social difficulties. Collectively, this emerging evidence supports the notion that neural heterogeneity in autism is a core feature rather than a limitation. Embracing individual variability can provide crucial insight into the inconsistencies and contradictions of earlier case-control and group-level findings. Moving forward, autism research must prioritize heterogeneity-based methods to establish reproducible subtypes and individualized brain-behavior links.
42919739:
CONTEXT: There are substantial regional differences in prostate cancer (PCa) epidemiology reflecting differences in risk factors, screening, management, and access to care.
OBJECTIVE: To assess geographical differences and temporal trends in PCa incidence and mortality and PCa risk factors.
EVIDENCE ACQUISITION: Estimated incidence and mortality data for the year 2024 and projections to 2050 based on the assumption that 2024 age-specific incidence and mortality rates remain unchanged (not accounting for changes in risk factors and/or treatments) in 185 countries were derived from the International Agency for Research on Cancer's GLOBOCAN 2024 database. A narrative review of the literature summarized risk factors and preventive measures.
EVIDENCE SYNTHESIS: Worldwide, 1.55 million new PCa cases were estimated in 2024, with an age-standardized rate (ASR) for incidence of 29 per 100 000. Northern America had the highest all-age incidence ASR (81), and South-Central Asia the lowest (7.2). PCa caused an estimated 420 000 deaths (7.5 per 100 000), with the highest mortality ASRs in the Caribbean (29) and the lowest in South-Central Asia (3.4). By 2050, new cases are projected to be 2.88 million (+86%) and deaths 924 000 (+120%), with the largest relative increases in Africa (+156%). Prostate-specific antigen-based screening influences both incidence and geographic variation. Family history, germ line pathogenic variants, polygenic risk scores, and ancestry are risk factors. Disparities in men of African versus European ancestry reflect both tumor biology and unequal access to care, with mortality gaps narrowing in equal-access health systems. No single nutrient or supplement has been shown to reduce PCa incidence. Cigarette smoking and obesity are associated with PCa-specific mortality, whereas physical activity and plant-based or Mediterranean dietary patterns are associated with a lower risk of disease progression.
CONCLUSIONS: The global burden of PCa because of population increase and aging is projected to rise substantially by 2050, particularly in low- and middle-income regions. Family history, germ line pathogenic variants, and ancestry are risk factors for PCa. Evidence remains insufficient to support any specific preventive intervention, although smoking, diet, and physical activity may modify risk of progression or mortality.
42920104:
BACKGROUND: Low-field magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has regained interest for musculoskeletal imaging due to advances in magnet design, hardware optimization, and artificial intelligence (AI)-based reconstruction, offering improved accessibility, patient comfort, and sustainability.
PURPOSE: This systematic review aimed to explore and summarize the current status of low-field MRI for knee investigations.
STUDY TYPE: Systematic review on MEDLINE, Cinhal, EMBASE, Web of Science, Scopus, and Google Scholar databases. PROSPERO protocol (CRD42024544354).
POPULATION: Approximately 3400 participants (8-89 years) encompassing healthy volunteers, community-based cohorts, and patients with diverse knee pathologies were evaluated. Few studies incorporate phantom experiments.
FIELD STRENGTH/SEQUENCE: This review covered a range of very-low-field (< 0.1 T), conventional low-field (0.1-< 0.29 T), and upper-range low-field (> 0.3 T-0.55 T) with standard, extremity, open, and weight-bearing/standing systems. SE/FSE and GRE sequences, 3D GRE quantitative protocols, and AI-based were used.
ASSESSMENT: Two reviewers independently extracted data on knee protocols, technical parameters, diagnostic performance, and reported advantages and limitations.
STATISTICAL TESTS: Study quality was assessed using appropriate JBI critical appraisal tools. A narrative synthesis and descriptive analysis of the findings from the included studies are provided due to the heterogeneity of the intervention and outcome.
RESULTS: From 3726 records, 31 were included. Low-field MRI demonstrated high diagnostic performance for meniscal and ligamentous injuries but lower sensitivity for early cartilage degeneration. Weight-bearing MRI provided distinct functional information but not direct equivalence to standard MRI. AI-enhanced reconstruction was evaluated in a limited number of single-center, vendor-specific studies and was associated with improved image quality and diagnostic confidence. Important limitations included lower signal-to-noise ratio, reduced spatial resolution, protocol heterogeneity, and limited pathology-validated evidence.
DATA CONCLUSION: Low-field MRI may provide a clinically useful complementary option for selected knee meniscal and ligamentous indications. However, heterogeneous evidence, influenced by field strength, scanner design, sequences, and reference standards, limits claims of equivalence with high-field MRI, particularly for subtle cartilage lesions. Advances in hardware and AI have improved image quality and efficiency; however, evidence is limited and larger standardized multicenter studies are required.
EVIDENCE LEVEL: 5.
TECHNICAL EFFICACY: Stage 5.
42921690:
BACKGROUND: DIO3 encodes type 3 iodothyronine deiodinase, the major thyroid hormone-inactivating enzyme, and is an imprinted gene with preferential paternal-allele expression demonstrated in human neonatal skin. Dio3-deficient mice develop neonatal thyrotoxicosis followed by central hypothyroidism, but human evidence has been lacking.
PATIENT FINDINGS: On newborn screening, thyrotropin (TSH) and free thyroxine (fT4) did not meet repeat-testing criteria, while T-cell lymphopenia was detected neonatally. From 5 months onward, fT4 progressively declined without compensatory TSH elevation. Chromosomal microarray identified a derivative chromosome 14 with a 14q32.31-q32.33 deletion encompassing DIO3 and TRAF3. The deletion originated from a paternal balanced 4p/14q translocation.
SUMMARY: In this patient, delayed-onset central hypothyroidism was most consistent with paternal DIO3 loss, whereas the accompanying T-cell lymphopenia was consistent with TRAF3 haploinsufficiency.
CONCLUSIONS: This case provides the first human evidence linking paternal DIO3 loss to delayed-onset central hypothyroidism, supporting a novel developmental mechanism that may alter hypothalamic-pituitary-thyroid axis programming.
42922094:
BACKGROUND: Endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) is a standard treatment for acute ischemic stroke (AIS) caused by large vessel occlusion (LVO). However, the efficacy and safety of bridging thrombolysis (BT) compared to direct EVT (dEVT) remain controversial, particularly in patients with large core infarcts (Alberta stroke program early CT score [ASPECTS] ≤5). This meta-analysis aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of BT versus dEVT in this population.
METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science from January 1, 2010, to September 21, 2024, for studies comparing BT and dEVT in AIS patients with ASPECTS ≤5. Outcomes included functional outcomes (mRS 0-2 and 0-3), intracranial hemorrhage (ICH), symptomatic ICH (sICH), 90-day mortality, and successful reperfusion. Data were pooled using random-effects models.
RESULTS: Twelve studies (3907 patients) were included. BT significantly improved favorable (OR: 1.43, 95% CI: 1.17-1.76) and moderate functional outcomes (OR: 1.28, 95% CI: 1.10-1.48) compared to dEVT. No significant differences were observed in sICH, ICH, 90-day mortality, or successful reperfusion.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that BT may be associated with better functional outcomes in patients with ASPECTS ≤5, without increasing major safety events compared with dEVT. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously because the evidence is mainly observational, and residual confounding cannot be excluded. Further well-designed randomized controlled trials are needed to confirm these findings.
42922241:
BACKGROUND: Breast cancer is the most frequently diagnosed malignancy in women globally, accounting for approximately 2.30 million new cases and 666,103 deaths in 2022. Artificial intelligence technologies including machine learning, deep learning, radiomics, and natural language processing have been widely applied across the breast cancer care continuum. However, no systematic review restricted to primary studies with patient-level or image-level data has synthesized evidence spanning all clinical domains simultaneously.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the performance, methodological quality, and clinical relevance of artificial intelligence primary studies across screening and diagnostic imaging, digital pathology, radiomics, perioperative management, prognostic prediction, and natural language processing in breast cancer.
METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from January 2015 to May 2026. Eligibility was restricted to original primary research reporting patient-level or image-level data; secondary syntheses were explicitly excluded. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2 and PROBAST. Reporting followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines.
RESULTS: Of 5,275 identified records, 17 primary studies met eligibility criteria. In screening mammography (seven studies; n = 7,540 to 144,231 examinations), deep learning achieved area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values of 0.876 to 0.939; a randomised trial in 80,033 women demonstrated non-inferiority to double reading with a 44.3% reduction in radiologist workload. In digital pathology (five studies; 270 to 44,732 whole-slide images), deep learning achieved AUC 0.985 to 0.994, exceeding unassisted pathologist performance in lymph node metastasis detection.
