CONCLUSION: EU-TIRADS was more sensitive and ACR TI-RADS more specific in these two studies, but the limited evidence and absence of paired discordant classifications preclude claims of superiority.
43022467:
OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate risk factors associated with non-sentinel lymph node (NSLN) metastasis in patients with sentinel lymph node (SLN)-positive breast cancer.
METHODS: A comprehensive literature search was performed in PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library from database inception to November 12, 2025. Studies reporting multivariable analyses of risk factors for NSLN metastasis were included. Study quality was independently assessed by two reviewers using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS). Pooled odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using a random-effects model. Heterogeneity, sensitivity analyses, and publication bias were also evaluated. All statistical analyses were conducted using Stata version 15.0.
RESULTS: A total of 37 studies involving 13,304 patients were included. The meta-analysis demonstrated that SLN macrometastasis (OR = 6.07, 95% CI: 2.21-16.7), abnormal preoperative AUS findings (OR = 3.51, 95% CI: 2.25-5.47), extranodal extension of SLN (OR = 2.67, 95% CI: 2.07 -3.44), lymphovascular invasion (OR = 2.68, 95% CI: 2.18-3.29), perineural invasion (OR = 2.37, 95% CI: 1.18-4.76), tumor diameter > 2 cm (OR = 2.06, 95% CI: 1.52-2.78), clinical T stage ≥ T2 (OR = 2.44, 95% CI: 2.02-2.95), histologic grade ≥ 3 (OR = 1.76, 95% CI: 1.44-2.16), number of positive SLNs (OR = 2.32, 95% CI: 1.53-3.53), SLN positivity ratio ≥ 50% (OR = 2.17, 95% CI: 1.74-2.70), multifocality (OR = 2.68, 95% CI: 1.98-3.63), HER2 positivity (OR = 2.22, 95% CI: 1.63-3.01), and a high Ki-67 index (OR = 2.20, 95% CI: 1.13-4.25) were associated with an increased risk of NSLN metastasis.
CONCLUSION: SLN tumor burden, abnormal preoperative axillary ultrasound findings, tumor aggressiveness, and intrinsic biological characteristics (e.g., HER2 status and Ki-67 index) are key predictors of NSLN metastasis. Given the limitations in the quality and quantity of the included studies, further high-quality, large-scale prospective studies are warranted to validate these findings and provide more robust evidence for individualized axillary management in breast cancer.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420261301905.
43023699:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: The liver removes about half of secreted insulin on first pass. Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt creation diverts portal blood past the liver; endovascular shunt obliteration restores it. We systematically reviewed glycaemic and insulin outcomes after both.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase and Web of Science were searched through September 2026 for paired glucose or insulin measurements before and after either intervention. Ratios of post-intervention to pre-intervention means were pooled by random effects with Hartung-Knapp adjustment, excluding cohorts at critical risk of bias.
RESULTS: Fifteen cohorts (17 records) were included. After shunt creation, fasting insulin rose 49% (95% confidence interval 24% to 80%; 6 cohorts) and the homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance rose 55% (5% to 129%; 4 cohorts), whereas fasting glucose (2.5%; -0.3% to 5.4%; 5 cohorts), glycated haemoglobin, and fructosamine were unchanged. Glucose tolerance worsened in one of two cohorts tested (area under the curve +14%). Insulin rose more than C-peptide or proinsulin in four cohorts; clamp-measured insulin sensitivity was unchanged. After obliteration, fasting insulin fell 15% (one cohort) and insulin area under the curve 17% and 19% (two cohorts). Antihyperglycaemic requirements changed in both directions after shunt creation and fell after obliteration.
CONCLUSIONS: Shunt creation raises insulin by nearly half without changing fasting glucose or glycation markers, and obliteration reverses the pattern. Secretion markers change less than insulin, indicating altered first-pass hepatic insulin extraction rather than secretion. Insulin-based resistance indices may mislead after shunting, and the consequences of chronic shunt-induced hyperinsulinemia need prospective study.
43023927: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is the most prevalent chronic liver condition and is linked to unhealthy lifestyle patterns. Dietary modification remains the cornerstone of management. Among available nutritional strategies, ketogenic diets (KDs) have gained increasing attention. This systematic review evaluated the impact of KD, versus no dietary intervention or control diets, on hepatic and metabolic outcomes in adults with MASLD. Following PRISMA guidelines, PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science were searched through June 2026. Two reviewers independently screened records, assessed eligibility and extracted data. Risk of bias was evaluated using CASP for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and ROBINS-I for non-randomized studies. Meta-analysis was not feasible due to study heterogeneity. Fourteen studies were included: five RCTs and nine prospective cohorts, involving 776 adults with MASLD and/or hepatic steatosis. KD was associated with improvements in MASLD severity indices, anthropometric measures, lipid profile, glycaemic markers and liver enzymes. Among RCTs, liver fat decreased by -4.77% (PDFF) to a 77% (relative MRI-LFF), with reductions in body weight (up to -12.0 kg) and waist circumference (up to -9.6 cm). Prospective studies showed similar findings, including reductions in controlled attenuation parameter (up to -57 dB/m), intrahepatic triglyceride (-31%) and Fatty Liver Index (-14.03 points). Evidence regarding liver stiffness and fibrosis-related outcomes was more limited and less consistent. KD may improve disease severity, hepatic steatosis, anthropometric measures, glycaemic control, lipid metabolism and liver-related biochemical markers in adults with MASLD. However, methodological heterogeneity precludes outcomes assessment, and limited evidence on fibrosis-related evidence precludes firm conclusions. Larger, longer-standardized RCTs are needed to clarify KD's role in MASLD management.
43024054: Cystic pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (c-PanNETs) are an uncommon cystic phenotype of well-differentiated pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors, accounting for approximately 7-12% of PanNETs in several surgical series, although reported frequencies vary according to the definition of cystic morphology and cohort selection. Retrospective studies suggest that c-PanNETs may exhibit less aggressive clinicopathologic features than their solid counterparts; however, their imaging appearance frequently overlaps with other pancreatic cystic neoplasms, particularly branch-duct intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms, mucinous cystic neoplasms, and atypical serous cystic neoplasms. Accurate preoperative recognition may have important implications for patient management and surgical planning. This review summarizes the imaging features of c-PanNETs across computed tomography, magnetic resonance imaging, and magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography, as well as the complementary roles of endoscopic ultrasound and somatostatin receptor PET/CT. Particular attention is given to arterial hyperenhancement of the cyst wall, septations, mural nodules, or residual solid components; assessment of communication with the main pancreatic duct; and integration of complementary imaging findings. Because these features are not specific, their interpretation in combination with lesion morphology and ductal relationships is emphasized. Practical approaches to differential diagnosis and common interpretive pitfalls are also discussed. The review further addresses emerging quantitative imaging techniques, including radiomics and artificial intelligence, while recognizing that evidence specific to c-PanNETs remains limited. A practical diagnostic algorithm and structured reporting checklist are provided to support systematic interpretation and multidisciplinary communication. Recognition of the imaging spectrum of c-PanNETs, combined with systematic assessment of enhancement characteristics, ductal anatomy, and complementary imaging findings, may improve diagnostic confidence and support appropriate patient management.
43024296:
BACKGROUND: Active surveillance is the preferred management strategy for men with low-risk and selected favorable intermediate-risk prostate cancer. However, conventional surveillance protocols rely heavily on repeated systematic biopsies, which impose procedural morbidity, patient burden, and limited precision in identifying true disease progression. Risk-adapted tools, including multi parametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI), molecular biomarkers, and genomic classifiers, have emerged as potential strategies to optimize surveillance intensity while preserving oncologic safety. To systematically evaluate the evidence supporting risk-adapted AS strategies incorporating mpMRI, molecular biomarkers, and genomic classifiers, with a focus on reducing biopsy burden without compromising oncologic outcomes.
METHODS: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus were searched for peer-reviewed studies evaluating mpMRI, molecular biomarkers, or genomic classifiers within AS cohorts. Randomized controlled trials and prospective or retrospective cohort studies reporting surveillance-related outcomes were included. Primary outcomes included biopsy upgrading or reclassification, AS failure, and oncologic safety endpoints. Due to methodological heterogeneity, results were synthesized narratively.
RESULTS: Five publications met inclusion criteria, representing four unique studies one randomized controlled trial and three observational cohorts and 1215 participants. The 2 Active Surveillance Magnetic Resonance Imaging Study publications were treated as linked reports from the same trial. Baseline mpMRI with targeted and systematic biopsy was associated with lower subsequent AS failure and upgrading, but biopsy avoidance was not directly tested. An MRI-led cohort omitted routine protocol biopsies, although the absence of a concurrent comparator precluded conclusions about equivalent oncologic safety. The 4Kscore demonstrated potential for confirmatory-biopsy triage; a hypothetical deferral strategy could have avoided 27% of biopsies but would have missed 2 Grade Group 2 upgrades. The Decipher genomic classifier independently predicted biopsy upgrading, although biopsy reduction was not evaluated. Evidence establishing the long-term oncologic safety of biopsy reduction remained insufficient.
CONCLUSION: Risk-adapted AS strategies incorporating mpMRI, molecular biomarkers, and genomic classifiers may improve risk stratification and support selective adjustment of biopsy intensity. However, current evidence does not establish the safety of routine biopsy omission or fully biopsy-free surveillance. Integration of these tools should remain individualized, with histologic reassessment when indicated and prospective validation of biopsy-deferral strategies.
43025799:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to compare single vs. dual antiplatelet therapy after fenestrated or branched endovascular aortic repair (FBEVAR).
DATA SOURCES: PubMed, MEDLINE, Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, and ProQuest Dissertations & Theses Global were searched from inception to 12 July 2026, with a supplementary targeted PubMed search on 5 September 2026.
REVIEW METHODS: Comparative studies of post-operative antiplatelet therapy were included. Methodological quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, and certainty of evidence using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation approach. Outcomes were synthesised narratively when clinical and methodological differences precluded meaningful pooling; an additional quantitative summary of study defined bleeding outcomes was also reported.
RESULTS: Six retrospective cohorts comprising 3 623 patients were included, with 3 197 patients in separately extractable single or dual antiplatelet therapy groups. Several studies reported associations favouring dual antiplatelet therapy for target vessel patency. However, differences in outcome definitions, analytical units, and treatment classification precluded a common pooled estimate, and one association was attenuated after accounting for treatment changes. Evidence regarding ischaemic events, mortality, re-intervention, and endoleak was insufficient for reliable pooled comparisons. Five cohorts reported peri-operative bleeding using heterogeneous definitions and observation periods, of which a four study summary yielded an odds ratio of 1.30 (95% confidence interval 0.87 - 1.94) for dual vs. single antiplatelet therapy. Given the differences in outcome definitions, this does not estimate a common clinical effect.
CONCLUSION: The current evidence comparing single and dual antiplatelet therapy after FBEVAR is based on heterogeneous cohort studies, focuses largely on surrogate outcomes such as target vessel patency, and shows no clear benefit for dual antiplatelet therapy. Comparative bleeding risk as well as clinical outcomes of single vs. dual antiplatelet therapy after FBEVAR remain uncertain. Future prospective studies are needed to better delineate superiority of one regimen over the other.
43025902: The purposes of this review are to summarize the pathophysiology of carotid near-occlusion (CNO) and formulate how known hemodynamic theory can be expanded to specifically address CNO. A systematic search revealed 51 articles addressing CNO pathophysiology. ICA flow reduction and collateral pathway activation are hallmarks of CNO. While CNO is associated with a high prevalence of reduced cerebrovascular reserve (CVR), severely impaired CVR was uncommon. Hence, hypoperfusion stroke mechanism is uncommon. Embolic mechanism studies are few and with mixed results. In hemodynamic theory variant, we propose that good collateral capacity results in CNO early during stenosis severity progression and no hemodynamic stroke/TIA. Conversely, we propose that poor collateral capacity results in more severe stenosis for CNO to develop and hemodynamic stroke/TIA will occur when the stenosis is sufficiently severe. This suggested theory predicts that a mismatch between too little distal collapse given a certain stenosis severity might indicate hypoperfusion. In conclusion, CNOs are flow-reducing stenoses associated with collateral use and unclear stroke mechanism. We propose an expansion of known hemodynamic theory to specifically address CNO where collateral capacity is the key factor that determines what stenosis severity is required for CNO to form and for hypoperfusion occur (if it occurs at all).
43026375:
BACKGROUND: Microvascular decompression (MVD) for glossopharyngeal neuralgia (GPN) presumes a compressive neurovascular conflict at the glossopharyngeal-vagal root entry zone, but the distribution of offending vessels has never been quantified across series.
OBJECTIVE: To estimate the pooled prevalence of each offending vessel identified at MVD for GPN, alongside pain relief, recurrence, mortality and complications.
METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched from inception through August 2026. Studies with at least five GPN patients undergoing MVD and extractable outcomes were included. Proportions were pooled using the Freeman-Tukey double arcsine transformation and a DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model. Risk of bias was assessed with the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS).
RESULTS: Nineteen observational studies (1,000 MVD patients) were included, and methodological quality was acceptable to moderate (modified NOS median 5/6; comparative cohorts 6-7/9). Fifteen studies (674 patients) reported vessel-specific findings. The posterior inferior cerebellar artery (PICA) was implicated, alone or in combination, in 87% of patients (95% confidence interval [CI] 83-90), the least heterogeneous outcome (I² = 27.9%). Vertebral artery involvement was 12% (7-17), anterior inferior cerebellar artery involvement 7% (4-12) and venous conflict 3% (1-6). Multiple-vessel conflict was present in 14% (9-20). Immediate pain relief was 94% (92-97) and relief at last follow-up 90% (85-94) after a weighted mean follow-up of 66 months, with recurrence in 4% (1-9). Five deaths occurred (0.5%), four in earlier surgical eras. Sensitivity analyses for cohort overlap, rootlet section and unretrieved reports changed no estimate by 2 percentage points or more.
CONCLUSION: The PICA was involved in about nine of ten patients with vessel data, the most consistent estimate in the review. About one in seven patients had more than one offending vessel, supporting full-length inspection of the IX-X rootlets rather than treatment of the first conflict encountered.
43026867: Positron emission tomography/magnetic resonance imaging (PET/MRI) has represented a paradigm shift in medical imaging, and although its use has not yet been fully incorporated into all clinical guidelines, scientific evidence supports its ability to provide a highly accurate simultaneous metabolic and anatomical assessment, which is particularly useful for staging, treatment planning, and evaluating treatment response in cancer patients. The limited availability of the technique and the demands it places on resources and coordination suggest that its initial use should focus on those applications that can provide the greatest benefit to patients, especially within the indications related to oncological processes, where PET and MRI have a defined and complementary role. This review focuses specifically on some of these conditions.
43031806:
BACKGROUND: Traditional Chinese medicine injections (TCMIs) are widely employed by Chinese clinicians as adjuvant therapy for Ischemic Heart Failure(IHF). A Bayesian network meta-analysis was conducted to compare the efficacy and safety of conventional treatment (CT) to those that included six TCMIs in patients with IHF.
OBJECTIVE: To compare the efficacy and safety of six TCMIs as adjuncts to CT for IHF using Bayesian network meta-analysis.
METHODS: Eight databases (CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, SinoMed, PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science) were searched from inception to May 6, 2026, for randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2.0, certainty of evidence using CINeMA, and Bayesian analyses using R 4.6.0 and Stata 17.0.
RESULTS: A total of 154 RCTs involving 13,756 participants were included. Compared with CT alone, adjunctive TCMIs generally improved clinical response and left ventricular ejection fraction(LVEF), and reduced B-type natriuretic peptide(BNP) and left ventricular end-diastolic dimension(LVEDD); effects on N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide(NT-pro BNP) were uncertain. Surface under the cumulative ranking curve(SUCRA) estimates Shenmai injection(SMI) had the highest probability of ranking favorably for clinical effectiveness rate(CER) and left ventricular ejection fraction(LVEF), Shengmai injection(SHMI) for B-type natriuretic peptide(BNP), Xinmailong injection(XMLI) for N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide(NT-pro BNP), Yiqifumai injection(YQFMI) for left ventricular end-diastolic dimension(LVEDD), and Shenfu injection(SFI) for 6-minute walking distance(6MWT). Short-term adverse-event rates were not increased overall.
CONCLUSION: TCMIs combined with CT has potential benefits in the treatment of IHF, but confidence in treatment rankings is limited by low or very low certainty of evidence, substantial heterogeneity for several outcomes, methodological limitations, and the absence of direct head-to-head trials. Large, rigorously designed RCTs with long-term safety follow-up are required.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier (CRD 420261380716).
43032439:
INTRODUCTION: Although computed tomography (CT) provides valuable information in severe asthma, its indications and interpretation remain nonstandardized and often undervalued, making consensus between pulmonologists and radiologists crucial to optimize its clinical use.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: An expert panel of 85 pulmonologists specialized in asthma and thoracic radiologists completed a two-round Delphi process, rating 33 statements on a 1-9 Likert scale using the RAND/UCLA appropriateness method.
RESULTS: Seventy-six experts completed round 1 (89.4%) and 70 completed both rounds (82.3%); 76.3% were pulmonologists and 23.7% thoracic radiologists. Consensus was achieved for 32/33 statements in round 1 and for the three reevaluated statements in round 2, yielding 34 recommendations organized in six thematic blocks. Panelists highly recommended performing high-resolution chest CT (HRCT) in all patients with severe uncontrolled asthma and when complications are suspected to establish differential diagnoses and identify associated entities. Specific recommendations were provided for CT acquisition and interpretation, including parameter-specific guidance for relevant features such as airway wall thickening (wall area percentage, lumen area, total airway count), small-airway disease (air trapping with or without emphysema), mucus plugging (standardized scoring), and comorbidities (e.g., bronchiectasis). They also agreed on the importance of performing HRCT before and after starting biologic therapies to guide drug selection and to assess response, and highlighted future opportunities for radiomultiomics and artificial intelligence.
CONCLUSIONS: Chest CT is a highly valuable objective tool in severe asthma, and CT-derived parameters have the potential to become established imaging biomarkers to support clinical decision-making. This consensus document provides recommendations to guide CT use and interpretation, contributing to improved patient management and personalized care.
43032931:
INTRODUCTION: Brachial plexus injuries carry significant long-term morbidity, and intraoperative differentiation of injury severity remains challenging, particularly in lesions in continuity and proximal/root-level injuries. Multimodal intraoperative neuromonitoring (IONM) offers real-time physiologic guidance during surgical decision-making. However, it remains unclear how each modality should be applied and interpreted, what quantitative criteria define a positive nerve action potential (NAP), what IONM can establish about nerve injury grade, and how robust the supporting evidence is. This review synthesizes the literature on multimodal IONM in brachial plexus surgery to address these gaps and appraise the methodological quality of the underlying studies.
METHODS: A PRISMA-aligned systematic review was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library. From 2909 records, 2120 unique studies were screened; 133 underwent full-text review, and 44 met inclusion criteria. Methodological quality was evaluated using the Methodological Index for Non-Randomized Studies (MINORS), scored out of 16. Data were synthesized qualitatively by modality and lesion type in adult and pediatric cohorts.
RESULTS: The 44 included studies encompassed traumatic, iatrogenic, and obstetric injuries with substantial heterogeneity in IONM protocols and reporting. Nerve action potential (NAP) recording was the primary modality for lesions in continuity, with conducting lesions preserved and managed by neurolysis. However, the corollary rule that a non-conducting lesion should be resected and grafted was not applied uniformly and is not supported by consistent data: in one series, six of six lesions with complete functional loss and no recordable NAP but no caliber change recovered usefully after internal neurolysis rather than grafting. Adjunct modalities (EMG, MEP, SSEP, CMAP) rarely overrode NAP-based decisions, although SSEPs and MEPs served the distinct role of separating preganglionic from postganglionic root injury. Of the 44 included studies, 11 assessed intraoperative NAPs, none of which reported explicit quantitative criteria for defining a positive NAP. Pediatric evidence was limited. Overall methodological quality was modest, with a median MINORS score of 9 of 16 (range 6-13); unbiased endpoint assessment was adequate in only 8 of 44 studies, and none reported a prospective sample-size calculation.
CONCLUSIONS: Multimodal IONM is standard in brachial plexus surgery, with NAP recordings guiding decisions for lesions in continuity. The contribution of this review is to show that the literature used to justify NAP-guided management is non-comparative, internally inconsistent for the non-conducting lesion, and rarely reports either a quantitative signal threshold or the grade of neurolysis performed. Prospective multicenter studies are needed to define signal thresholds, generate contemporary outcome data for non-conducting lesions managed by preservation, and report the specific procedure meant by "neurolysis." These needs are most acute in pediatric populations, where validated thresholds are entirely lacking.
43033237: Desmoid tumors are proliferative mesenchymal tumors arising from musculoaponeurotic structures. Although lacking the ability to metastasize, these neoplasms have a propensity to locally invade and recur, resulting in significant morbidity and reduced quality of life. This variable natural history and unpredictable biologic behavior can complicate clinical management. Active surveillance may be appropriate as initial management, with systemic, surgical and other local treatment options considered depending on the extent of disease progression, in accordance with the current National Comprehensive Cancer Network guidelines. Notably, image-guided percutaneous cryoablation has emerged as an effective treatment option for rapid local control and sustained lesion regression. The efficacy of cryoablation in the management of these tumors is now supported by an increasing body of literature. This article will review the pathophysiology and natural history of desmoid tumors, together with treatment indications and national cancer guidelines. Image-guided ablation techniques will be described as well as how these options can fit into clinical paradigms and management pathways.
43033238:
OBJECTIVE: Evidence on endovascular treatment (EVT) for isolated cervical internal carotid artery occlusion (c-ICA-O) due to dissection is limited. We evaluated the impact of EVT for dissection-related isolated (non-tandem) c-ICA-O.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: This secondary analysis of the multicenter EVT for Isolated cervical Internal Carotid Artery occlusion (ETIICA) retrospective study included patients with dissections. Patients treated with EVT were compared with those treated with best medical treatment alone. The primary endpoint was 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) shift analysis. Secondary outcomes included mRS 0-2 or return to baseline, early neurological deterioration (END), symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage (sICH), carotid patency at the end of EVT, and intracranial embolization. Analyses used regressions with inverse probability of treatment weighting.
RESULTS: Of 998 patients, 108 (10.8%) had dissection [mean age 53.7 (SD 11.2) years, 26.9% female]. EVT was performed in 60 (55.5%) patients. EVT patients had higher admission NIHSS (median 13 [4-18] vs 2 [0-9]). There was no difference in mRS shift (acOR 0.80, 95% CI: 0.29-2.20). Functional independence was observed in 64.9% of EVT patients vs 81.3% of BMT patients (aOR 1.69, 95% CI: 0.52-5.51; BMT as reference). END was numerically more frequent in the EVT group (28.8% vs 8.3%; aOR 2.38, 95% CI: 0.62-9.18). sICH occurred in 2 EVT patients. Carotid patency was achieved in 45/60 (75%) patients undergoing EVT, and 18/59 (30%) patients had intracranial embolization.
CONCLUSION: In this exploratory analysis, EVT was not associated with improved 3-month functional outcomes, despite achieving carotid patency in three out of four patients.
KEY POINTS: Question What are the technical and clinical outcomes of EVT compared with best medical treatment in patients with isolated cervical internal carotid artery occlusive dissection? Findings EVT effectively recanalized acutely occluded dissected extracranial internal carotid arteries, but intracranial emboli and re-occlusion were frequent, with no adjusted 90-day clinical benefit. Clinical relevance Precaution and technical refinement of EVT for isolated cervical carotid artery dissection appear necessary. Larger studies focusing on severely affected patients are warranted. Until such evidence is available, treatment decisions should be individualized on a case-by-case basis.
43033282:
IMPORTANCE: Carboplatin improves pathological complete response (pCR) in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), but its effect on long-term survival remains uncertain. We conducted a strict randomized-contrast meta-analysis to assess the incremental effect of adding carboplatin to otherwise substantially comparable chemotherapy regimens.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched from database inception. Phase II/III randomized controlled trials comparing carboplatin-containing versus carboplatin-free otherwise substantially comparable chemotherapy regimens in non-metastatic TNBC were included. Directly reported HRs for trial-defined disease-control endpoints and OS, and odds ratios (ORs) for pCR were pooled using random-effects models. Sensitivity analyses assessed the robustness of the disease-control and OS findings.
RESULTS: Seven randomized contrasts (2,627 randomized participants) contributed disease-control evidence. Carboplatin significantly improved trial-defined disease control (HR 0.779, 95% CI 0.671-0.904; p = 0.001; I2 = 40.6%) and increased pCR rates (OR 2.038, 95% CI 1.653-2.512; p < 0.001; I2 = 29.9%). The OS estimate favored carboplatin but was compatible with no effect (HR 0.810, 95% CI 0.627-1.046; p = 0.107; I2 = 41.4%). The sensitivity analysis restricted to aligned EFS-type endpoints remained favorable (HR 0.793, 95% CI 0.656-0.960; p = 0.017; I2 = 31.4%).
CONCLUSION: Carboplatin addition significantly improves pCR and trial-defined disease control in TNBC when evaluated in otherwise substantially comparable randomized chemotherapy contrasts. However, the strict evidence did not establish an OS benefit.
43033338:
BACKGROUND: Histotripsy is an emerging noninvasive, nonthermal ablative therapy recently introduced for the treatment of hepatic malignancies. This systematic review evaluated the efficacy and safety of histotripsy for primary and secondary liver tumors.
METHODS: PubMed and Scopus were searched from inception through August 2026 in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. Search terms included combinations of subject headings and keywords such as "histotripsy," "hepatic," and "metastases."
RESULTS: Ten clinical studies published between 2022 and 2026 met inclusion criteria. Study populations included hepatocellular carcinoma and metastases from colorectal, neuroendocrine, pancreatic, breast, and other malignancies. Technical success ranged from 68.8% to 100%, although definitions varied across studies. Early treatment efficacy and local control were generally high among successfully treated tumors, with several studies reporting rates exceeding 90%. Longer-term oncologic data were limited by heterogeneous imaging criteria, treatment intent, and patient populations. Major complications were uncommon, although vascular thrombosis and acute kidney injury emerged as potential safety concerns.
CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence supports the technical feasibility and short-term efficacy of hepatic histotripsy. However, standardized outcome definitions, longer follow-up, and comparative studies are needed to establish its durability and role relative to existing liver-directed therapies.
43033487:
BACKGROUND: Chronic subdural hematoma (cSDH) is increasingly treated with middle meningeal artery embolization (MMAe), but the impact of technical factors such as degree of penetration, standalone coiling, and the number of embolized branches remains poorly defined. We sought to perform a systematic review and meta-analysis to determine how these technical factors affect outcomes.
METHODS: We performed a PRISMA‑guided systematic review and meta‑analysis of studies reporting on technical factors identified in PubMed, Scopus, Ovid Embase (Elsevier), and the Web of Science. Adults with nonacute subdural hematomas undergoing standalone or adjunct MMAe were included. Outcomes of interest included need for rescue treatment and radiographic success. Random effects models were used to obtain pooled estimates for each outcome.
RESULTS: A total of 13 studies comprising 1,480 patients undergoing 1,727 embolizations were included. The weighted mean age was 70.8 years and 27.8% of patients were female. Onyx was the most common embolic agent used. Compared with distal penetration, proximal penetration was not significantly associated with radiographic success (OR 0.63, 95% CI 0.40-1.01; I2 = 25.4%; P = 0.05) or rescue treatment (OR 1.60, 95% CI 0.67-3.81; I2 = 0%; P = 0.29). Standalone coiling was not significantly associated with radiographic success (OR 1.30, 95% CI 0.77-2.21; I2 = 0%) or rescue treatment (OR 1.20, 95% CI 0.43-3.38; I2 = 0%; P = 0.73). There was also no significant difference in the odds of radiographic success (OR 0.83, 95% CI 0.49-1.42; I2 = 51.5%; P = 0.50) or rescue treatment (OR 0.96, 95% CI 0.39-2.34; I2 = 27.9%; P = 0.93) when comparing single versus multiple MMA branches embolized.
CONCLUSIONS: Degree of penetration, standalone coiling, and number of branches embolized were not significantly associated with outcomes in this limited meta-analysis. Although the point estimate favored distal penetration for radiographic success, the confidence interval included no difference and does not establish superiority. The evidence is limited by a small number of retrospective studies, heterogeneous reporting/outcome definitions, short follow-up, and potential selection bias. Multicenter studies with core lab-adjudicated outcomes are needed to investigate this topic further.
43034193:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate whether automated carotid plaque quantification on carotid computed tomography angiography (CTA) can serve as an adjunctive risk stratification tool for identifying patients with coexisting obstructive coronary artery disease (OCAD).
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This dual-center retrospective study included 2533 adults undergoing paired carotid and coronary CTA within 3 months. Carotid plaque components (calcified, fibrotic, and lipid) were quantified automatically. In the modeling cohort, three diagnostic models for OCAD (stenosis ≥ 50%) were developed using LASSO regression: clinical, plaque, and integrated models. Performance was assessed by AUC (with DeLong's test), decision curve analysis, and calibration curves, with validation in an internal validation set and a temporally independent validation cohort. Sensitivity analysis was performed using severe stenosis (≥ 70%) as the outcome.
RESULTS: All carotid plaque volumes were significantly associated with OCAD (p < 0.001). Calcified plaque volume (OR, 2.43; 95% CI: 1.95-3.04) and fibrotic plaque volume (OR, 1.37; 95% CI: 1.01-1.85) were independent predictors. The plaque model achieved an AUC of 0.785 (95% CI: 0.761-0.810) in the training set, comparable to the integrated model (AUC, 0.800) and superior to the clinical model (AUC, 0.723; p < 0.001). Performance remained robust in the internal (AUC, 0.824) and external validation set (AUC, 0.813). The integrated model demonstrated good calibration. Sensitivity analysis yielded consistent results.
CONCLUSION: In this retrospective study, automated carotid plaque quantification on CTA provides an adjunctive risk stratification tool to identify patients at high risk for coexisting OCAD, potentially guiding decisions regarding downstream coronary examinations.
KEY POINTS: Question Quantitative analysis of carotid plaque components on CTA may help identify patients with OCAD. Findings A model integrating automated carotid plaque volumes and clinical factors effectively identified OCAD. Clinical Relevance This study demonstrates that automated carotid plaque quantification on CTA may serve as an adjunctive risk stratification tool to guide downstream coronary testing in patients with cerebrovascular disease.
43034255: Acute aortic syndromes (AAS) are a group of aortic pathologies with high morbidity and mortality. In the emergency setting, an accurate diagnosis is usually achieved by aortic computed tomography angiography (CTA). Recently, reporting and management guidelines have evolved due to modifications in surgical techniques and the expansion in utilization of endovascular techniques. This being said, radiologists require a more in-depth knowledge of key points to report to surgeons, their clinical implications, and some insights into available imaging-guided treatment options. Given the urgent nature of AAS, the need for rapid, detailed, and standardized reporting is crucial. In this review, we aim to introduce a step-by-step approach to accurate reporting of AAS, discussing recent guidelines and the role of imaging in the preprocedural evaluation of each disease entity (namely, intramural hematoma, penetrating aortic ulcer, and aortic dissection). Additionally, we will highlight the role of key imaging findings in the management of each disease entity. KEY POINTS: Question Acute aortic syndromes require rapid, sufficiently detailed, and accurate diagnosis to allow for timely patient management. Findings In this article, we propose a step-by-step approach using a structured reporting checklist. Clinical relevance Using a stepwise approach will allow timely reporting, give important details, and help guide further patient care.
43034599:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Lack of international guidelines is hampering treatment quality and progress in the field of rectal endoluminal high dose rate brachytherapy (EHB). Standardisation of dose reporting would allow for better comparison of clinical results between patient cohorts and allow tumour control and normal tissue complication probability modelling. This work presents consensus recommendations for target volume and organs at risk (OAR) delineation in rectal EHB to support standardised dose reporting, for which consistent delineation is a prerequisite.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Recommendations were developed according to the AGREE II instrument, using a modified Delphi approach. The process included selection of international experts, a survey on current practices, delineation of three patient cases, and three consensus meetings to discuss the findings and formulate recommendations.
RESULTS: The expert group included 30 members from nine countries. The survey and first delineation round showed marked variation in treatment preparation and in the definition and delineation of target volumes and OARs. Consensus was reached on prerequisites for adequate delineation. Target volumes for dose reporting were defined: GTV primary at the time of EHB (GTVp_BT), an evaluation structure (GTVp_BT_ev05), and any macroscopic lymph nodes at the time of EHB (GTVn_BT). Recommendations for OAR selection and delineation were also established.
CONCLUSION: The GI GEC working group of GEC-ESTRO has developed consensus recommendations for target volume definition and OAR delineation in rectal EHB. These recommendations will be implemented in clinical practice. The proposed structures provide a foundation for standardised dose reporting, independent of local prescription practices.
43034829:
BACKGROUND: Several clinical guidelines exist to identify intracranial injury (ICI) after head injury. The Scandinavian Neurotrauma Committee (SNC) published evidence- and consensus-based guidelines in 2000, updated in 2013. Since then, demographic changes, including an ageing population and increased use of antithrombotic therapy have prompted further revision. The aim of this study is to provide a clinically relevant update to the SNC guidelines for the initial management of adults with minimal, mild, or moderate head injury.
METHODS: A PRISMA-compliant systematic review and meta-analysis addressed population, exposure, comparator, and outcome questions on which emergency department patients with minimal or mild head injury require head computed tomography (CT), direct discharge, in-hospital observation, or repeat CT. Evidence was graded using the GRADE approach. Recommendations were developed through a modified Delphi process with stakeholder review.
FINDINGS: Twenty-nine stakeholders participated in developing a seven-point recommendation set and updated management flowcharts. Key changes include reduced emphasis on routine CT in patients receiving direct oral anticoagulants, incorporation of glial fibrillary acidic protein and ubiquitin C-terminal hydrolase L1 biomarkers, and use of structured observation as an alternative to CT in selected risk groups.
INTERPRETATION: The updated guidelines support risk-adapted imaging and observation strategies that may reduce unnecessary CT scans and hospital admissions, although further validation of safety and effectiveness is needed.
FUNDING: No specific funding.
43034937: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is highly prevalent and frequently first recognized at ultrasound, but conventional B-mode assessment is limited by subjectivity and reduced sensitivity for mild steatosis. Quantitative ultrasound (QUS) techniques address these limitations by converting acoustic signal properties into numerical biomarkers of hepatic fat, including attenuation coefficient, backscatter coefficient, speed of sound, and composite measures. This review summarizes the technical principles, current evidence, clinical implementation, and limitations of ultrasound-based liver fat quantification techniques in MASLD. Their major advantages are accessibility, integration into routine ultrasound examinations, and potential use alongside elastography for multiparametric assessment. However, thresholds vary across vendors, software implementations, acquisition protocols, reference standards, and patient populations, limiting interchangeability and universal cutoffs. In clinical practice, ultrasound fat quantification should not be interpreted in isolation but integrated with fibrosis risk stratification and metabolic risk assessment. Further multicenter studies are needed to standardize acquisition and reporting, define clinically meaningful longitudinal changes, and link ultrasound-derived fat reduction with patient outcomes. QUS is therefore best regarded as an evolving, practical framework for objective steatosis assessment that complements, rather than replaces, comprehensive MASLD risk stratification. KEY POINTS: Question Conventional B-mode ultrasound is subjective and insensitive to mild hepatic steatosis, creating an unmet need for objective, reproducible liver fat quantification in MASLD. Findings Attenuation-based and composite quantitative ultrasound methods provide objective liver fat assessment, but vendor-dependent thresholds currently limit interchangeability and universal clinical application. Clinical relevance Quantitative ultrasound enables accessible, objective liver fat assessment during routine imaging, improving detection and grading of hepatic steatosis and supporting risk-based MASLD care; however, vendor-specific thresholds and acquisition variability require technique-specific interpretation.
43034939:
OBJECTIVES: To compare conventional and delayed (≥ 30 min) hepatobiliary-phase (HBP) gadoxetate-enhanced MRI for the detection of bile leaks.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included all consecutive gadoxetate-enhanced MRI examinations comprising delayed HBP acquisitions performed for suspected biliary leak over 2 years at a tertiary hepatobiliary referral center. Two abdominal radiologists blinded to clinical records independently assessed leak presence at each timepoint. A composite reference standard incorporating endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography, surgical exploration, percutaneous drainage findings, and multidisciplinary assessment was utilized to assign ground-truth leak status. Sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values (PPV, NPV), accuracy, and inter-reader agreement were calculated.
RESULTS: Thirty-five patients (22 men; median age, 56 years; interquartile range (IQR), 48-65) undergoing 36 examinations were included. The most common indications were liver transplantation (n = 13/35, 37%) and cholecystectomy (n = 11/35, 31%). Conventional and delayed HBP were acquired at a median of 21 and 65 min after injection, respectively. Twenty-two of 36 examinations (61%) were ground-truth positive. Inter-reader agreement was perfect for conventional HBP (κ = 1.00) and excellent for delayed HBP (κ = 0.94; 95% CI 0.84-1.00). Conventional HBP demonstrated 27% sensitivity (95% CI 11-50%), 100% specificity (95% CI 77-100%), and 56% accuracy (95% CI 38-72%). Delayed HBP demonstrated 82% sensitivity (95% CI 60-95%), 100% specificity (95% CI 77-100%), and 89% accuracy (95% CI 74-97%). NPV increased from 47% to 78%. Delayed HBP yielded higher sensitivity and overall accuracy than conventional HBP (p < 0.001, exact McNemar tests).
CONCLUSION: Delayed HBP improved bile leak detection without loss of specificity.
KEY POINTS: Question Does extending gadoxetate hepatobiliary-phase MRI acquisitions beyond the conventional 20-min window improve the detection of active bile leaks? Findings Delayed hepatobiliary-phase imaging raised sensitivity for bile leak detection from 27% to 82% without loss of specificity, highlighting acquisition timing as a key diagnostic determinant. Clinical relevance Delayed gadoxetate hepatobiliary-phase imaging is an effective adjunct for detecting active bile leaks and should be considered when findings at conventional timing are negative or equivocal, with direct implications for clinical management.
43035265: Conventional CT-guided percutaneous for thoracic lesions is primarily performed via freehand manipulation by the operator, and its accuracy is constrained by individual experience. Artificial intelligence optical navigation-assisted systems enable precise execution of preplanned puncture trajectories and visual guidance through high-precision spatial localization and robotic arm navigation, thereby markedly improving puncture success rate and procedural safety. To standardize and promote this technique and advance the precision diagnosis and treatment of thoracic tumors, this consensus was formulated by domestic experts organized jointly by the Ablation Expert Committee of the Chinese Society of Clinical Oncology (CSCO), the Society of Tumor Ablation Therapy of the Chinese Anti-Cancer Association, the Expert Group on Tumor Ablation Therapy of the Chinese Medical Doctors Association, the Tumor Ablation Committee of the Chinese College of Interventionalists,following in-depth discussions. This consensus mainly covers: (1) artificial intelligence optical navigation systems and puncture devices; (2) protocols and precautions for artificial intelligence optical navigation-assisted CT-guided percutaneous puncture for thoracic lesions.
43035977:
PURPOSE: Iodine contrast enhancement is assessed using computed tomography (CT) number, though this value is not proportional to iodine concentration. This study develops a metric for iodine enhancement that is directly proportional to iodine concentration.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Using studies previously reported in the literature, we parameterized the effect to create a correction for tube potential and patient-size-specific beam hardening on iodine CT number decrease. To validate the correction, we performed a study using different iodine concentrations, phantom sizes, and tube potentials. We also applied the correction to patient pulmonary angiogram data. Patients were grouped by tube potential [80, 100, 120, 140] (kV). Quantitative iodine contrast enhancement (Q-ICE) (ie, the difference between noncontrast and contrast-enhanced CT number) of the pulmonary artery (PA) was calculated. Pearson correlation coefficients are reported to characterize trends in PA Q-ICE across weight before and after correction.
RESULTS: The range of CT numbers measured for [10, 15] mg/mL iodine inserts was [290, 433] HU before correction, and [24, 36] HU after correction. Before correction, median PA Q-ICE enhancement was [662, 490, 263, 175] HU for [80, 100, 120, 140] kV, with a range of 487 HU observed across all measurements. After correction, the median PA Q-ICE enhancement was [366, 373, 285, 249] HU, with a range of 124 HU. Pearson correlation coefficients significantly (P < 0.05) decreased after correction from -0.67 to -0.37.
CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrated a method to normalize effects of tube potential and beam hardening on CT number, yielding a metric proportional to iodine concentration.
43036028:
OBJECTIVES: After FDA approval in 2021, photon-counting detector computed tomography (PCCT) has demonstrated its feasibility for high-resolution imaging while lowering the radiation dose at the same time. High-resolution visualization of cochlear implant (CI) integrity and positioning is crucial for postoperative management. The aim of this study was to evaluate the performance of PCCT for postoperative imaging after CI implantation in comparison to high-resolution flat-detector CT (FDCT), the current clinical gold standard.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Postoperative PCCT scans after cochlear implantation were retrospectively analyzed from August 2024 to April 2026. Scans were included for analysis if FDCT acquisition had been before PCCT on the same patient in the course of sequential bilateral cochlear implantation. Image quality was assessed in consensus by 2 experienced readers using a scoring system analyzing structural delineation of the inner and middle ear, CI integrity, metal and motion artifacts as well as calculating an overall score. Radiation dose was retrieved from the picture archiving and communication system.
RESULTS: Twenty-eight postoperative PCCT scans of patients after CI implantation with a mean time delay of 4.5±5.1 years between FDCT and PCCT scans were evaluated. Image quality of PCCT was noninferior to FDCT for all single imaging features (P<0.001, eg, distinction of single CI electrodes: median [interquartile range] PCCT 3 [3 to 3]; FDCT 3 [3 to 3]; P<0.001) with the exception of the homogeneity of bony structures and the mastoid cell septation (P=0.999). PCCT was superior to FDCT in reducing metal and motion artifacts and increasing the delineation of the stapes (P=0.009 to <0.001; eg, metal artifacts PCCT 3 [2.75 to 3]; FDCT 2 [1 to 2]; P<0.001). Effective radiation dose of PCCT was 0.05±0.01 mSv and 8.8±5.4-times lower than for FDCT with 0.44±0.29 mSv (P<0.001) applying our institutional protocols.
CONCLUSIONS: Regarding image quality in postoperative assessment of CI, PCCT is noninferior to or in single features better than FDCT at a significantly lower radiation dose and shorter scan time.
43036317: High dose rate (HDR) interstitial liver brachytherapy has become one of the established local ablative treatment options for selected primary and secondary liver tumours that are unsuitable for surgical resection. With its steep dose gradient and high conformality, it enables precise dose delivery to the target while effectively sparing surrounding healthy liver tissue and adjacent organs at risk. These consensus recommendations provide comprehensive, standardised guidance on the technique and workflow of interstitial HDR liver brachytherapy, including image-guided catheter implantation, implantation techniques, and treatment planning. The recommendations further summarise available evidence on oncological outcomes, toxicities and adverse event management, and outline principles for post-treatment follow-up. The consensus recommendations were developed by an expert panel of the GEC-ESTRO Gastrointestinal Working Group based on published evidence and collective clinical experience. They aim to harmonise practice across centres, promote safe and effective treatment delivery, and facilitate future research and data comparison in this evolving field of liver-directed radiotherapy.
43036367: Cerebral autosomal dominant arteriopathy with subcortical infarcts and leukoencephalopathy (CADASIL) is the most common monogenic cause of cerebral small vessel disease, yet its clinical management remains poorly harmonized across Europe. This consensus review, developed on behalf of the NEUROVASC Working Group, examines current diagnostic and management practices for CADASIL in Europe and identifies priority areas for evidence generation and care harmonization. We describe the geographic distribution of pathogenic NOTCH3 variants across European populations, the organization of referral pathways and specialized care networks, and current approaches to neuroimaging staging, genetic testing, and long-term follow-up. Management of major clinical manifestations is reviewed, including antithrombotic therapy and thrombolysis in acute stroke, cardiovascular risk factor control, migraine treatment, and cognitive and neuropsychiatric symptoms, areas in which practice is largely extrapolated from sporadic small vessel disease in the absence of disease-specific trials or guidelines. Closing these gaps will require multicenter registries and harmonized care pathways, validated outcome measures such as standardized MRI tools and disease severity staging, greater integration of patient-reported outcomes, and coordinated international collaboration. These efforts will help leverage the statistical power, genetic diversity, and clinical insights needed to advance-based, precision medicine approaches for patients with CADASIL.
43036783:
OBJECTIVES: Stage III NSCLC represents one of the most heterogeneous and clinically challenging scenarios in thoracic oncology. The rapid integration of immunotherapy into multimodal treatment strategies has reshaped therapeutic algorithms, particularly for resectable and borderline resectable diseases. However, uncertainty persists regarding optimal staging procedures, resectability assessment, and the integration of surgery, systemic therapy, and radiotherapy.
METHODS: A multisocietal Delphi consensus was conducted to address key areas of uncertainty in the multidisciplinary management of stage III NSCLC. Experts in thoracic surgery, medical oncology, radiation oncology, interventional pulmonology, and pathology, nominated by four Italian scientific societies, participated in a structured consensus process. Sixty-five statements covering baseline evaluation, local treatment, and integrated therapeutic strategies were rated using a 9-point Likert scale across two Delphi rounds.
RESULTS: Consensus was achieved for 62 of 65 statements. Strong agreement supported comprehensive baseline staging, including contrast-enhanced computed tomography, positron emission tomography imaging, brain magnetic resonance imaging, and systematic mediastinal staging with endosonographic techniques. Molecular characterization, including Programmed Death-Ligand 1 expression and testing for EGFR and ALK alterations, was considered essential for treatment selection. Neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy was endorsed as the preferred strategy for most patients with resectable stage III NSCLC without actionable driver alterations. Lung-sparing surgical procedures were strongly favored, while pneumonectomy should be reserved for highly selected cases. For unresectable disease, concurrent chemoradiotherapy followed by consolidation immunotherapy remains the standard of care.
CONCLUSION: This multidisciplinary consensus provides an updated framework for the contemporary management of stage III NSCLC, emphasizing accurate staging, molecular profiling, and coordinated multidisciplinary decision-making to optimize multimodal treatment strategies.
43036895: People with peripheral artery disease (PAD) are often misdiagnosed or diagnosed late and, even after diagnosis, are undertreated with both pharmacologic and invasive therapies. The disease is associated with an increased risk of mortality, myocardial infarction, stroke, other vascular disease, limb loss, and reduced quality of life. Although the risks and long-term management of PAD are well documented, these risks are acutely magnified when PAD exists as a comorbidity in patients hospitalized for other cardiovascular or medical conditions. Procedures requiring vascular access for the treatment of acute myocardial infarction, cardiogenic shock, or valvular heart disease, as well as procedures for the treatment of the patient's underlying PAD, require special consideration in patients with PAD. Familiarity with the use and placement of mechanical circulatory support in patients with PAD, as well as the management of recent endovascular or surgical vascular interventions, is essential for providing appropriate care in the acute care setting.
43037655: Biomarkers reflect underlying physiological or pathological processes and support disease detection, cancer diagnosis, treatment selection and prognosis, monitoring of therapeutic response, and identification of disease recurrence in interventional oncology (IO) care. In recent years, liquid biopsy of circulating biomarkers has emerged as a transformative approach in oncology. Given the growing role of IO in cancer care and the potential for circulating biomarkers to directly impact patient care in Interventional Radiology, this narrative review summarizes circulating biomarker types, current detection technologies and workflows, clinical applications in IO care, and next-generation biomarker modalities and detection instruments for Interventional Radiologists.
43039116:
OBJECTIVE: To compare vascular complications between percutaneous and surgical access during transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve implantation (tf-TAVI) and estimate pooled outcomes following percutaneous access.
DESIGN: Systematic review and meta-analysis of comparative and single-arm studies.
DATA SOURCES AND REVIEW METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to 8 July 2026 (PROSPERO CRD420261454909). Comparative (odds ratio [OR]) and single-arm (pooled proportion) random-effects meta-analyses were performed. Subgroup, meta-regression, sensitivity, and publication-bias analyses were conducted for the primary outcome. Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-I, ROBINS-I Single Arm, and RoB 2.
RESULTS: Ten comparative studies (4 736 patients) and eight single-arm studies (5 113 patients) were included. Major vascular complications did not differ significantly between percutaneous access and surgical cutdown (OR 0.83, 95% CI 0.61-1.14; I2 = 41.8%; 95% prediction interval 0.39-1.78), with no significant differences in secondary clinical outcomes, including hospital length of stay (mean difference -0.96 days, 95% CI -2.38 to 0.47; p = .19). In the single-arm analysis, pooled major vascular complications after percutaneous TAVI were 5.20% (95% CI 3.52-7.63%; 95% prediction interval 1.43-17.21%; I2 = 91.1%), with 30-day mortality of 2.20% (95% CI 1.41-3.40%; 95% prediction interval 0.72-6.46%; I2 = 66.9%). Funnel plot asymmetry (Egger's p = .034) was attributable to a single zero-event study and was not confirmed by the Peters test (p = .651) or after its exclusion (p = .164).
CONCLUSION: Percutaneous femoral access was not associated with a statistically significant difference in major vascular complications or other clinically relevant outcomes compared with surgical cutdown in anatomically suitable patients treated at experienced centres; residual confounding cannot be excluded, and this evidence is largely observational and should be considered hypothesis-generating pending confirmation in randomized trials.
REGISTRATION: PROSPERO (CRD420261454909).
43039217:
PURPOSE: To compare bleeding-related adverse events after percutaneous liver biopsy with and without tract sealing, separating clinical outcomes from randomized evidence on a surrogate endpoint.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Systematic review following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Five databases were searched (2000 to August 2026) for percutaneous liver biopsy with tract sealing by any agent or energy. Adverse events were graded on the Society of Interventional Radiology scale as mild (grade 1) or moderate to fatal (grades 2 to 5). Comparative data were pooled using random-effects models, with the Peto method for major bleeding. Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 and ROBINS-I.
RESULTS: Twenty-two studies reporting 4,560 liver biopsy procedures were included. Two retrospective studies compared sealing with no sealing on clinically defined outcomes. Overall bleeding-related adverse events did not differ (OR 0.52; 95% CI 0.13-2.17; P = .370), whereas major bleeding was less frequent with sealing (Peto OR 0.09; 95% CI 0.02-0.42; P = .002; absolute risk difference 3.3%). Two randomized trials favored sealing on a Doppler surrogate but not on clinically significant bleeding. Major bleeding in single-arm cohorts ranged from 0% to 2.2%. Three studies comparing plugged percutaneous with transjugular biopsy allocated patients with worse coagulation indices to the transjugular arm.
CONCLUSION: Tract sealing was associated with fewer major bleeding-related adverse events but not fewer events overall. The evidence supports selective use in patients with identifiable bleeding risk but does not establish benefit in unselected low-risk patients.
43039767:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: To quantify heterogeneity in the treatment effects of first-line immuno-oncology (IO)-based combination regimens among patients with metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma (RCC) according to prognosis and potential effect modifiers and to assess which patients benefit most.
METHODS: Meta-analysis (preregistered in PROSPERO: CRD42023483638) including randomised trials underpinning first-line IO-based regimens recommended in the European Society for Medical Oncology 2024 guidelines using sunitinib as control, with mature overall survival (OS) data available as of November 2023. Individual patient data (IPD) were obtained for two trials and aggregate data for two others. Prognostic stratification was performed by the International Metastatic Renal Cell Carcinoma Database Consortium (IMDC) model and, for IPD trials, by the Clinical Prognostic Index in the Checkpoint Inhibitor era (CPI2) model. Effect modification by sex and programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression was assessed. OS benefit was summarised as a hazard ratio (HR) and, in IPD, as the difference in restricted mean survival time (dRMST), and was pooled across trials using fixed-effects inverse-variance-weighted models.
KEY FINDINGS AND LIMITATIONS: CheckMate-214, CheckMate-9ER, KEYNOTE-426 and CLEAR were included, totalling 3320 patients (IPD for CheckMate-214 and CheckMate-9ER; n = 1747). Among IPD studies, 42%, 32%, and 26% of patients had CPI2 favourable, intermediate, and poor prognosis, respectively. The respective pooled subgroup dRMSTs were 1.21 (95% CI = -0.82 to 3.25), 3.15 (0.50 to 5.81), and 7.36 (4.56 to 10.17) mo. Using all four studies, the pooled HRs for IMDC favourable, intermediate, and poor subgroups were 0.98 (0.81 to 1.19), 0.78 (0.68 to 0.89), and 0.51 (0.40 to 0.65), respectively. PD-L1 expression at 5% significantly modified the treatment effect.
CONCLUSIONS AND CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS: IO-based regimens showed highly divergent OS efficacy across prognostic subgroups, with no significant benefit among patients with a favourable prognosis and the strongest benefit in patients with a poor prognosis.
43040039:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the prevalence of pre-procedural US-MRI discordance and its association with Society of Interventional Radiology (SIR)-standardized outcomes in patients undergoing US-guided high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) ablation for symptomatic uterine fibroids.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: 308 consecutive patients were included. Discordance was defined as mismatch in fibroid type, location, uterine position, or absolute volume percentage difference > 50%. Patients were stratified into concordant (n = 252) and discordant (n = 56) groups. Outcomes were assessed according to SIR domains: technical success (non-perfused volume ratio on day-1 contrast-enhanced MRI), technical efficacy (through six procedural surrogates as a whole: energy-efficiency factor, overall treatment time, cumulative sonication time, treatment intensity, average sonication power, and oxytocin dose), adverse events (SIR classification), and favorable short-term procedural outcome.
RESULTS: Discordance occurred in 18.2% of cases. Categorical agreement was high, with Gwet's AC1 > 0.93, and volume agreement was good, with an intraclass correlation coefficient of 0.773. Day-1 non-perfused volume ratio and technical-success thresholds were comparable between groups. In unadjusted analysis, the energy-efficiency factor was higher after discordant imaging (p = 0.024) and oxytocin use was shifted toward the 60 IU dose (p = 0.036). After adjustment, neither association remained significant (p = 0.191 and 0.228). Adverse-event profiles and the favorable short-term procedural outcome did not differ significantly.
CONCLUSION: In this study, pre-HIFU US-MRI discordance was not associated with clear differences in technical success, technical efficacy, adverse events, or short-term procedural outcomes. Recognition of discordance may still help inform procedural planning and patient counseling within SIR-standardized frameworks.
43041118:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the adverse events and complications associated with focused ultrasound ablation surgery(FUAS)for benign uterine diseases in teaching and training centers.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: From October 2010 to December 2023, 26,844 patients with benign uterine diseases were treated with FUAS and more than 2000 doctors had been trained in three teaching and training centers. Among the treated patients, 16,619 had uterine fibroids, 8732 had adenomyosis, 1154 had cesarean scar pregnancy, and 379 had placental accreta spectrum. According to the classification system of the Society of Interventional Radiology (SIR), these adverse events were classified as mild adverse event (no therapy or nominal therapy), moderate adverse event (moderate escalation of care, requiring substantial treatment), severe adverse event (marked escalation of care), Life-threatening or disabling event, and patient death or unexpected pregnancy abortion.
RESULTS: Mild adverse effects occurred in 2,352 (8.75%) patients, moderate adverse events were seen in 147 (0.55%) patients, severe adverse events encountered in 50 (0.18%) patients. No life-threatening or disabling event, and patient death or unexpected pregnancy abortion occurred. The overall incidence rate of severe adverse events was 0.18% (n = 50). From 2010 to 2023, the annual incidence rates of severe adverse events were 0%, 0.42%, 0%, 0%, 0.28%, 0.23%, 0.09%, 0.08%, 0.20%, 0.28%, 0.44%, 0.16%, 0.16%, and 0.10%, respectively.
CONCLUSION: Based on the results, we concluded that FUAS is a safe treatment for benign uterine diseases. The training course for trainee did not increase the risk of severe adverse events.
43041327:
BACKGROUND: Peripheral absolute lymphocyte count (ALC) has emerged as a potential prognostic biomarker in patients with triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), but the available evidence remains inconsistent. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate the association between peripheral ALC and survival outcomes in patients with TNBC.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Wanfang, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI) were systematically searched from database inception to June 20, 2026. Observational studies evaluating the association between peripheral ALC and survival in adult patients with TNBC were included. Hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using random-effects models.
RESULTS: Ten studies involving 1,799 patients with TNBC were included. Low peripheral ALC was significantly associated with poorer overall survival (OS; eight studies, HR 2.22, 95% CI 1.73-2.85; I2 = 0%) and progression-free survival (PFS; six studies, HR 2.09, 95% CI 1.61-2.72; I2 = 4%). Subgroup analyses showed that no statistically significant subgroup differences in the association between low ALC and OS were detected according to tumor stage (stage I-III vs. stage IV), timing of ALC measurement (pretreatment vs. during treatment), method for determining the ALC cutoff (receiver operating characteristic curve analysis, median value, or predefined cutoff), ALC cutoff value (< 1.5 vs. ≥ 1.5 × 109/L), follow-up duration, analytic model (univariate vs. multivariate), or study quality (all p for subgroup differences > 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: Low peripheral ALC is associated with poorer OS and PFS in patients with TNBC. However, given the predominantly retrospective and geographically concentrated evidence, the potential prognostic utility of ALC requires validation in prospective studies across more diverse populations.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/, identifier CRD420261467726.
43042602:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the independent association in twin pregnancy between single intrauterine fetal demise (sIUFD) and major short-term adverse outcomes, particularly severe brain injury (SBI) or death, in extremely and very preterm liveborn cotwins (delivered < 32 weeks), to examine whether this association extends beyond chorionicity and to identify critical gestational windows of vulnerability and potential mediating pathways.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort study included twin pregnancies, with or without sIUFD, delivered < 32 weeks at Shengjing Hospital of China Medical University, Shenyang, China, between January 2014 and December 2024, with neonates admitted immediately after birth to the hospital's neonatal intensive care unit. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to assess associations between sIUFD and the primary outcome, a composite of SBI or death of the liveborn cotwin prior to hospital discharge. Subgroup analyses stratified by chorionicity and gestational age at sIUFD were performed to identify risk patterns and critical gestational windows of vulnerability. Mediation analyses were conducted to explore whether the association between sIUFD and SBI or death was mediated by early-onset sepsis, disseminated intravascular coagulation within 24 h after birth or the 5-min Apgar score, and sensitivity analyses incorporating propensity-score matching to balance baseline confounders were performed to assess the robustness of the results.
RESULTS: In total, 1069 twin pregnancies delivered < 32 weeks were included (113 with and 956 without sIUFD). sIUFD was independently associated with significantly increased odds of SBI or death (adjusted odds ratio (aOR), 2.85 (95% CI, 1.61-4.97)). This association was consistent across monochorionic and dichorionic subgroups. The highest point estimate was observed when sIUFD occurred at 28 + 0 to 29 + 6 weeks' gestation (aOR, 3.72 (95% CI, 1.64-8.06)). Mediation analysis identified a 5-min Apgar score < 7, suggestive of perinatal asphyxia, as the primary mediator of SBI or death (proportion mediated: 24.30%), while disseminated intravascular coagulation within 24 h after birth and early-onset sepsis acted as significant secondary mediators (proportions mediated: 6.60% and 4.30%, respectively).
CONCLUSIONS: sIUFD is independently associated with an increased risk of SBI or death in liveborn cotwins delivered < 32 weeks, regardless of chorionicity, particularly when demise occurs at 28 + 0 to 29 + 6 weeks. Perinatal asphyxia is the primary mediator of this association. These findings support intensified monitoring of all surviving cotwins, with surveillance guided by the gestational age at sIUFD. © 2026 International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology.
43042747:
RATIONALE: The link between endometriosis and infertility has been firmly established; however, the mechanism remains controversial. Management of ovarian endometriosis (endometrioma) in the context of assisted reproductive technology (ART) varies greatly both in regard to the intervention chosen or, indeed, the decision to treat at all. Management remains a key clinical decision for patients requiring fertility treatment and guidance from scientific evidence is vital. This is an update of a Cochrane review first published in 2010.
OBJECTIVES: To assess the effects of surgery, medical treatment, combination therapy (both medical and surgical) or no treatment for improving reproductive outcomes among women with endometrioma, prior to undergoing ART cycles.
SEARCH METHODS: We searched the Cochrane Gynaecology and Fertility Group's specialised register, CENTRAL, MEDLINE, Embase and PsycINFO on 7 October 2025. We also searched trial registries, checked reference lists of relevant studies and contacted experts in the field for any additional trials.
ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: We selected randomised controlled trials (RCTs) that compared any medical and/or surgical intervention with another medical and/or surgical intervention or placebo/no intervention for the treatment of endometrioma prior to ART. The included population was women with endometrioma diagnosed by laparoscopy or pelvic imaging such as ultrasound, computed tomography (CT), or magnetic-resonance imaging (MRI).
OUTCOMES: Our critical outcomes of interest, as presented in the summary of findings tables, were: live birth and adverse events.
RISK OF BIAS: We used the Cochrane RoB 1 tool to assess bias in the included studies.
SYNTHESIS METHODS: Due to significant heterogeneity between the included studies, we synthesised the results into a narrative review. We summarised key findings from individual studies descriptively and we structured them by outcome domain. We used GRADE to assess the certainty of evidence for the critical outcomes.
INCLUDED STUDIES: We included a total of seven parallel-arm RCTs with 646 participants randomised. Two studies (173 participants) evaluated medical interventions and five studies (473 participants) evaluated surgical interventions for endometrioma prior to ART. No studies evaluated combination therapy.
SYNTHESIS OF RESULTS: No clear benefit was found for any treatment over no treatment. We judged all studies to have a high or unclear risk of bias in at least two domains and graded the evidence as very low certainty as a result of this and imprecision due to low study numbers and wide confidence intervals. Below we report the critical outcomes, as presented in the summary of findings tables. Medical intervention: GnRH agonist protocol compared to control for ART The evidence is very uncertain about the effect of a GnRH agonist protocol compared to control on live birth (OR 3.70, 95% CI 1.25 to 10.90; 1 study, 64 participants; very low-certainty evidence). Adverse events were not reported. Surgical intervention (s): Endometrioma aspiration versus no aspiration The evidence is very uncertain about the effect of endometrioma aspiration compared to control on live birth (OR 1.66, 95% CI 0.59 to 4.62; 1 study, 81 participants; very low-certainty evidence). Adverse events were not reported. Endometrioma cystectomy versus no cystectomy The evidence is very uncertain about the effect of endometrioma cystectomy compared to control on live birth (OR 1.97, 95% CI 0.71 to 5.49; 1 study, 73 participants; very low-certainty evidence). Zero adverse events were reported in each study arm (1 study, 73 participants; very low-certainty evidence). Endometrioma transvaginal sclerotherapy versus no sclerotherapy No included study assessed live birth. Adverse events were not reported.
AUTHORS' CONCLUSIONS: This narrative review highlights the uncertainties regarding the management of endometrioma prior to ART. There is no high-certainty evidence that might change the current guidance for management plans to be developed on an individual basis, taking into account previous outcomes, ovarian reserve, and patient's wishes. Further robust, adequately powered studies are required to guide future clinical decision-making which include critical outcomes as per the core outcome set for endometriosis.
FUNDING: This Cochrane review had no dedicated funding.
REGISTRATION: Protocol (2010) https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD008571. Original review (2010) https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD008571.pub2.
43043089:
BACKGROUND: MCT8 transports thyroid hormones into the central nervous system. A genetic deficiency of MCT8 leads to hypothyroidism in the brain and severe neurological symptoms, a condition known as Allan-Herndon-Dudley syndrome (AHDS). Replacing MCT8 with gene therapy could effectively treat AHDS, but the most suitable target cell is yet to be identified. Since endogenous Mct8 is expressed by the glial tanycytes that form the blood-cerebrospinal fluid barrier in the hypothalamus, we tested the efficacy of tanycyte-directed gene therapy.
METHODS: We used Mct8-/- mice on an Oatp1c1-/- background (double knockout, DKO) as a model of AHDS to avoid compensation of OATP1C1 for MCT8 deficiency. After DKO mice received an intracerebroventricular injection of an adeno-associated virus encoding Mct8 at postnatal day 40, we investigated endocrine and neurological parameters of the disease.
RESULTS: The gene therapy approach restored Mct8 expression and normalized thyrotropin releasing hormone-induced signaling in DKO tanycytes, suggesting intact MCT8 function in these cells. Although MCT8 rescue in tanycytes did not correct the overactive hypothalamus-pituitary-thyroid axis in DKO mice, it improved triiodothyronine concentrations and gene expression in the cortex. Furthermore, it counteracted the reduction in brain weight in DKO mice.
CONCLUSIONS: Gene therapy targeting tanycytes improves neurological parameters in mice with Mct8 deficiency. Further research is needed to determine whether this approach could be used to treat AHDS.
43043132:
BACKGROUND: Invasive mold disease (IMD) remains a substantial cause of patient morbidity and mortality. Aspergillosis and mucormycosis remain the predominant infections encountered, although rare molds continue to emerge as important pathogens. Improvement in patient outcomes has been the result of progress in risk stratification, diagnostics, supportive care, antifungal therapy, and/or prophylaxis, yet substantial challenges remain, requiring the development of novel treatment strategies. Clinical trials evaluating treatment response are currently based on consensus criteria published in 2008. However, advances in clinical mycology and the broadening variety of mold diseases in clinical trials necessitate a revision of these criteria to ensure that adjudication of patient outcomes accurately captures responses to therapeutic intervention.
METHODS: To tackle this task, an international expert panel nominated by the European Confederation of Medical Mycology (ECMM) and Mycoses Study Group Education and Research Consortium (MSGERC) was convened.
