CONCLUSIONS: The current randomized evidence did not establish superiority of either timing strategy for mortality. Mortality evidence was low-certainty and substantially below the required information size of 15 352 patients; timing should therefore remain an individualized decision.
43056220:
AIMS: Despite phenotypic heterogeneity, the management of idiopathic non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (NICM) remains generalized and dominantly guided by left ventricular (LV) ejection fraction (EF) and NYHA class. We aimed to develop a point-of-service phenomapping pathway for dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) and hypokinetic non-dilated cardiomyopathy (HNDC) at time of CMR imaging leveraging the integration of i) patient self-reported health status, ii) imaging phenotype, and the iii) electronic health record (EHR).
METHODS AND RESULTS: 1,355 patients (752 DCM and 603 HNDC) were followed for the composite MACE outcome of mortality, heart failure hospitalization or ventricular arrhythmia. K-means clustering was independently applied to DCM and HNDC derivation cohorts using 55 routinely captured features (16 patient-reported health variables, 19 CMR-derived, 14 EHR-derived, and 6 combined features), identifying three phenogroups in each cohort. Over a median of 3.9 and 3.7 years, 145 DCM patients (22%) and 65 HNDC patients (13%), respectively, experienced MACE. Adjusting for age, sex, NYHA class, and LV EF, phenogroup membership was independently associated with future outcomes. In DCM, the adjusted HR (95% CI) of phenogroups 2 and 3 versus Phenogroup 1 were 2.8 (1.6-4.8) and 3.5 (1.9-6.5), respectively (p<0.001 for both). In HNDC, Phenogroup 3 demonstrated an adjusted HR of 4.2 (1.7-10.2; p=0.001) versus Phenogroup 1. Prospective phenogroup assignment was enabled by a decision tree-classifier and validated in a temporal hold-out cohort.
CONCLUSION: Phenomapping delivers incremental value to LVEF and NYHA for identification of high-risk NICM patients. These findings support value from standardized, point-of-service data integration for the delivery of phenomics-driven personalized care.
43056272: Yttrium 90 transarterial radioembolization has evolved from a palliative lobar therapy for advanced liver malignancies into a versatile potentially curative treatment across hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) stages, intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA), and liver metastases. Central to this evolution is the shift from empirical population-based activity prescriptions to personalized dosimetry, tailoring administered activity to each patient's anatomy, tumor biology, treatment intent, and microsphere distribution to optimize tumor absorbed dose while constraining normal tissue exposure. Prospective studies have demonstrated that personalized dosimetry significantly improves tumor response and overall survival compared with conventional dosing. Despite this evidence, clinical adoption remains inconsistent. In this review, the authors aim to address that gap by providing a practical intent-based framework for implementation. They present dosimetric principles, activity prescription methods, and dose-response evidence across HCC, iCCA, and liver metastases, with practical recommendations organized by treatment intent. Treatment intent, whether curative or palliative, is the primary determinant of dosimetric strategy, guiding selection of the dosimetry model, target dose, and normal liver dose constraints. The authors review pretreatment planning work flows and posttreatment verification and present a practical decision algorithm integrating clinical intent, imaging, and dosimetry modeling. ©RSNA, 2026 See the invited commentary by Malone and Toskich in this issue.
43056276: Female infertility affects approximately 15% of couples of reproductive age, with tubal disease responsible for up to one-third of cases. Therefore, accurate, minimally invasive evaluation of tubal patency is a cornerstone of fertility assessment. Among the available modalities, including hysterosalpingography (HSG), MR HSG, and laparoscopic chromopertubation, hysterosalpingo-contrast sonography (HyCoSy) has gained prominence as a valuable alternative to conventional methods due to its safety, accessibility, and diagnostic reliability. Recent advances in contrast-enhanced US involving the use of second-generation microbubble agents combined with three-dimensional (3D) and four-dimensional (4D) acquisition technologies have significantly improved the performance of HyCoSy. These developments enable real-time volumetric visualization of the uterine cavity and fallopian tubes, enhancing both anatomic delineation and functional assessment of tubal patency. In addition, combined 3D and 4D (3D-4D) HyCoSy enables complementary evaluation of uterine morphology, adnexal structures, and associated infertility-related disorders such as endometriosis and adhesions, facilitating a comprehensive "one-stop" reproductive imaging approach. This article is intended to serve as a practical guide to performing 3D-4D HyCoSy with microbubble contrast agents, including preparation, technical parameters, and findings interpretation. In addition, the authors compare HyCoSy with conventional techniques, review characteristic imaging patterns of tubal patency and occlusion, and discuss potential pitfalls and preventive strategies. As an advanced US technology combined with a dynamic functional perspective, 3D-4D HyCoSy represents a powerful, cost-effective, and patient-friendly tool for integrated fertility evaluation in modern radiology practices.
43056402: Mosquito-borne diseases (MBDs) remain a major global health challenge. Vector surveillance, pathogen detection, and clinical diagnosis are central to control efforts but are limited by labor-intensive workflows and shortages of trained personnel. Computer vision (CV) offers opportunities for scalable automation throughout the MBD management pipeline. We aimed to systematically characterize the applications of computer vision in mosquito-borne diseases research, summarize methodological developments, and identify opportunities and barriers to translating these advances into public health practice. We conducted a systematic review in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines, searching PubMed, Scopus, and IEEE Xplore for studies published between January 1, 2010, and December 31, 2025, that applied computer vision to any aspect of MBD research or control. A total of 1,521 records were screened, and 650 studies met the inclusion criteria. Studies were categorized by computer vision application area, data types, algorithmic approaches, and data acquisition methods. Descriptive quantitative analysis and qualitative thematic synthesis were performed. The use of computer vision in MBD research increased significantly over the review period. Most studies focused on diagnostic applications, particularly Plasmodium detection in malaria microscopy. More recent work incorporated deep learning models for mosquito species classification, UAV- and satellite-based habitat mapping, and smartphone-based non-invasive diagnostic imaging. Emerging areas included 3D mosquito behavioral analysis and Internet of Things-enabled surveillance. Algorithmic approaches evolved from traditional image processing to convolutional neural networks, You Only Look Once (YOLO)-based object detectors, and transformer architectures. However, most models were developed using small, geographically-limited datasets, lacked external or prospective validation, and were rarely evaluated in operational settings, limiting their translational readiness.
43056600:
BACKGROUND: Alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) is a major cause of liver-related morbidity and mortality, and abstinence is fundamental for treatment. Liver stiffness measurement (LSM) using vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE) is commonly used to assess hepatic fibrosis and inflammation. While studies suggest LSM decreases after alcohol cessation, the magnitude and timing of these changes are poorly understood. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated liver stiffness changes after alcohol cessation.
METHODS: Medline, EMBASE, and Cochrane databases were searched from 1996 to 2024 for paired VCTE assessments in adults who underwent alcohol cessation and reported abstinence or relapse. Absolute mean kPa changes were back-transformed estimates from pooled effect sizes and standard deviations. ROBINS-I assessed risk of bias.
RESULTS: A total of 6620 articles were reviewed; 75 underwent full-text review, and 11 studies involving 1557 patients were included. In abstinent patients, a mean absolute LSM change was identified to be -1.95 kPa at 7 days, -2.30 kPa at 30 days, and -2.76 kPa after 56 days. The pooled standardized effect size was -0.13 SD units (95% CI -0.20 to -0.07). LSM reduction was significant within 7 days of abstinence (-0.21 SD units; 95% CI -0.38 to -0.05) but not at later follow-up (-0.11 SD units; 95% CI -0.24 to 0.03). In relapse patients, mean absolute LSM change was +0.86 kPa at 30 days and +0.40 kPa after 56 days; pooled standardized effect size was +0.18 SD units (95% CI +0.02 to +0.33).
CONCLUSIONS: VCTE detected short-term, directionally opposite LSM changes with alcohol cessation or relapse. These changes are consistent with alcohol-associated inflammatory liver injury, while its correlation with histologic fibrosis is uncertain, necessitating further evaluation with paired VCTE and histology during abstinence.
43056691:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Epithelial barrier alterations contribute to the pathogenesis and progression of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Barrier healing may predict long-term outcomes more accurately than endoscopic, histological or even transmural healing, and persistent epithelial abnormalities despite mucosal healing may underlie residual symptoms. Reliable tools are therefore needed to determine whether this therapeutic goal has been achieved and to support the development of barrier-directed therapies. We systematically reviewed the methods available to assess intestinal epithelial barrier structure and function in IBD.
METHODS: MEDLINE and Scopus were searched to July 25, 2025, for studies assessing epithelial barrier structure or function in patients with IBD. Animal, in vitro and ex vivo studies, and those without a clearly described assessment method, were excluded. Two reviewers independently screened records and extracted data on tools, thresholds, and associations with disease activity, treatment and outcomes.
RESULTS: Of 12 307 records screened, 124 studies were included: 73 evaluated permeability probes, 30 endogenous biomarkers and 25 invasive techniques, with four studies assessing both permeability probes and endogenous biomarkers. Probe-based testing relies on urinary recovery of orally administered sugars, polyethylene glycols, iohexol, radiolabelled compounds or fluorophores. Biomarkers reflect epithelial injury, microbial translocation, or the host response to it. Invasive techniques allow real-time, segment-specific assessment, principally probe-based confocal laser endomicroscopy, whose scores predict relapse and major adverse outcomes; endocytoscopy combined with multispectral spatial imaging is an emerging alternative.
CONCLUSIONS: A broad range of functional, molecular and morphological tools is now available. Validating thresholds, standardising outcome measures and better defining barrier healing are the next steps before it can become a therapeutic target.
43056705:
BACKGROUND: Glioblastoma (GBM) and brain metastasis (BM) are the most common malignant intracranial tumors in adults. Noninvasive differentiation between them remains challenging, as they frequently share similar imaging features. Although radiomics-based machine learning (ML) models show promise, systematic evidence of their performance remains limited.
OBJECTIVE: We aimed to systematically estimate the diagnostic performance of radiomics-based ML models in differentiating GBM from BM and to explore multiclass classification involving primary central nervous system lymphoma (PCNSL), thereby assessing their potential for clinical use.
METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library databases from inception to January 22, 2026, for studies reporting the diagnostic performance of radiomics-based ML models for differentiating GBM from BM. Multiclass studies involving PCNSL were also retained. Methodological quality was appraised via the Radiomics Quality Score 2.0. Binary diagnostic accuracy was pooled using a bivariate random-effects model, stratified by internal and independent external validation. Multiclass sensitivities and specificities were pooled using separate joint generalized linear mixed models. Physician assessments were evaluated as an exploratory benchmark.
RESULTS: A total of 39 studies (31 binary and 8 multiclass), involving 11,558 patients, were included. For binary classification, pooled sensitivity and specificity were 88.9% (95% CI 84.1%-92.4%) and 83.0% (95% CI 76.8%-87.9%) in internal validation, and 83.8% (95% CI 77.4%-88.7%) and 80.7% (95% CI 71.1%-87.7%) in external validation, respectively. In multiclass analyses, pooled sensitivity was 84.4% (95% CI 72.4%-91.8%) for GBM, 70.6% (95% CI 54.4%-82.8%) for BM, and 75.0% (95% CI 62.7%-84.3%) for PCNSL, with corresponding specificities of 82.5% (95% CI 70.1%-90.4%), 88.8% (95% CI 81.9%-93.3%), and 94.4% (95% CI 88.4%-97.4%), respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: Radiomics-based ML models could distinguish between GBM and BM in the included cohorts. However, due to methodological limitations and scarce evidence, their generalizability and clinical utility remain unclear. Further multicenter prospective studies should conduct independent external validation in consecutive patients.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD420261295269; https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261295269.
43056714:
BACKGROUND: Retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) is one of the major causes of preventable blindness in premature infants. Early screening, accurate diagnosis, and severity classification are crucial for reducing irreversible visual impairment. Recently, image-based AI models have been widely applied to ROP screening, diagnosis, and severity classification. However, the model architecture, data source, validation method, and diagnostic task vary across studies. Consequently, the overall diagnostic efficiency and clinical utility of deep learning (DL) remain to be systematically assessed.
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of image-based AI for ROP by disease type, validation method, model type, and use of transfer learning (TL).
METHODS: We performed a systematic search across Web of Science, Embase, IEEE Xplore, PubMed, and Cochrane Library as of October 12, 2026, to identify studies investigating image-based AI for ROP detection or clinical subtype classification. The risk of bias (RoB) of included studies was assessed using the Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies 2 (QUADAS-2) tool. Sensitivity and specificity were pooled using bivariate mixed-effects models, with analyses stratified by diagnostic task and validation method.
RESULTS: Sixty-two studies contributed 185 contingency tables. For normal vs ROP, pooled sensitivity was 0.94 (95% CI 0.92-0.96) and specificity was 0.96 (95% CI 0.94-0.97). For normal vs treatment-requiring ROP (TR-ROP), sensitivity was 0.97 (95% CI 0.91-0.99) and specificity was 0.74 (95% CI 0.66-0.80). For mild vs severe ROP, specificity was 0.78 (95% CI 0.59-0.90). In external validation, pooled sensitivity and specificity were 0.95 (95% CI 0.89-0.97) and 0.83 (95% CI 0.72-0.90), respectively, while the corresponding estimates were 0.95 (95% CI 0.93-0.96) and 0.97 (95% CI 0.96-0.98) in internal validation. For DL and conventional machine learning (ML) models, pooled sensitivity was 0.95 (95% CI 0.94-0.96) and 0.96 (95% CI 0.90-0.98), respectively, while specificity was 0.96 (95% CI 0.95-0.97) and 0.91 (95% CI 0.84-0.94), respectively. With and without TL, pooled sensitivity was 0.95 (95% CI 0.94-0.96) and 0.95 (95% CI 0.92-0.97), respectively, while specificity was 0.97 (95% CI 0.96-0.98) and 0.92 (95% CI 0.86-0.95), respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: Image-based AI may have high sensitivity for ROP assessment, but its specificity is lower for identifying TR-ROP and in the external-validation subgroup. Given the predominance of retrospective studies, heterogeneity, and limited external validation, current evidence supports AI as an adjunct to screening and referral, with clinicians retaining responsibility for diagnostic and treatment decisions. Prospective, multicenter external validation is needed.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD420261418502; https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261418502.
43057246:
BACKGROUND: The European Society of Gastrointestinal Endoscopy (ESGE) published its first Position Statement on digestive conditions that do not require endoscopy in 2020. Since then, multiple ESGE guidelines have expanded recommendations that promote appropriate indications, de-escalation of surveillance, and evidence-based avoidance of low value procedures. In parallel, avoiding unnecessary endoscopy has emerged as a major strategy for reducing the environmental burden of gastrointestinal endoscopy. This updated Position Statement consolidates such ESGE recommendations into a practical framework defining when endoscopy is not required.
METHODS: This Position Statement is based exclusively on recommendations developed or endorsed by ESGE. Recommendations from ESGE Guidelines and Position Statements published in Endoscopy were systematically reviewed and synthesized. Positive recommendations advocating alternative management strategies were reformulated, where appropriate, into explicit "do not perform endoscopy" statements without modifying the underlying evidence or recommendation strength. The resulting document provides a clinically oriented synthesis rather than new guideline recommendations.
RESULTS: Recommendations covering upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, colonoscopy, endoscopic ultrasound, endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography, capsule endoscopy, and therapeutic endoscopy were identified. Across these modalities, four overarching scenarios emerged in which endoscopy is not required: screening when endoscopy does not meaningfully prevent disease incidence or improve relevant outcomes; surveillance when repeat endoscopy provides no additional benefit beyond an adequate index examination or when expected benefit is limited by age, co-morbidity, or life expectancy; diagnostic endoscopy when validated noninvasive strategies provide sufficient information or when endoscopic findings are unlikely to change management; and therapeutic endoscopy when intervention does not improve clinically relevant outcomes compared with conservative or alternative management. Additional principles include avoiding redundant investigations and unnecessary repetition of adequately performed procedures. Together, these recommendations provide a framework for reducing low value endoscopy while limiting patient burden, healthcare resource use, and environmental impact.
CONCLUSIONS: An appropriate indication is the cornerstone of high quality endoscopy and the primary driver of sustainable endoscopic practice. Endoscopy should be avoided when it does not provide meaningful additional benefit in screening, surveillance, diagnosis, or therapy. Applying these principles can improve patient safety, optimize healthcare resources, and reduce the environmental footprint of endoscopy. This updated ESGE Position Statement provides an evidence-based framework for high value, patient-centered, and sustainable endoscopic practice.
43057630:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the outcomes of thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) for type B aortic dissection (TBAD) with concurrent retrograde intramural hematoma (RTIMH) involving the aortic arch, with or without further extension into the ascending aorta.
METHODS: A systematic search of MEDLINE and EMBASE to June 2026 was performed. Studies reporting TEVAR outcomes in adults with TBAD-associated RTIMH, defined as a primary intimal tear at or distal to Ishimaru zone 3 with retrograde intramural hematoma extension into zones 0-2, were included. Co-primary outcomes were technical success and post-TEVAR retrograde type A aortic dissection (RTAD), defined as the new development of a communicating dissection flap within the previously non-flow intramural hematoma. Secondary outcomes included early mortality, stroke, type I endoleak, reintervention, survival, aortic rupture, and aortic remodelling. Proportions were pooled using single-arm random-effects meta-analysis following logit transformation; remaining findings were synthesised narratively.
RESULTS: Seven retrospective cohort studies comprising 342 patients, all from mainland Chinese institutions, were included. The pooled technical success rate was 99% (95% CI 97-99%; I2 = 0.0%). The pooled post-TEVAR RTAD rate was 3% (95% CI 1-8%; I2 = 7.6%), with all events preceded by proximal stent-graft-induced new entry. Secondary outcomes included pooled 30-day mortality of 2% (95% CI 1-4%; I2 = 0.0%), aortic rupture of 2% (95% CI 1-4%; I2 = 0.0%), reintervention of 7% (95% CI 5-11%; I2 = 0.0%), late all-cause mortality of 4% (95% CI 3-6%; I2 = 0.0%), and type I endoleak of 4% (95% CI 2-7%; I2 = 0.0%). All studies reporting pre- and post-procedural imaging demonstrated reductions in ascending aortic diameter and hematoma thickness, with complete ascending IMH resolution in 52.5-100% of patients.
CONCLUSIONS: TEVAR is technically feasible with low perioperative mortality and consistent aortic remodelling in selected patients with TBAD-associated RTIMH. Post-TEVAR RTAD and type I endoleak represent the principal procedure-specific risks. Contemporary evidence remains limited to small retrospective cohorts from a single geographic region.
43057653:
INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Metabolic dysfunction- and alcohol-associated liver disease (MetALD) describes steatotic liver disease in individuals with cardiometabolic dysfunction and alcohol consumption. As MetALD-specific evidence remains limited, practical guidance is needed for diagnosis, fibrosis assessment, alcohol use disorder management, cardiometabolic treatment, and transplant evaluation.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a two-round modified Delphi study with an international multidisciplinary expert panel. Statements were developed after a targeted literature review and organized into four domains: diagnosis and disease stratification, alcohol use assessment and alcohol use disorder treatment, metabolic and cardiometabolic management, and liver transplant assessment. Statements were rated on a five-point Likert scale. Consensus agreement was predefined as a median score ≥4, ≥70% of ratings in the 4-5 range, and interquartile range ≤1.
RESULTS: All 30 experts from 10 countries participated in round 1, and 29 (97%) in round 2. In round 1, 31 of 33 statements met agreement criteria; two were revised and re-evaluated. After round 2, consensus was achieved for all statements. The panel recognized MetALD as having dual metabolic and alcohol-related drivers and endorsed systematic cardiometabolic assessment, longitudinal quantification of alcohol intake, selective use of direct alcohol biomarkers, and stepwise noninvasive fibrosis risk stratification. Recommended care integrates individualized goals for alcohol reduction or abstinence, evidence-based alcohol use disorder treatment, structured lifestyle intervention, weight loss, physical activity, and optimization of diabetes, dyslipidemia, and hypertension. Transplant assessment should be individualized and multidisciplinary.
CONCLUSIONS: This consensus provides practical recommendations for integrated MetALD care and identifies priorities for future clinical research and external validation.
43058387:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Superpulsed thulium fiber laser (sTFL) and Lumenis MOSES pulse-modulated holmium: yttrium-aluminum-garnet (Ho: YAG) represent contemporary standards for retrograde intrarenal surgery (RIRS), operating through distinct photothermal and pulse-shape modulation mechanisms. Previous meta-analyses comparing these modalities have yielded conflicting conclusions largely due to pooling heterogeneous, non-modulated Ho: YAG generations and diverse surgical procedures. This study aims to systematically review and meta-analyze existing evidence evaluating sTFL exclusively against MOSES Ho: YAG regarding stone-free rates, operative efficiency, and safety in adults undergoing RIRS for stones ≤ 20 mm.
RECENT FINDINGS: Of 1,290 records identified across five databases (PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, and Europe PMC) through August 2026 (PROSPERO: CRD420261492557), 7 studies (3 randomized controlled trials and 4 comparative cohorts; 1,278 matched patients) met the inclusion criteria for the systematic review and meta-analysis. Meta-analysis showed that the sTFL cohort demonstrated a significantly superior absolute 0-mm stone-free rate compared to MOSES Ho: YAG (pooled RR 1.09, 95% CI 1.02-1.17, p = 0.014, I²=0.0%). However, clinically insignificant residual fragment (CIRF, ≤ 2-4 mm) rates were statistically equivalent between modalities both overall (pooled RR 1.06, 95% CI 0.93-1.21, I²=87.1%) and following the resolution of registry-driven heterogeneity (pooled RR 1.02, 95% CI 0.96-1.08, p = 0.59, I²=29.2%). Operative and lasing times were comparable between platforms. Both lasers exhibited equivalent overall complications (pooled RR 1.44, 95% CI 0.92-2.26) and severe adverse events (Clavien-Dindo ≥ III: RD 0.01, 95% CI - 0.00 to 0.02). Subgroup analyses revealed that elevated complication rates with sTFL were isolated to non-randomized, pure intrarenal cohorts (pooled RR 1.83, 95% CI 1.30-2.57) and follow-up ≥ 3 months (pooled RR 1.84, 95% CI 1.30-2.61), reflecting procedural confounders-such as ureteral access sheath underutilization-rather than inherent laser physics. Most studies were rated as having a high or serious risk of bias, primarily because of confounding and outcome measurement concerns. Leave-one-out sensitivity analyses supported the robustness of the findings. This systematic review highlights that while sTFL achieves superior absolute stone clearance (0 mm), both sTFL and MOSES Ho: YAG yield equivalent CIRF rates, operative efficiency, and safety profiles under standardized operative conditions. Relying on institutional availability and enforcing strict intrarenal pressure management may be valuable strategies for guiding clinical laser application.
43058542:
BACKGROUND: Whether intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) before endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) benefits patients with acute ischemic stroke and large-vessel occlusion remains uncertain.
METHODS: We pooled randomized trials comparing IVT + EVT with EVT alone in eligible adults presenting within 4.5 h. Outcomes were summarized as risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) using random-effects models. Strict modified Rankin Scale (mRS) 0-2 was also assessed using risk difference (RD), number needed to treat for benefit (NNTB), and post hoc Bayesian methods.
RESULTS: Seven trials included 2,884 patients. Strict mRS 0-2 occurred in 741/1,448 IVT + EVT and 689/1,436 EVT-alone participants (RR, 1.07; 95% CI, 0.99-1.15). The pooled RD was + 3.08% points (95% CI, - 0.90 to + 7.05; P=.129), equivalent to 31 additional favorable outcomes per 1,000 (95% CI, 9 fewer to 71 additional) and a point-estimate NNTB of 33. The Bayesian median RD was + 2.93 points (95% credible interval [CrI], - 2.24 to + 7.72); the probabilities of any benefit and benefit of at least 1.3 points were 88.8% and 75.8%. Mortality was similar between groups (RR, 0.98; 95% CI, 0.84-1.16). Trial-defined primary symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH) occurred in 81/1,435 versus 68/1,432 participants (RR, 1.19; 95% CI, 0.87-1.63); the posterior probability of an absolute excess of at least 1 point was 22.6%.
CONCLUSIONS: Randomized evidence did not demonstrate superiority of IVT + EVT over EVT alone. Clinically meaningful functional benefit remains plausible, whereas sICH harm remains uncertain. These findings do not establish equivalence.
43058597:
BACKGROUND: Drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS) syndrome is a rare but potentially life-threatening drug reaction characterized by cutaneous eruption, hematologic abnormalities and other multiorgan involvement. This condition generally develops after the use of anticonvulsants, allopurinol, or sulfonamides. Despite amoxicillin being commonly prescribed, it is an uncommon cause of DRESS syndrome, and respiratory involvement remains infrequently reported. We present, to our knowledge, the first reported Ethiopian case of probable amoxicillin-associated DRESS syndrome with respiratory manifestations, together with a systematic review of published cases to define its clinical characteristics, diagnostic challenges, and therapeutic outcomes in a resource-limited clinical setting.
METHODS: We performed a systematic review according to the PRISMA standards through PubMed/MEDLINE, Google Scholar, Embase, and Scopus databases up to March 2026. From the literature search, 63 articles were initially identified. Eligibility criteria include: (1) presence of case reports or case series involving DRESS syndrome, (2) amoxicillin as one of the causative drugs, (3) diagnosis supported by RegiSCAR criteria or its equivalent validated tool, and (4) English-language articles only. The quality assessment of the selected case reports was done using the Critical Appraisal Checklist for Case Reports from the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI). we describe an index case of DRESS due to amoxicillin according to the CARE guidelines.
RESULTS: After JBI quality assessment of 13 eligible studies, 11 published case reports were included, plus our index case, yielding a total of 12 cases for descriptive synthesis. Our index case involved a 23-year-old female patient of Ethiopian descent who presented with DRESS syndrome on day 7 of amoxicillin monotherapy for tonsillopharyngitis, presenting with morbilliform rash (≈ 72% BSA), fever (38.5 °C), facial and periorbital edema, tachypnea, tachycardia, hypoxemia (oxygen saturation of 84-86%) and bilateral crackles on chest auscultation. The patient's laboratory tests revealed eosinophilia (850/µl) and mild transaminitis. Chest x-ray revealed bilateral perihilar and lower lobe zone patchy airspace opacities. The RegiSCAR score was 5 (probable DRESS). Among 12 pooled cases, the latency period was between 3 days and 5 weeks; isolated amoxicillin-induced DRESS was seen in 5 cases (41.7%); pulmonary involvement was found in 3 cases (25.0%); and all have favorable outcomes.
CONCLUSION: A high index of suspicion is needed for DRESS syndrome for patients presented with fever, rash, and other systemic symptoms following widely used antibiotics like amoxicillin. This study demonstrates that amoxicillin monotherapy can trigger DRESS and clinically significant respiratory involvement can occur independent of hepatic or renal dysfunction. Early recognition, prompt drug discontinuation, systemic corticosteroid therapy, and enhanced pharmacovigilance are essential to improve patient safety and outcomes.
43059045: Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) has emerged as a promising approach to improving glycemic management in hospitalized individuals. Evidence from inpatient studies supports the benefits of CGM in monitoring glucose trends and improving the detection of otherwise unrecognized hypoglycemic and hyperglycemic episodes. Improvements in glycemic control have also been reported with CGM-integrated management, although these benefits may depend on structured insulin titration protocols, confirmatory point-of-care testing, dedicated glycemic management teams, and institutional workflows. However, the inpatient setting presents unique challenges, including hemodynamic instability, surgical interventions, radiologic procedures, and potential drug interference, which may affect CGM accuracy and safety. Systematic guidelines for implementing CGM in inpatient care remain scarce internationally, highlighting the need for structured evidence synthesis and practical recommendations. In this position statement, the Korean Diabetes Association Digital Health Committee reviews current evidence on the efficacy and accuracy of CGM in inpatient settings and highlights key considerations for its safe implementation, including target populations, hybrid monitoring strategies, and procedural safety. We propose an operational framework for inpatient CGM use, aiming to establish a foundation for its systematic adoption and to inform future institutional and regulatory frameworks.
43059107:
BACKGROUND: Microwave ablation (MWA) and liver resection (LR) are both established treatment options for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but comparative evidence on survival outcomes and safety for gallbladder-adjacent HCC remains lacking.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Between January 2006 and December 2024, 1,242 patients with primary HCC from five tertiary hospitals who underwent MWA or LR as first-line therapy were identified. Primary endpoints were overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS); secondary endpoints were complications, operative time, hospital stay, and costs. Propensity score overlap weighting balanced baseline characteristics, with propensity score matching as a sensitivity analysis. Survival was assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis, log-rank test, and multivariable Cox regression with subgroup analyses.
RESULTS: A total of 254 patients were included, with 66 in the MWA group and 188 in the LR group. After overlap weighting, no significant difference in OS was observed (p = 0.315), whereas LR showed significantly better PFS (p = 0.048). Multivariable analysis revealed that treatment modality was not an independent predictor of OS (p = 0.310) or PFS (p = 0.096). Subgroup analysis showed no significant treatment interaction for OS (p = 0.193) or PFS (p = 0.986). MWA demonstrated comparable complications, with shorter operative time, shorter hospital stay, and lower cost than LR (all p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: In conclusion, for gallbladder-adjacent HCC, MWA achieved OS and a safety profile comparable to LR, while offering shorter operative time, shorter hospital stay, and lower cost, suggesting MWA may be an effective and less invasive alternative in selected patients.
43059205:
BACKGROUND: Given the similarity of risk factors and pathophysiological mechanisms, suspecting HFpEF in COPD is challenging because of overlapping clinical features. Echocardiographic assessment of diastolic dysfunction (DD) may help identify patients with abnormal left ventricular filling who warrant further cardiac evaluation, although DD is not equivalent to a clinical diagnosis of HFpEF. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to estimate the pooled prevalence of DD among patients with COPD.
METHODS: PubMed, EMBASE, Scopus, and Cochrane databases were searched from inception to February 5, 2026. Studies reporting the prevalence of DD in COPD using any echocardiographic criteria were included. A random-effects meta-analysis was performed using restricted maximum-likelihood estimation. Heterogeneity was assessed with Cochran's Q, I2, and τ2. Subgroup, sensitivity, and meta-regression analyses were conducted. Study quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa scale, and the certainty of the evidence was evaluated using the GRADE approach.
RESULTS: Forty-eight studies comprising 6845 patients were included. The pooled prevalence of echocardiographic findings consistent with DD was 47% (95% CI: 39%-56%), with substantial between-study heterogeneity (I2 = 95.5%; 95% prediction interval, 7%-91%). Prevalence increased across GOLD stages, from 30% (95% CI: 16%-50%) in Stage I to 38% (22%-57%) in Stage II, 58% (39%-75%) in Stage III and 72% (56%-84%) in Stage IV. These stage-specific estimates were interpreted descriptively because several studies contributed data to multiple stages. Sensitivity analyses yielded pooled prevalences of 54% after excluding low-quality studies and 62% after excluding studies with fewer than 50 participants. Multivariable meta-regression explained only a modest proportion of between-study variance. No statistically significant asymmetry was detected by Egger's test, although its interpretation for prevalence outcomes is limited. Overall certainty of evidence was low.
CONCLUSIONS: Echocardiographic findings consistent with DD are frequently reported among patients with COPD, but the absolute pooled prevalence is uncertain because of substantial heterogeneity, variation in echocardiographic definitions and predominantly low study quality. A severity-associated increase across GOLD stages was observed but should be interpreted descriptively because of nonindependent subgroup data. Further prospective studies using standardized echocardiographic definitions and comprehensive cardiopulmonary phenotyping are required.
43061368: Preoperative accurate assessment of cervical lymph node metastasis (LNM) in papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) is essential for optimal surgical planning and reducing recurrence risk. Conventional ultrasound has limited sensitivity, and although fine-needle aspiration cytology (FNAC) demonstrates high specificity (up to 97%), its diagnostic performance is compromised by sampling errors, cystic degeneration, and micrometastases, resulting in a false-negative rate of 10%-30%. Thyroglobulin measurement in fine-needle aspiration washout fluid (FNA-Tg), with its tissue-specific biochemical advantages and reported sensitivity of up to 92%, serves as an ideal complementary modality. This review systematically consolidates the theoretical foundations and evidence regarding the combination of FNAC and FNA-Tg for cervical LNM in PTC. These two modalities are orthogonal in their diagnostic dimensions-FNAC provides cytomorphological evidence, whereas FNA-Tg offers biochemical evidence of tissue origin-forming the basis for the incremental value of the combined strategy. Meta-analyses demonstrate a pooled sensitivity of 94% (95% CI: 91%-96%) and a negative predictive value exceeding 95%, with benefits particularly pronounced in suspicious/indeterminate cytology, micro-lymph nodes (<5 mm), and TgAb-positive patients. However, a negative combined FNAC/FNA-Tg result should be interpreted in the context of ultrasound features and clinical risk, because it reduces but does not definitively exclude the possibility of micrometastasis, particularly in persistently suspicious or small lymph nodes. However, translation to routine practice faces challenges, including lack of standardized FNA-Tg assays, inconsistent cut-off values, and absence of external quality assessment programs. Future efforts should prioritize multicenter collaboration and prospective validation under a unified framework, establishing a cut-off value reference system, and exploring artificial intelligence-based multimodal fusion models. The core issue has evolved from "whether there is an incremental benefit" to "how to standardize its application." Standardization initiatives and high-quality prospective studies remain critical for future breakthroughs.
43062045:
BACKGROUND: Radical resection combined with intestinal autotransplantation (RRCIA) has emerged as a potential curative option for highly selected patients with locally advanced pancreatic cancer (LAPC) and extensive mesenteric vascular involvement. This project aimed to develop expert consensus recommendations on indications, surgical strategies, perioperative management, and long-term care of RRCIA in patients with LAPC.
METHODS: An international multidisciplinary panel of experts in pancreatic surgery, transplant surgery, medical oncology, radiation oncology, radiology, critical care, and perioperative care was convened. A modified Delphi process was used to develop consensus recommendations. The survey comprised six domains with a total of 20 questions covering patient selection, neoadjuvant therapy, surgical strategies, perioperative management, adjuvant therapy, and follow-up. Consensus was predefined as ≥80% agreement.
RESULTS: Twenty consensus statements were developed. The quality of evidence was low for 17 statements and moderate for 3. Six recommendations were strong and 14 conditional. RRCIA was recommended only for highly selected patients at experienced high-volume centres following adequate neoadjuvant therapy and multidisciplinary evaluation. Surgical strategies should be individualized according to tumour location and vascular involvement. No definitive minimum residual bowel length was established, and preservation of well-perfused bowel and the ileocaecal valve was emphasized. Postoperative management should be tailored, including anticoagulation, nutritional support, selective implementation of enhanced recovery principles, adjuvant therapy, and structured long-term follow-up.
CONCLUSION: This consensus provides the first international framework to guide the application of RRCIA for LAPC, emphasizing its use in carefully selected patients treated at experienced centres with multidisciplinary expertise.
43062145: Craniospinal irradiation (CSI) plus chemotherapy is standard for pediatric standard/average-risk medulloblastoma, but the safest de-escalated dose remains uncertain. We systematically reviewed four databases and meta-analyzed 5-year disease-control survival (DCS) and overall survival (OS). Fifteen studies were included. Modern 18/23.4-Gy CSI yielded 79.6% DCS and 85.3% OS. At 23.4 Gy, corresponding estimates were 81.0% and 86.7%; at 18 Gy, 71.3% and 79.1%. Current evidence supports 23.4 Gy as the most reproducible platform, whereas routine 18-Gy use is not supported outside prospectively selected, molecularly favorable populations.
43062379:
DESCRIPTION: The purpose of this American Gastroenterological Association (AGA) Institute Clinical Practice Update (CPU) is to review the available evidence and best practices regarding the use of liver biopsy in liver diseases, evaluation of abnormal liver tests, and liver masses.
METHODS: This CPU was commissioned and approved by the AGA Institute CPU Committee and the AGA Governing Board to provide timely guidance on a topic of high clinical importance to the AGA membership. This CPU underwent internal peer review by the CPU Committee and external peer review through the standard procedures of Clinical Gastroenterology and Hepatology. This expert commentary incorporates important as well as recently published data in this field and reflects the experiences of the authors.
43062386: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) begins early in life, driven in large part by cumulative exposure to low-density lipoprotein cholesterol and other atherogenic lipoproteins. Contemporary evidence from epidemiologic cohorts, genetic studies, imaging studies, and lipid-lowering trials supports a paradigm of earlier identification and more sustained treatment of individuals at increased ASCVD risk. This American College of Cardiology Scientific Statement reviews the rationale for early adoption of lipid-lowering strategies, with emphasis on lifetime lipid burden, inherited and acquired risk enhancers, and the role of subclinical atherosclerosis assessment. Available clinical trial data suggest that greater absolute low-density lipoprotein cholesterol reduction and longer treatment duration can reduce ASCVD events, even though direct evidence remains limited in younger populations at low short-term risk. Atherosclerosis detected by imaging may identify individuals whose ASCVD risk is underestimated by traditional calculators, but optimal strategies for screening, treatment thresholds, safety, adherence, cost-effectiveness, and value require further study. Clinicians should integrate estimated short- and long-term risk, lipid burden, risk enhancers, imaging findings when appropriate, and patient preferences to guide individualized, shared decision making to reduce lifetime ASCVD risk.
43062460: Shoulder overuse injuries are highly prevalent among athletes participating in overhead sports such as baseball, tennis, swimming, and volleyball, where repetitive high-velocity loading imposes unique biomechanical demands on the glenohumeral complex. These injuries span a broad spectrum, including rotator cuff tears, subacromial/subdeltoid impingement, superior labrum anterior-to-posterior (SLAP) lesions, long head of the biceps tendinopathy, glenohumeral instability, internal impingement, glenohumeral internal rotation deficit (GIRD), and Little League shoulder. Accurate diagnosis requires an understanding of sport-specific biomechanics, particularly the extreme forces generated during the late cocking and early acceleration phases of throwing, which produce characteristic injury patterns such as posterosuperior partial articular-sided rotator cuff tears and type II SLAP lesions via the peel-back mechanism. Imaging plays a central role in diagnosis and management. Radiographs remain the initial study for evaluating osseous anatomy and acromial morphology. MRI is the principal modality for soft-tissue assessment, while MR arthrography offers superior sensitivity for intra-articular pathology, including labral and partial articular-sided rotator cuff tears. Musculoskeletal ultrasound provides dynamic, cost-effective evaluation of tendons and bursae, and 3D CT or zero-time echo (ZTE) MRI is essential for quantifying glenoid bone loss in the setting of instability. Because many imaging findings are present in asymptomatic athletes, careful clinical correlation is essential. This review summarizes the imaging features, diagnostic pearls, and limitations of current modalities for shoulder overuse injuries in overhead athletes.
43062466:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the robust visualization of photon-counting CT (PCCT) for right adrenal vein (RAV) across body mass index (BMI) groups with respect to virtual monochromatic imaging (VMI) energy levels and reconstruction kernels.
METHODS: A total of 302 patients who underwent contrast-enhanced abdominal PCCT were enrolled and stratified into non-obese, overweight, and obese groups based on Asian-specific BMI criteria. VMIs were reconstructed at 40, 55, and 70 keV with three vascular‑specific reconstruction kernels (Bv40, Bv48, Bv60). For quantitative evaluation, two radiologists assessed image metrics, including CT attenuation, image noise (standard deviation [SD]), signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR). Separately, another pair of radiologists independently evaluated qualitative image quality (encompassing both overall image quality and RAV visualization quality) using a 5-point Likert scale.
RESULTS: Quantitative evaluation showed that VMI energy level and reconstruction kernel were associated with changes in quantitative image quality metrics, with significant interactions between energy level and reconstruction kernel for all four quantitative metrics (all P < 0.001). Exploratory analyses suggested BMI-related interactions in RAV attenuation and subjective visualization quality. Lower keV increased RAV CT attenuation and CNR, with the highest values at 40 keV across all BMI groups. Qualitative evaluation demonstrated a 100% RAV visualization rate across all reconstruction settings and BMI groups, with median visualization scores ranging from 3.0 to 5.0. Inter-reader agreement was excellent (weighted κ = 0.82).
CONCLUSION: PCCT provides favorable RAV visualization across the investigated BMI groups, with low-keV imaging and smoother reconstruction kernels associated with improved visualization quality.
43062471:
Although inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) may lead to an increased risk of cardiovascular disease, evidence regarding cardiovascular and lipid parameters in childhood is limited. We compared vascular markers, blood pressure and lipid levels between patients with pediatric or childhood-onset IBD and controls. This study was performed according to the Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions and adhered to PRISMA guidelines. A search of major databases (MEDLINE/PubMed, Scopus and Cochrane Library) was conducted from inception until April 24, 2025 (CRD420251039588). The study quality was evaluated using the modified Newcastle-Ottawa Scale; statistical analysis was conducted using R software. Reactive hyperemia index (RHI) was lower in three studies, involving 109 participants (MD - 0.25, 95% CI - 0.48 to - 0.02; p = 0.03). No statistically significant difference in carotid intima-media thickness (cIMT) was detected based on six studies. Primary systolic blood pressure (SBP) pooling across ten studies, was also not statistically significant (MD 0.84 mmHg, 95% CI - 0.67 to 2.35; p = 0.28). The exclusion of one influential study resulted in a small difference in SBP (MD 1.89 mmHg, 95% CI 1.17 to 2.61). Primary analyses detected no statistically significant differences in diastolic blood pressure or lipid levels.
CONCLUSIONS: Lower RHI suggests possible early endothelial dysfunction, but the evidence is preliminary. No difference was observed in cIMT, DBP and lipid levels between the two groups. Future prospective cohort studies should investigate the longitudinal changes in these parameters, in order to elucidate whether early alterations lead, in the long-term, to increased cardiovascular morbidity in adulthood.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is characterized by persistent gastrointestinal inflammation and immune activation. • IBD may lead to an elevated risk of cardiovascular disease. However, limited data exist regarding cardiovascular parameters on pediatric IBD patients.
WHAT IS NEW: • Lower Reactive Hyperemia Index (RHI) suggests possible endothelial dysfunction; carotid intima-media thickness (cIMT) and lipid levels remain inconclusive. • No statistically significant difference in cIMT was detected between participants with IBD and controls; primary systolic blood pressure (SBP) pooling was not statistically significant; a small increase appeared only after exclusion of one study.
43062498:
BACKGROUND: Resident attrition creates a significant burden for trainees, residency programs, and the healthcare system. The global trends in attrition from neurosurgical residency have not been previously synthesized. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to estimate the global rate of attrition in neurosurgery residents and compare attrition in male and female trainees.
METHODS: We systematically searched Medline, EMBASE, Web of Science, Scopus, and Google Scholar for studies reporting on attrition in neurosurgical trainees. Results were pooled, analyzed using random-effects models, and are presented as Forest plots, pooled proportions, and relative risk. The Newcastle-Ottawa Scale was used for risk of bias assessment, and the GRADE Working Group criteria was used for quality of evidence assessment.
RESULTS: Fourteen studies were included in systematic review, and four studies met the inclusion criteria for meta-analysis. The pooled estimated rate of attrition from neurosurgical residency was 0.13 (95% CI: 0.09-0.17), with significant between-study variation (I2 = 95.9%, p < 0.001). Attrition was higher among female compared with male residents (0.19 vs 0.11; p = 0.001), and females had nearly twice the probability of leaving neurosurgery compared to males (RR 1.92, 95% CI:1.35-2.73). Residents leaving neurosurgery most commonly transferred to radiology, anesthesiology, or emergency medicine, and most frequently left during the first two years of clinical training.
CONCLUSION: Neurosurgery residency has a high attrition rate, with an estimated 13% of residents leaving their program throughout residency training. The rate of attrition in female residents is nearly double the rate of attrition in male residents. Further research is warranted to understand factors which contribute most to attrition, particularly in females.
43062559: Medical vision-language foundation models such as BiomedCLIP offer a promising basis for medical image classification, retrieval, and computer-aided diagnosis. However, local adaptation in healthcare institutions is constrained by data governance requirements, limited computational resources, and the need for maintainable model updates. Full fine-tuning is resource-intensive, whereas conventional parameter-efficient methods may not sufficiently preserve semantic consistency between image features and diagnostic concepts. We propose multimodal semantic reconstruction (MSR), a lightweight adaptation framework for BiomedCLIP with frozen image and text encoders. MSR uses learnable text context vectors, a language-guided visual prompt coupling matrix, weighted multi-level visual feature aggregation, and a learnable contrastive temperature to align visual representations with text-based class prototypes. Its training objective integrates cross-entropy classification with mean squared error and in-batch contrastive alignment losses. We evaluated MSR and six parameter-efficient baselines on ten public medical image classification datasets spanning multiple modalities using three random seeds, with zero-shot BiomedCLIP as an additional reference. Using the full training splits, MSR achieved the highest mean accuracy (89.42%) and macro F1 (87.53%) across the ten datasets among the evaluated methods, with 49,177 trainable parameters. In the few-shot evaluation, MSR did not consistently outperform the compared methods, particularly VPT. Category-level analyses and qualitative visualizations characterized model behavior and residual errors among visually similar classes. These findings suggest that language-guided visual feature reconstruction may provide a technical basis for lightweight, locally maintainable adaptation of medical vision-language models.
43062619:
OBJECTIVES: Radiomics holds potential for personalised treatment, but reproducibility is hindered by inconsistent reporting of imaging parameters and methodological details. This study aims to identify and evaluate key MR imaging parameters to support radiomics reproducibility and to systematically evaluate the quality of published MRI radiomics studies focused on pancreatic tumours.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: The literature search was conducted in the Scopus, PubMed, and Web of Science databases. Human studies investigating MRI radiomics in pancreatic tumours were included. An imaging reporting checklist was developed and used to identify and evaluate imaging parameters in eligible studies. The methodological quality score (METRICS) and checklist for evaluation of radiomics research (CLEAR) score were calculated for each study.
RESULTS: Seventy-eight studies, encompassing 241 MRI pulse sequences (143 anatomical and 98 functional), were included. The imaging checklist identified ten core items as key parameters for ensuring reproducible MRI radiomics. Across all studies, none provided complete or consistent reporting of these parameters, with frequent omissions in imaging acquisition and reconstruction details. Methodological and reporting quality remained suboptimal, reflected by median METRICS and CLEAR scores of 52.4% (45-60%) and 62.3% (56-69%), respectively. Reproducibility and quality of radiomics studies would benefit from clear reporting of imaging parameters, consistent documentation of radiomics settings, and control of confounding variables. Additionally, transparency in model validation, preprocessing, and explanation methods would further enhance reproducibility and clinical relevance.
CONCLUSION: A focused imaging reproducibility checklist has been developed, and it has been demonstrated that no pancreatic tumour MRI radiomics study reported all necessary imaging parameters for reproducibility. Methodological and reporting quality on broader radiomics components was also poor, highlighting the potential value of such a checklist for improving standardised reporting in radiomics studies.
KEY POINTS: Question There is inconsistent reporting of imaging parameters across MRI protocols used for pancreatic tumours radiomics analysis. Findings The developed MR imaging reporting checklist provides structured guidelines to promote consistent documentation of MR imaging parameters and support reproducible radiomics research. Relevance statement By identifying how key MR imaging acquisition and reconstruction parameters are currently presented in MRI radiomics studies of pancreatic tumours, this study highlights inconsistencies and omissions in reporting, underscoring the need for more transparent reporting and adherence to guidelines to support radiomics reproducibility.
43062745:
OBJECTIVE: Carotid endarterectomy (CEA) remains the benchmark open revascularization strategy for appropriately selected patients with extracranial carotid stenosis, whereas carotid artery stenting (CAS) provides an endovascular alternative when cervical exposure, medical comorbidity, or anatomic factors make open surgery less favorable. Balancing periprocedural stroke, myocardial infarction, cranial nerve injury, and long-term stroke risk remains central to contemporary cerebrovascular decision-making. This study compared periprocedural and exploratory long-term outcomes after CAS versus CEA using randomized head-to-head trial evidence across trial eras.
METHODS: PubMed, EMBASE, CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched through April 2026. Eligible studies were randomized trials directly comparing CAS with CEA in adults with extracranial carotid stenosis. Arm-level event counts were extracted. Random-effects risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using inverse-variance models with DerSimonian-Laird estimation. Hartung-Knapp intervals and absolute risk differences were added to support sensitivity analysis and clinical interpretation. The primary endpoint was 30-day stroke or death. Secondary endpoints included periprocedural stroke, death, myocardial infarction (MI), cranial nerve injury, disabling stroke or death, and exploratory long-term stroke-related outcomes.
RESULTS: Six randomized cohorts contributed to the primary endpoint; up to eight contributed to secondary analyses. Thirty-day stroke or death occurred in 244 of 5285 patients assigned to CAS (4.6%) and 156 of 4522 assigned to CEA (3.4%), corresponding to an absolute excess of 1.2 percentage points with CAS and a pooled RR of 1.42 (95% CI, 1.12-1.81; I²=27.9%). Periprocedural stroke was also more common after CAS (291/6305 [4.6%] vs. 186/5546 [3.4%]; RR, 1.44; 95% CI, 1.18-1.75; I²=9.1%). Periprocedural death did not differ significantly (RR, 1.30; 95% CI, 0.77-2.19). MI (RR, 0.45; 95% CI, 0.29-0.71) and cranial nerve injury (RR, 0.05; 95% CI, 0.02-0.11) favored CAS. In a prespecified sensitivity analysis excluding CAVATAS-because most patients in its endovascular arm underwent balloon angioplasty rather than stenting-the primary result was unchanged (RR, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.17-1.95). Exploratory long-term stroke-related outcomes did not differ significantly (RR, 1.05; 95% CI, 0.87-1.26), although endpoint definitions and follow-up windows varied substantially.
CONCLUSIONS: In randomized head-to-head trials, CAS was associated with higher early stroke and stroke-or-death risk than CEA, whereas MI and cranial nerve injury were reported less often after CAS. Selection of open versus endovascular carotid revascularization should be guided by symptom status, age, lesion morphology, cervical and arch anatomy, perioperative cardiac risk, and operator outcomes.
43063058:
BACKGROUND: This systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluated the clinical efficacy and ovarian hemodynamic effects of adjunctive Chinese herbal medicine (CHM) combined with human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) versus hCG alone in infertile women with luteinized unruptured follicle syndrome (LUFS).
METHODS: Seven electronic databases (PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, CBM, CNKI, VIP, and Wanfang Data) were searched from inception through October 6, 2024. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using the Cochrane RoB 2 (Cochrane Risk of Bias Tool for Randomized Trials) tool and modified Jadad scale. The primary outcome was ultrasound-confirmed ovulation rate; secondary outcomes included clinical pregnancy rate, ovarian artery pulsatility index (PI), and resistance index (RI). Dichotomous outcomes were pooled as risk ratios (RRs) using the Mantel-Haenszel method, whereas continuous outcomes were pooled as weighted mean differences (WMDs) using the inverse-variance method, with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Heterogeneity was assessed using I2 and Cochran Q-test, and publication bias using Begg and Egger tests. The protocol was registered with PROSPERO (CRD42025637729).
RESULTS: Seventeen RCTs were included in the review. After exclusion of Zhang LX 2015, the ovulation analysis included 16 RCTs and showed a higher ovulation rate with CHM plus hCG than with hCG alone (RR 1.48, 95% CI: 1.37-1.59; P < .001; I2 = 2%). The combined intervention was also associated with a higher clinical pregnancy rate (RR 2.01, 95% CI: 1.62-2.49; P < .001; I2 = 61%; 15 RCTs). Ovarian artery PI (WMD - 0.49, 95% CI: -0.81 to -0.17; P = .002; I2 = 52%) and RI (WMD - 0.18, 95% CI: -0.31 to -0.06; P = .005; I2 = 78%) were lower with combined treatment, although each analysis included only 2 RCTs. Tests for funnel plot asymmetry were not statistically significant for ovulation rate (Begg P = .260; Egger P = .080). Interpretation was limited by methodological weaknesses, variation in CHM regimens, and sparse evidence for hemodynamic outcomes.
CONCLUSION: Adjunctive CHM may enhance ovulation and clinical pregnancy rates and improve ovarian arterial hemodynamics in infertile women with LUFS. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously given methodological limitations, heterogeneous herbal regimens, and sparse hemodynamic data. Well-designed, multicenter RCTs using standardized CHM formulations and live birth as a primary endpoint are warranted to confirm these findings.
43064237:
INTRODUCTION: Pathologic response (PR) after neoadjuvant therapy is an established surrogate endpoint in lung cancer clinical trials. Although IASLC recommendations standardizing PR assessment in primary tumors are widely adopted, guidance for evaluating treatment response in regional lymph nodes (LNs) has been lacking. The IASLC has developed multidisciplinary consensus recommendations for LN assessment in resected lung cancer specimens following neoadjuvant therapy.
METHODS: A core group of IASLC pathologists drafted statements addressing key aspects of gross and microscopic LN evaluation. These were refined through a two-round Delphi process involving 48 international experts in thoracic oncology, surgery, radiology, and pathology. Consensus was predefined as ≥85% agreement. Experts reviewed, commented upon, and voted on 13 final recommendations.
RESULTS: All 13 recommendations reached consensus (86-100%). Key statements include: defining pathologic complete response (pCR) as the absence of residual viable tumor (RVT) in both lung and LNs; introducing MPR(N+) for cases with ≤10% RVT at the primary site but residual nodal disease; requiring estimation of RVT, stroma, and necrosis across LN stations; accepting unweighted ("eyeball") microscopic assessment; encouraging reporting of metastasis size; and advising complete LN submission with selective use of deeper levels and/or immunohistochemistry. The recommendations further clarify interpretation of direct tumor extension into LN, interpretation of psammoma bodies or acellular mucin, and interactions with ypTNM staging principles.
CONCLUSION: These IASLC multidisciplinary recommendations provide the first standardized framework for assessing treatment response in LNs after neoadjuvant therapy in lung cancer and are intended to improve diagnostic reproducibility, support trial harmonization, and to outline research opportunities.
43064364: Fetal cardiology has become an important subspecialty in Pediatric Cardiology. It includes prenatal detection of congenital heart defects and arrhythmia as well as prenatal therapeutic procedures, planning of perinatal management, and the important part of parental counseling. Currently available methods to diagnose congenital heart disease prenatally, major requirements for parental counseling, available prenatal treatment options, and perinatal care of fetuses and newborns are outlined. A risk-stratified level of care classification system is proposed. This consensus statement of the Fetal Cardiology Working Group of the German Society of Pediatric Cardiology gives an overview about the current status of fetal cardiology in Germany from a Pediatric Cardiology perspective emphasizing that detection rates in Germany stay behind in international comparison due to the minimal requirement of displaying a 4-chamber-view only in screening guidelines according to the "Mutterschaftsrichtlinie." We require mandatory views of the outflow tracts and the 3-vessel-trachea view in the 19 to 22 weeks' examination.
43064644:
BACKGROUND: Scanning at 70 kV on photon-counting CT (PCCT) reduces radiation dose by 50% compared to 120 kV in infants under 10 kg without loss of diagnostic quality. Whether scanning at a lower kV is of benefit in larger children, in whom greater attenuation increases image noise, has not been determined.
METHODS: We retrospectively compared ultra-high-pitch cardiac PCCT examinations in children weighing 10-30 kg acquired at 70 kV (n = 79) or 120 kV (n = 80), both at a CARE keV IQ level of 25. We measured signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) in the ascending aorta and main pulmonary artery and compared radiation dose. Two pediatric cardiac radiologists rated image quality in five vascular structures on a 5-point Likert scale.
RESULTS: Groups were similar in age and size. Neither CNR nor SNR differed significantly. Median Likert scores were at least 4 for four of five structures in both groups. Median CTDIvol was 0.49 vs 0.63 mGy (P < 0.001), and effective dose 0.65 vs 0.75 mSv (P < 0.001) for 70 vs 120 kV.
CONCLUSION: In children weighing 10-30 kg, 70 kV ultra-high-pitch cardiac PCCT was associated with lower radiation dose than 120 kV, with no significant difference in CNR and median reader scores in the diagnostic range. A 120 kV protocol remains appropriate when metal-artifact reduction or advanced spectral reconstructions are needed.
43064856:
BACKGROUND: Photon-counting detector computed tomography (PCD-CT) enables native spectral imaging with the generation of virtual non-contrast (VNC) images from contrast-enhanced acquisitions. Two reconstruction algorithms are currently available, Virtual Unenhanced (VUE) and Liver Virtual Non-Contrast (LVNC), but their reliability compared with True Non-Contrast (TNC) imaging in abdominal applications remains incompletely established. This study evaluated the quantitative accuracy, image quality, and potential clinical impact of VNC reconstructions derived from PCD-CT.
METHODS: In this retrospective single-center study, 150 patients, of whom 140 were included for the analyses, underwent multiphasic PCD-CT including TNC, arterial, and portal venous phases. VNC datasets were generated from arterial and venous acquisitions using the VUE and LVNC algorithms. Tissue attenuation, signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) were compared with TNC images. The agreement of VNC reconstructions with TNC-based classification criteria for hepatic steatosis, myosteatosis, and osteoporosis was also evaluated.
RESULTS: Significant attenuation differences were observed between TNC and VNC reconstructions across most tissues. The smallest errors were found in soft tissues, particularly the liver and spleen, whereas the largest discrepancies occurred in vascular and osseous structures. SNR was higher on VNC than on TNC images in the liver, spleen and paravertebral muscle but lower in several other tissues, whereas CNR was higher with LVNCa and lower with VUEv than with TNC. VUE most closely reproduced TNC attenuation in the liver and spleen, whereas LVNC systematically underestimated attenuation in iodine-enhancing organs. Agreement with TNC-based criteria for hepatic steatosis, myosteatosis and osteoporosis required reconstruction-specific cut-offs, which should be considered exploratory. Omitting TNC could potentially reduce radiation exposure by 16.5% for upper abdomen and 21.2% for total abdominal examinations.
CONCLUSIONS: VUE reconstructions showed good agreement with TNC attenuation in the liver and spleen in both contrast phases, whereas LVNC systematically underestimated attenuation in iodine-enhancing organs and was closer to TNC than VUE only in subcutaneous fat and venous-phase muscle. Substantial bias in vascular and bone structures limits the interchangeability of both algorithms with TNC imaging. VNC may support a potential reduction in radiation dose when replacing a planned TNC acquisition; since lesion detection and characterization were not evaluated, the safe omission of TNC was not demonstrated.
43064857:
BACKGROUND: Noninvasive staging of liver fibrosis is essential in chronic liver disease (CLD). Magnetic resonance elastography (MRE) is well validated but requires dedicated hardware, whereas the apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) derived from conventional diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) lacks specificity. Restriction spectrum imaging (RSI) decomposes the diffusion signal into multiple compartments and may capture fibrosis-related microstructural changes.
PURPOSE: To investigate the feasibility of RSI for noninvasive liver fibrosis staging in CLD and to compare its diagnostic performance with that of MRE, using liver biopsy as the reference standard.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 100 consecutive patients with CLD who underwent liver biopsy, 3.0-T multi-b-value DWI (nine b values, 0-1500 s/mm²), and MRE within 6 months. Multi-compartment RSI models (K = 2-5) were fitted to region-of-interest-averaged signals, and the optimal model was selected using the Bayesian information criterion (BIC). An RSI liver fibrosis index (RSI-LF) was derived from compartment fractions using ordinal logistic regression and internally validated with 1000 bootstrap resamples. AUCs of RSI-LF were compared with those of MRE and ADC using the paired DeLong test.
RESULTS: The five-compartment RSI model (RSI5) showed the lowest BIC. The second and fourth fractions, K5C2 and K5C4, correlated positively (ρ = 0.53) and negatively (ρ = -0.55) with fibrosis stage (both false discovery rate [FDR]-adjusted p < 0.001). RSI-LF yielded AUCs of 0.774 (95% CI: 0.651-0.898), 0.863 (0.793-0.933), and 0.911 (0.842-0.981) for ≥F2, ≥F3, and F4, respectively, with negligible bootstrap optimism. AUCs did not differ significantly from those of MRE at any threshold (all p > 0.05). RSI-LF also outperformed ADC at the ≥F3 and F4 thresholds (both p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Five-compartment RSI provides diffusion metrics associated with histologic fibrosis stage, and RSI-LF showed diagnostic performance numerically comparable to that of MRE. RSI is a promising microstructure-sensitive biomarker for liver fibrosis staging that warrants multicenter validation.
43064860:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate MRI-derived popliteal artery wall index in relation to knee cartilage volume and 24-month cartilage loss in the Foundation for the National Institutes of Health (FNIH) Osteoarthritis Biomarkers Consortium cohort.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This observational cohort study included 594 participants with one indexed knee each. Mean wall index was calculated by averaging values derived using the Fully Automated and Robust Analysis Technique for Popliteal Artery Evaluation across all evaluable axial cross-sectional images reformatted from the sagittal three-dimensional dual-echo steady-state MRI volume. Fully adjusted models, including relevant clinical and imaging covariates, evaluated cross-sectional and change-on-change associations with regional cartilage volume. Mixed-effects and sensitivity analyses assessed robustness.
RESULTS: At baseline, each 10-percentage-point higher mean wall index was associated with lower lateral femoral cartilage volume (β = -67.4 mm3; 95% CI, -126.4 to -8.3; p = 0.025) and thickness (-0.091 mm; 95% CI, -0.162 to -0.021; p = 0.011). Each 1-SD increase in mean wall-index change was associated with greater medial tibial (β = 0.53 percentage points; 95% CI, 0.12 to 0.95; p = 0.012) and lateral femoral (β = 0.35 percentage points; 95% CI, 0.01 to 0.69; p = 0.048) cartilage-volume loss. The medial tibial association was supported by mixed-effects, robust, rank-based, and baseline-adjusted sensitivity analyses.
CONCLUSION: A greater 24-month increase in mean wall index was associated with greater concurrent medial tibial cartilage-volume loss. Mean wall index derived from standardized 3D DESS knee MRI may provide complementary information about concurrent cartilage loss, although further longitudinal studies are needed to establish its clinical significance.
43064865:
OBJECTIVES: The molar tooth sign (MTS) is based on maloriented superior cerebellar peduncles (SCPs), a deepened interpeduncular fossa, and vermian hypoplasia, which may be less clearly delineable prenatally. Phenotypic assessment of patients with suspected Joubert syndrome (JS) was conducted, and additional morphological characteristics of JS on fetal MRI were defined.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this retrospective study, phenotypic assessment was performed for patients with a fetal MRI-based suspected diagnosis of JS. Analysis of the fetal brain included detection of MTS, brainstem anomalies, elevation of the fastigium in the midsagittal plane, thickened SCP with a course parallel to the anterior/middle cerebral fossa in the parasagittal plane, cerebellar dysplasia, cephaloceles, and extracerebral ciliopathic manifestations.
RESULTS: Eleven patients were identified and analyzed-three cases with genetic confirmation of JS, three with incomplete genetic testing, five without confirmatory genetic testing. Classical MTS was present in 55% of cases. Pathological appearance of the SCPs was observed in 73%, and dysplastic cerebellum and brainstem hypo- or dysplasia in 100%. Elevation of the fastigium was observed in 91%, cephaloceles in 46%, and extracerebral anomalies, especially renal, in 64%. All cases showed a hypo- and dysplastic vermis.
CONCLUSION: This study provides novel insights into the prenatal presentation of molar tooth malformations and accompanying anomalies commonly observed in patients with a suspected diagnosis of JS. JS can be suspected on fetal MRI even in the absence of classical MTS based on characteristic anomalies of the SCPs, brainstem, and cerebellum in combination with extracerebral anomalies supporting this diagnosis.
KEY POINTS: QuestionWhat are phenotypical presentations of patients with suspected Joubert syndrome (JS) in fetal MRI and can JS be suspected in absence of molar tooth sign? FindingsJS can be suspected in fetal MRI without MTS based on characteristic changes in superior cerebellar peduncles, brainstem, and cerebellum and co-occurring extracerebral anomalies. Clinical relevanceThis exploratory study provides novel insights into the prenatal presentation of molar tooth malformations and associated anomalies commonly observed in cases with suspected JS. These findings may aid counseling physicians in selecting appropriate pregnancy management for patients with suspected JS.
43064868:
PURPOSE: Upper limb dysfunction (pain, reduced shoulder mobility and strength, activity limitation) is common after breast cancer treatment, with or without breast cancer-related lymphedema (BCRL). Proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation (PNF) has been proposed to improve upper limb function and range of motion (ROM). This systematic review evaluates PNF for upper limb dysfunction in women treated for breast cancer, analyzing women with and without BCRL separately.
METHODS: The Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement was followed. Four databases were searched without date restrictions. Randomized or quasi-randomized English-language trials of PNF-containing interventions in women treated for breast cancer were included. Risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool and certainty of evidence with the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach.
RESULTS: Six trials (366 women) were included: three enrolled women with confirmed BCRL and three women without BCRL. PNF was mostly part of multimodal programs, but the between-group contrast isolated PNF in four trials. In BCRL trials, limb volume decreased in all groups, with no consistent advantage of PNF over active comparators. In women without BCRL, single trials reported improvements in ROM, strength and function. Risk of bias was low in one trial, high in one and of some concern in four; certainty of evidence was low or very low.
CONCLUSION: PNF may be a promising component of multimodal rehabilitation for upper limb dysfunction after breast cancer treatment; its independent effectiveness and its effects on BCRL remain unproven, and in women with BCRL it should complement, not replace, decongestive treatment. Trials in women with confirmed BCRL and standardized PNF protocols are needed.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD42025641774, registered on 2 February 2025 (retrospectively registered).
43064878:
OBJECTIVE: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) has an extremely dismal postoperative prognosis. Conventional TNM staging cannot adequately characterize tumor heterogeneity and microenvironment, leading to suboptimal risk stratification. This study aimed to develop and externally validate an integrated prognostic system for PDAC by combining deep learning (DL)-based radiomic features with guideline‑recommended clinicopathological variables.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included 592 patients with PDAC who underwent R0 surgical resection. A Swin Transformer-assisted DL classifier (Outcome Prediction for PDAC, OP-PDAC) was built using multi-planar contrast-enhanced CT scans (axial, coronal, and sagittal planes). Radiogenomic analysis was conducted in 41 patients to elucidate the biological underpinnings of the OP-PDAC. Furthermore, the Intelligent Prognosis Stratification System (IPSS-PDAC) was developed by incorporating clinicopathological variables into the OP-PDAC framework.
RESULTS: In the derivation and test cohorts, the C‑index of OP-PDAC for predicting 1‑year disease‑free survival (DFS) ranged from 0.807 to 0.844, which was significantly higher than that of the clinicopathological model (CP-PDAC; C‑index, 0.631-0.656). The IPSS-PDAC further enhanced predictive performance, yielding a C‑index of 0.836-0.871, and enabled effective stratification for both DFS and overall survival (all log‑rank p < 0.01). Radiogenomic analysis revealed that high‑risk patients exhibited an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, elevated stromal scores, activated oncogenic pathways, and reduced CD8+ T‑cell infiltration.
