CONCLUSION: IPSS-PDAC is a non-invasive and robust prognostic stratification system that integrates imaging features and clinicopathological features. By sensitively reflecting tumor heterogeneity and TME, it provides references for clinical decision-making in the postoperative management of PDAC patients.
KEY POINTS: Question This study constructs an integrated prognostic model combining imaging signatures and guideline-recommended clinicopathological variables to address unmet clinical challenges in postoperative risk stratification for PDAC patients. Findings A multi-planar Swin Transformer-based deep learning model (IPSS-PDAC) achieves a C-index of 0.836-0.871 for disease-free survival prediction. Critical relevance statement High-risk patients stratified by the OP-PDAC model display a profoundly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, activation of core oncogenic signaling pathways, and reduced CD8+ T-cell infiltration.
43065182:
OBJECTIVES: Cerebral redistribution consists of the preferential redirection of the arterial and well-oxygenated blood flow to the fetal brain and is commonly associated with fetal growth restriction (FGR) secondary to placental insufficiency. In this study, we aimed to evaluate the perinatal outcomes of fetuses with late-onset FGR and cerebral redistribution, examining whether outcomes differed according to the normality or abnormality of the individual Doppler components that determine a reduction in the cerebroplacental ratio (CPR).
METHODS: This was a retrospective, multicenter cohort study conducted across four tertiary maternity units in Italy (University of Parma, Parma; Fondazione Policlinico Universitario 'A. Gemelli' IRCCS, Rome; IRCCS Materno Infantile Burlo Garofolo, Trieste; and University of Brescia, Brescia), including non-anomalous singleton pregnancies complicated by late-onset FGR associated with cerebral redistribution (defined as CPR < 5th percentile according to the Fetal Medicine Foundation reference charts). The study included cases collected at the four participating units between January 2019 and December 2024. Cases were categorized according to umbilical artery (UA) and middle cerebral artery (MCA) Doppler data (Group 1: normal UA-pulsatility index (PI) (≤ 95th percentile for gestational age) and MCA-PI (≥ 5th percentile); Group 2: abnormal UA-PI (> 95th percentile) and normal MCA-PI; Group 3: normal UA-PI and abnormal MCA-PI (< 5th percentile); and Group 4: abnormal UA-PI and MCA-PI), and perinatal outcomes were compared and evaluated using univariate and multivariable logistic regression analyses.
RESULTS: In total, 352 cases were included, of which 117 (33.2%) were assigned to Group 1, 84 (23.9%) to Group 2, 85 (24.1%) to Group 3 and 66 (18.8%) to Group 4. In the univariate logistic regression analysis, Group 4 showed greater odds of preterm delivery (odds ratio (OR), 2.07 (95% CI, 1.08-3.96); P = 0.03), birth weight < 3rd percentile (OR, 2.44 (95% CI, 1.31-4.57); P = 0.01), neonatal hypoglycemia (OR, 3.34 (95% CI, 1.46-7.67); P < 0.01), neonatal intensive care unit admission (OR, 2.33 (95% CI, 1.24-4.37); P = 0.01) and composite adverse perinatal outcome (CAPO) (OR, 2.44 (95% CI, 1.31-4.57); P = 0.01) compared with Group 1. Furthermore, Group 2 showed greater odds of preterm delivery (OR, 2.06 (95% CI, 1.12-3.79); P = 0.02) and birth weight < 3rd percentile (OR, 1.92 (95% CI, 1.07-3.46); P = 0.03) and Group 3 showed greater odds of birth weight < 3rd percentile (OR, 1.79 (95% CI, 1.01-3.26); P = 0.02) and CAPO (OR, 1.88 (95% CI, 1.05-3.38); P = 0.03) compared with Group 1. However, in the multivariable logistic regression analysis only Group 4 was associated with greater odds of birth weight < 3rd percentile (adjusted OR, 2.11 (95% CI, 1.11-4.00); P = 0.02) and neonatal hypoglycemia (adjusted OR, 2.68 (95% CI, 1.10-6.50); P = 0.03) compared with Group 1. In the univariate logistic regression analysis, abnormal UA and MCA Doppler parameters were also associated with perinatal complications. However, none of the associations were confirmed after adjustment for gestational age at delivery and birth weight in the multivariable models.
CONCLUSIONS: In cases of late-onset FGR associated with cerebral redistribution, isolated abnormalities of the UA-PI or MCA-PI could not identify fetuses at increased risk of perinatal complications. However, the coexistence of both abnormal UA-PI and abnormal MCA-PI, indicating the highest extent of cerebral redistribution, was independently associated with perinatal complications including neonatal hypoglycemia and birth weight < 3rd percentile. In such cases, birth weight was also independently associated with perinatal complications. © 2026 International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology.
43065480:
BACKGROUND: Spinal tuberculosis is a severe form of extrapulmonary tuberculosis that often results in delayed diagnosis and irreversible neurological complications. Xpert MTB/RIF and Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra have been developed as rapid molecular diagnostic tools; however, their diagnostic performance in spinal tuberculosis remains uncertain, particularly across different reference standards.
OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of Xpert-based assays for spinal tuberculosis and assess the influence of different reference standards on pooled diagnostic estimates.
METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library was performed from database inception to June 2026. Studies evaluating Xpert MTB/RIF or Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra in patients with suspected spinal tuberculosis and providing sufficient data to construct 2×2 diagnostic tables were included. Pooled sensitivity, specificity, likelihood ratios, and diagnostic odds ratios were estimated using a bivariate random-effects model. Hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic (HSROC) curves were generated. The primary analysis included studies using composite or clinical reference standards, whereas mycobacterial culture alone was evaluated in a separate sensitivity analysis.
RESULTS: Twelve studies were included in the quantitative synthesis. In the primary analysis based on composite or clinical reference standards, the pooled sensitivity and specificity of Xpert-based assays were 0.77 (95% CI: 0.66-0.86) and 1.00 (95% CI: 0.99-1.00), respectively. The pooled positive and negative likelihood ratios were 43.86 (95% CI: 23.65-81.36) and 0.24 (95% CI: 0.15-0.37), respectively, with a diagnostic odds ratio of 213.28 (95% CI: 89.30-509.42). In the sensitivity analysis using mycobacterial culture as the reference standard, pooled sensitivity increased to 0.94 (95% CI: 0.88-0.98), whereas specificity decreased to 0.62 (95% CI: 0.44-0.78). Only one included study evaluated Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra, limiting conclusions regarding its comparative performance.
CONCLUSION: Xpert-based assays demonstrate high diagnostic accuracy for spinal tuberculosis, particularly strong confirmatory capability due to high specificity. However, negative results alone are insufficient to exclude disease. The choice of reference standard substantially influences pooled diagnostic estimates, highlighting the importance of interpreting Xpert results together with clinical, radiological, microbiological, and histopathological findings.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261427181, identifier CRD420261427181.
43066650:
INTRODUCTION: Reliable cell annotations are essential for supervised image analysis, yet producing the annotations required for quantitative cellular morphometry is laborious, and results can vary with both tissue preparation and expert interpretation of ambiguous morphology. Nissl staining has long underpinned comparative neuroanatomy, generating extensive and taxonomically diverse records of cellular organization across the nervous system. We developed Anatolution to make this resource more amenable to standardized quantitative analysis by integrating independent annotations alongside explicit measures of rater agreement for quality control under computer vision bookkeeping.
METHOD: Anatolution is an open-source web platform for annotating single images or 3D volumes (https://anatolution.herokuapp.com/public-tool/). Multiple raters independently outline cellular structures using a shared set of labels or conventions, and the platform enables consensus analysis alongside conventional image segmentation.
RESULT: We evaluated 603,297 annotations produced by 48 raters across 1,024 image tiles and tested a subset of 68 fully annotated tiles against unsupervised segmentation. Boundary overlap in cell drawings, scored from 0 ("no overlap") to 1 ("identical"), rose from 0.30 for 1 rater to 0.79 with 7 users, and in a subset of 68 annotated tiles, 88% contained unsupervised segmentation results.
CONCLUSION: Agreement between groups of raters increased as raters were added to an optimum of ∼7 users, and within a subset of images nearly 9 in 10 annotations were spatially anchored to unsupervised methods. Anatolution supports the production of consensus labels whose stability can be quantified and improved by adding independent raters, providing structured reference data for training and evaluating cell segmentation models for quantitative histology.
43066668:
BACKGROUND: Atherosclerosis, silent in its early stages, underlies most cardiovascular manifestations. The inter-relation between silent atherosclerosis across vascular territories remains insufficiently characterized.
OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to assess the association between peripheral and coronary atherosclerosis in asymptomatic individuals.
METHODS: A subgroup of individuals of the PESA (Progression of Early Subclinical Atherosclerosis) cohort underwent contrast-enhanced coronary computed tomography angiography in addition to peripheral (carotid and femoral) atherosclerosis assessment using 3-dimensional vascular ultrasound. Peripheral global plaque volume was calculated as the sum of bilateral carotid and femoral plaque burden using an artificial intelligence-based automated approach. Coronary computed tomographic angiographic images were qualitatively evaluated for the presence and severity of coronary atherosclerosis (percentage stenosis) and quantitatively for coronary artery calcium score (CACS) and global coronary plaque volume measurement.
RESULTS: A total of 374 participants (mean age: 55 years, 34% women, 63% with CACS = 0) were included. Peripheral atherosclerosis was present in 75%. Peripheral global plaque volume was significantly associated with the presence, severity, and burden of coronary atherosclerosis (coronary plaque volume) (r = 0.69; P < 0.001). After adjustment for age, sex, and conventional risk factor profile, individuals with peripheral atherosclerosis had nearly 3 times greater odds of having coronary atherosclerosis than those without (OR: 2.66; 95% CI: 1.50-4.72; P = 0.001). Both carotid and femoral atherosclerosis remained significantly and independently associated with coronary plaque. Among participants with CACS = 0, noncalcified coronary plaque was detected in 12.0%, nearly all of whom (93%) had concomitant peripheral atherosclerosis.
CONCLUSIONS: Peripheral and coronary atherosclerosis were strongly correlated in asymptomatic persons. Both carotid and femoral atherosclerosis were associated with coronary artery disease independently of each other.
43066738:
BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence (AI)-based tools are increasingly used for bone age assessment, but their agreement with traditional atlas-based methods requires further evaluation.
OBJECTIVE: To compare bone age estimates obtained using the Greulich and Pyle Atlas, the Pocket Atlas of Skeletal Age, and the Hand Bone Age AI web application developed at Stanford University.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective analysis was performed in 376 pediatric patients. Agreement between methods was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), Bland-Altman analysis, Friedman tests, and subgroup analyses according to age, sex, and pubertal status.
RESULTS: Median bone age estimates were identical across methods (144 months). Overall agreement was high (ICC=0.93, 95% CI 0.92-0.94). Significant differences were observed between the AI-based method and both atlas-based methods, whereas no significant difference was found between the two atlas-based approaches. Clinical agreement within ±12 months reached 96.5% for the atlas-based methods and 77.4-83.8% for comparisons involving AI. Sex significantly influenced agreement, while pubertal status showed less consistent effects.
CONCLUSION: AI-based and atlas-based methods showed high overall agreement, although AI demonstrated greater variability at the individual patient level. Patient sex may influence agreement between assessment methods.
43066743:
INTRODUCTION: Cubital tunnel syndrome (CuTS) is a common and debilitating compression neuropathy of the ulnar nerve. Using MRI, the early effects on skeletal muscle might be quantifiable, enabling early diagnosis and curative surgery. Muscle oedema is quantified through T2 mapping, and lipoatrophy is quantified through muscle fat fractions (FF). This prospective cohort study aims to investigate whether CuTS changes the muscle T2 of FF.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: 29 healthy controls and 19 patients awaiting surgery were scanned at 3.0 T. In the forearm and the hand, FF images were acquired via three-point Dixon and T2 measurements were made using a multi-echo spin echo sequence. Measurements were extracted from ulnar-innervated muscles (flexor carpi ulnaris, 1st dorsal interosseous and adductor policis) and a control muscle, brachioradialis. Between-group comparisons are made using linear methods, and 95% confidence intervals (CI) are computed.
RESULTS: Patients with CuTS had prolonged T2 and elevated FF in their ulnar-innervated muscles, compared to controls. In patients with CuTS, the flexor carpi ulnaris muscle had 3 ms longer T2 (CI 0.49, 5.64), and the 1st dorsal interossesi and adductor policis had prolonged T2 (mean 5.59 ms [CI 1.61, 9.58] and 5.35 ms [CI 1.18, 9.51], respectively). Patients' flexor carpi ulnaris also had 2% higher fat [CI 0.25, 3.60] than healthy controls. There were no detectable differences in T2 or FF in the brachioradialis between patients and controls.
CONCLUSION: We show that adults with CuTS have prolonged T2 in ulnar-innervated muscles and an elevated FF in the flexor carpi ulnaris.
KEY POINTS: Question There is no reliable or quantifiable diagnostic tool for diagnosing cubital tunnel syndrome. Findings The ulnar-innervated skeletal muscles in adults with cubital tunnel syndrome exhibit increased fat fractions and prolonged T2, which are subclinical. Clinical relevance Quantitative MRI, specifically muscle T2 and fat fractions, may be an early biomarker of cubital tunnel syndrome and useful for selecting patients for surgery.
43066744:
OBJECTIVES: To compare the magnitude of diffusion tensor image analysis along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS) reduction across normal pressure hydrocephalus (NPH), Alzheimer's disease (AD), and Parkinson's disease (PD), and to refine its interpretation across the fluid-dynamic spectrum.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched on 2 March 2026. Studies reporting baseline ALPS indices in AD, PD, or NPH with healthy controls were included. Standardized mean differences were calculated using Hedges' g with random-effects models. Cross-disease differences were evaluated using independent Z-tests.
RESULTS: Forty-nine studies contributing 50 datasets and involving 5318 participants were included. ALPS indices were reduced in all three disorders compared with controls. The pooled standardized mean difference was -0.95 (95% CI -1.16 to -0.75; k = 16; I² = 59.5%) in AD and -0.70 (95% CI -0.86 to -0.54; k = 28; I² = 78.8%) in PD. In contrast, NPH demonstrated a markedly larger reduction of -2.20 (95% CI -2.84 to -1.56; k = 6; I² = 82.0%). The distribution of study-level ALPS values showed NPH clustered at markedly lower values with minimal overlap with AD or PD. Consistent with this, summary-level (unadjusted) Z-tests indicated a larger reduction in NPH than in AD (Z = 3.63, p < 0.001) and PD (Z = 4.44, p < 0.001), whereas AD and PD did not differ significantly (p = 0.061).
CONCLUSION: DTI-ALPS reductions were observed across AD, PD, and NPH, with a substantially greater though heterogeneous reduction in NPH. This pattern may reflect CSF fluid-dynamic disturbance, structural distortion of the ALPS measurement environment, or both, although its physiological basis and diagnostic utility require prospective validation.
KEY POINTS: Question Do diffusion tensor image analysis along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS) alterations demonstrate distinct magnitudes and patterns across normal pressure hydrocephalus and major neurodegenerative disorders? Findings ALPS indices were reduced across all three disorders, with a substantially larger reduction in normal pressure hydrocephalus (Hedges' g = -2.20) than in Alzheimer's disease (-0.95) or Parkinson's disease (-0.70). Clinical relevance Beyond the diagnosis of normal pressure hydrocephalus, which is radiologically apparent, the magnitude of DTI-ALPS reduction may hold value as a marker of fluid-dynamic or structural severity and treatment response, warranting prospective evaluation.
43066745:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the performance of AI algorithms in reducing gadolinium (Gd) administration in brain MRI by generating synthetic post-contrast images from low-dose inputs.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Comprehensive searches of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase were conducted through April 17, 2026. Study screening, eligibility assessment, quality evaluation, and data extraction were performed independently by two reviewers. Pooled peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and structural similarity index (SSIM) values were calculated using a random-effects model. Heterogeneity was quantified using the I² statistic. These analyses were additionally followed by evaluations of the reported qualitative assessments.
RESULTS: Twelve studies met the inclusion criteria, most of which used convolutional neural network architectures. The pooled PSNR was 32.91 dB (95% CI: 31.37-34.46; I² = 99.08%) across seven studies, and the pooled SSIM was 91.81% (95% CI: 89.33-94.30; I² = 99.69%) across six studies. Subgroup analyses stratified by contrast-dose reduction level, deep learning model type, and input modality did not identify consistent contributors to heterogeneity. Given substantial between-study heterogeneity, pooled estimates were interpreted descriptively. Across the qualitative assessments, synthetic images were generally rated as diagnostically acceptable or comparable to full-dose images for most tasks, although subtle differences in lesion conspicuity and artifact patterns were reported.
CONCLUSION: AI models demonstrate promising technical performance for generating synthetic post-contrast brain MRI with high voxel-wise similarity to full-dose images at substantial contrast-dose reductions. However, marked heterogeneity, limited external validation, and the lack of clinically oriented diagnostic outcomes limit the interpretability and generalizability of current evidence.
KEY POINTS: Question There is a need to determine how effectively artificial intelligence can reduce gadolinium use in brain MRI by generating synthetic post-contrast images from low-dose inputs. Findings Across 12 studies involving 3846 patients, AI-generated post-contrast brain MRI achieved pooled peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and structural similarity index (SSIM) values of 32.91 dB and 91.81%, respectively, with substantial between-study heterogeneity. Clinical relevance AI-assisted synthetic post-contrast imaging may substantially reduce gadolinium exposure in neuroradiology while preserving diagnostic confidence. However, high heterogeneity highlights the need for cautious interpretation and further multicenter standardization before clinical adoption.
43066770: Acute Necrotizing Encephalopathy (ANE) is a rare para-infectious encephalopathy typically affecting young children, characterized by symmetric bilateral thalamic lesions on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Adolescent- or adult-onset remains exceptional. Familial or recurrent forms are associated with heterozygous RAN-binding protein 2 (RANBP2) variants and classified as ANE type 1 (ANE1). We describe two siblings with late-onset ANE1 from an Italian family and systematically reviewed the demographic and genetic spectrum of RANBP2-associated disease. The proband, a 20-year-old woman, presented with a mild post-infectious encephalopathy and bilateral thalamic lesions, with good recovery after immunomodulatory therapy. Her brother developed a fulminant post-febrile encephalopathy at age 15, progressing to coma, with bilateral thalamic, pontine, and external capsule involvement on MRI, and persistent sequelae. Whole-exome sequencing in the proband identified the heterozygous RANBP2 variant c.1754C > T (p.Thr585Met), confirmed by Sanger sequencing in her brother, enabling a retrospective diagnosis. Their father and another brother were asymptomatic carriers, supporting incomplete penetrance. The systematic review identified 53 reports (138 affected individuals from 85 case/family-units). Among 130 individuals with available data, 57 had recurrences. Age at onset was available for 84 patients, six presented at 12 years or older, and four in adulthood. The p.Thr585Met variant accounted for 60% of family-units and 65% of affected individuals. These findings expand the age and phenotypic spectrum of RANBP2-associated ANE and demonstrate intrafamilial variability. To our knowledge, this is the third Italian family reported, and the first with late-onset presentations. Our findings support considering RANBP2 testing beyond childhood and prompt immunomodulatory treatment in suspected cases.
43066784: Pancreatoblastoma is a malignant tumor, which accounts for less than 1% of all pancreatic neoplasms. Further, it is rarely seen in adults and has a poor prognosis with metastasis or local invasion is present in nearly half of adult patients at diagnosis, most often involving the liver. CT is the first-line modality for detection and surgical planning, yet the findings overlap those of more common pancreatic tumors. Pancreatoblastoma typically presents as a large exophytic mass in the pancreatic head with well-defined margins and an enhancing capsule. However, the capsule is often incomplete, and advanced tumors may show infiltrative borders. The mass is heterogeneous and may be solid or mixed solid and cystic, with calcification, enhancing internal septations, necrosis, hemorrhage, or potentially even internal vascularity. Pancreatoblastoma is mostly hypoattenuating relative to normal pancreatic parenchyma and shows progressive enhancement. Large tumors may cause biliary or main pancreatic ductal dilatation, tumor thrombus, or invasion of adjacent organs. Using pathologically proven adult cases, this pictorial review illustrates the spectrum of CT appearances of pancreatoblastoma and highlights the imaging characteristics of this rarely encountered tumor.
43066792: Management of acute subdural hematoma in the elderly requires nuanced clinical decision-making. While the Brain Trauma Foundation incorporates clot thickness and midline shift in their ASDH management guidelines, they do not quote an age bracket cut-off. Evidence to date suggests the elderly see disproportionately high morbidity and mortality regardless of surgical or conservative management. To systematically review the evidence comparing surgical evacuation versus conservative management of ASDH in elderly patients and assess the impact of patient factors on outcomes, a systematic review was conducted examining six observational studies (n = 812) comparing surgical and conservative management of traumatic ASDH in patients aged 60 or older. Outcomes included in-hospital mortality, 6-month mortality, and functional outcomes. MEDLINE, Embase and CINAHL were searched up to December 2025. Risk of bias assessment was performed using the Newcastle Ottawa Scale. Results were presented descriptively and synthesized narratively by outcome timepoint as clinical and methodological heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis. Surgery was not consistently associated with improved mortality nor improved functional outcomes. Surgical patients presented with worse clinical and radiological severity. In-hospital mortality analysis of three cohorts demonstrated substantial heterogeneity, with relative risks ranging from 1.37 to 13.63, favoring conservative management. Six-month mortality showed even greater heterogeneity with directionally inconsistent findings. Functional outcomes, when reported, either favored conservative management or were neutral. Current evidence does not establish a consistent mortality or functional advantage for surgical evacuation of ASDH in elderly patients. Patients with poor neurological status demonstrate high mortality regardless of intervention, while those with mild neurological impairment may not derive meaningful benefit from surgery. Future prospective studies should standardize frailty assessment alongside clinical and radiographic parameters to identify where true clinical equipoise exists and establish guidelines in this distinct patient population. No funding was received for this review.
43066852: Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor (MPNST) is the leading cause of cancer-related death in neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1), with a lifetime risk of 8-15% and five-year survival below 50% in most series. Imaging surveillance, most often whole-body magnetic resonance imaging (WB-MRI), is offered on the premise that earlier detection of premalignant or early malignant lesions permits curative resection, but the supporting evidence has not been formally synthesized. Following the PRISMA 2020 statement, we searched MEDLINE, EMBASE, Cochrane CENTRAL, trial registries, and conference proceedings from 2000 to July 2026 for studies of structured surveillance or lesion characterization in people with NF1. Two reviewers screened and extracted data independently, risk of bias was assessed with design-specific tools, and certainty was graded with GRADE. Sixteen records were included: six surveillance-impact or natural-history cohorts, five imaging diagnostic-accuracy studies, two investigational cell-free DNA studies, and three contextual records (a guideline, a prognostic meta-analysis, and a registered protocol). Because the data were few and heterogeneous, no meta-analysis was possible and the primary objectives could not be addressed quantitatively. The only comparative incidence estimate came from one retrospective cohort compared with expected population-based rates. One retrospective imaging study traced 91% of MPNSTs to a pre-existing distinct nodular lesion. Diffusion-weighted MRI and FDG-PET discriminated benign from malignant tumors with high sensitivity in symptomatic referral cohorts, with threshold-dependent specificity. Harms were inconsistently reported. Certainty was very low for surveillance impact and harms and low for diagnostic accuracy. Current evidence is insufficient to establish whether surveillance improves outcomes; this review informs the design of prospective trials and the next revision of international surveillance guidelines.
43067325:
BACKGROUND: The management of atypical ductal hyperplasia (ADH) remains a clinical challenge. The use of contrast-enhanced (CE) imaging has been proposed to reduce the upgrade rates of ADH and minimize unnecessary surgical procedures.
PURPOSE: This systematic review aims to estimate the pooled upgrade rate of ADH diagnosed through percutaneous biopsy in cases with a negative CE examination, independent of biopsy technique, needle size, imaging guidance.
METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed, EMBASE, and Web of Science databases was performed in December 2024. Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses, or PRISMA, guidelines were followed. The Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies checklist was used to assess the risk of bias. Upgrades were calculated using random-effects meta-analysis based on the log risk-ratios.
RESULTS: Out of 124 screened articles, 7 studies were included, providing data on 312 ADH lesions, including 145 cases with a negative CE-MRI. The pooled upgrade rate was 1 % (95 % [CI]: 0 %-4 %) for ADH lesions with negative CE imaging after biopsy. The pooled risk ratio was 8.80, with a statistically significant difference (p < 0.001) between positive and negative CE imaging. The overall sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV) were 0.95 (0.85-1.00), 0.75 (0.58-0.89), 0.62 (0.41-0.82), and 0.98 (0.93-1.00), respectively.
CONCLUSION: Although the study cohort was relatively small, we found a pooled upgrade rate lower than 2 %, suggesting that conservative management rather than surgery may be justified for ADH with a negative MRI-imaging, as established for BI-RADS category 3 lesions.
43067619: AI-powered cardiac screening could evolve sports medicine by boosting accuracy, efficiency, and cost-effectiveness, with automated ECG interpretation based on foundation models becoming key for large-scale athlete screening. Before deployment, it is crucial to verify whether these clinically developed models are applicable to this population. We evaluated whether ECG foundation models trained on general clinical populations can diagnose athlete-specific ECG findings. We fine-tuned three models (ECG-FM, HuBERT-ECG, ECGFounder) on PhysioNet/CinC 2021, 87,662 samples, and tested them on 43 expert-annotated ECGs from highly trained/national-level athletes. Performance was strong on PhysioNet/CinC 2021 (AUROC 0.97, AUPRC 0.57, Sensitivity 0.89) but dropped on athletes' data, confirming domain shift. ECGFounder performed best (AUROC 0.84, AUPRC 0.72, Sensitivity 0.57) and detected the most frequent findings, Sinus Bradycardia (AUROC 0.87) and Sinus Arrhythmia (AUROC 0.95), well. Per-label estimates for rare classes must be interpreted cautiously, given the small cohort. This work contributes to developing athlete-focused AI frameworks for reliable ECG-based screening.
43068514:
BACKGROUND: Surgical margin assessment in oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) remains poorly standardized by HPV status, subsite, and treatment context. This European Head and Neck Society (EHNS) consensus aimed to harmonize margin assessment and margin-based decisions.
METHODS: Following systematic review, 25 multidisciplinary panelists evaluated recommendations through two Delphi rounds; consensus was ≥80 % and near-consensus 70-79.9 %. Margindefinitionswerebasedonformalin-fixed,paraffin-embeddedsections,notintraoperativeor postoperativegrossingestimates.
RESULTS: Of 48 recommendations, 32 reached consensus, six near-consensus, and 10 were rejected. "Ink on tumor" defined a positive margin irrespective of HPV status (96 %). A 5-mm mucosal margin was retained for HPV-negative OPSCC (84 %), whereas 3 mm reached near-consensus for HPV-positive disease (78.3 %); smaller thresholds were unsupported. A clear margin alone should not determine adjuvant treatment (78.3 %, near-consensus). Re-resection was recommended when the margin site was identifiable and would change adjuvant management. Positive margins warranted radiotherapy in pT1-T2 HPV-positive disease without other adverse features (80 %), whereas chemoradiotherapy was recommended with high-risk features, such as pT3-T4 disease or extranodal extension (95.8 %), and in HPV-negative disease (100 %). For close margins, selective de-escalation could be considered in highly selected HPV-positive disease without high-risk features (82.6 %), whereas HPV-negative disease warranted radiotherapy, with escalation according to additional risks (91.3 %). In fit patients aged ≥70 years with positive margins, radiotherapy alone was favored for HPV-positive disease (87.5 %), while chemoradiotherapy was retained for fit patients with HPV-negative disease (95.7 %).
CONCLUSIONS: This consensus provides a multidisciplinary framework for harmonized OPSCC margin assessment and risk-adapted postoperative management across HPV status, anatomy, and treatment-related morbidity.
43068765:
INTRODUCTION: The Thoracoabdominal Branch Endoprosthesis (TAMBE) recently received FDA approval as the first off-the-shelf endovascular device for complex aneurysmal disease involving the visceral aorta. Prior to formal FDA approval, a pivotal pre-approval analysis demonstrated high procedural success, low perioperative morbidity, and no perioperative mortality. Using Medicare Fee-for-Service (FFS) data, we sought to evaluate real-world adoption patterns and 30-day outcomes following TAMBE implementation nationwide.
METHODS: Medicare Fee-for-Service beneficiaries undergoing TAMBE between October 2024 and December 2025 were identified using the TAMBE-specific ICD-10-PCS code (X2VE3SA). Outcomes were compared to a contemporaneous cohort undergoing ≥4-vessel F/BEVAR in 2023, the year preceding TAMBE approval. Primary outcomes included 30-day mortality, stroke, myocardial infarction (MI), acute kidney injury (AKI), spinal cord ischemia (SCI), bowel ischemia, and reintervention, and were analyzed using Fine-Gray competing-risk regressions with adjustment for demographic, clinical, and procedural characteristics. Pre-specified sub-analyses examined outcomes by aortic indication, hospital procedure volume, and adoption period. Consistent with CMS small-cell suppression policy, any outcome frequencies <11 events were masked and not reported.
RESULTS: The primary cohort consisted of 869 patients treated at 351 hospitals, compared with 678 patients undergoing 4-vessel F/BEVAR. TAMBE was associated with significantly higher unadjusted 30-day mortality (6.7% vs. 4.0%; P=.02), though this difference did not persist after adjustment (adjusted HR 1.37 [0.85-2.21]). No differences were observed in stroke (<1.3% vs. <1.6%), MI (2.0% vs. <1.6%), AKI (7.2% vs. 6.9%) or SCI (5.0% vs. 4.1%) (all P>.05). The majority of implanting hospitals (N=195; 56%) performed a single TAMBE during the study period, and 30-day outcomes did not differ significantly by hospital volume after adjustment. A sensitivity analysis restricted to unambiguously coded, elective TAMBE cases compared with elective F/BEVAR showed similarly elevated 30-day mortality (6.8% vs. 4.0%), albeit not statistically different following adjustment (aHR 1.46 [0.75-2.84]).
CONCLUSION: In this national analysis of Medicare FFS beneficiaries, real-world 30-day outcomes following TAMBE in the first year-plus of commercial availability were notably worse than those reported in the pivotal trial and early single-institution post-market series, with a nearly 7% 30-day mortality rate that persisted across indications, hospital volumes, and time periods. The rapid dissemination of TAMBE to over 351 hospitals, most performing only a single procedure, highlights a fundamental tension between the device's off-the-shelf accessibility and the institutional readiness required for safe deployment, underscoring the need for ongoing post-market surveillance, structured proctorship programs, and a more deliberate approach to patient and operator selection as TAMBE adoption continues.
43069085:
BACKGROUND: Neonatal early-onset sepsis (EOS) caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae is a rare but life-threatening, presenting with a fulminant clinical course despite vaccine-driven epidemiological shifts in older populations. Serotype 3 is notorious for its thick polysaccharide capsule and high virulence, yet its specific neonatal phenotype remains poorly characterized. We present a case of severe serotype 3 EOS integrated with a 25-year systematic literature review to elucidate the clinical pattern of this phenotype, differentiating the role of intrinsic virulence from antimicrobial resistance.
CASE PRESENTATION: A term female neonate developed severe respiratory distress, metabolic acidosis, and multilineage cytopenias on her first day of life. Chest radiography revealed a reticulonodular pattern consistent with neonatal pneumonia. Blood cultures rapidly isolated S. pneumoniae, later identified as capsular serotype 3, which was fully susceptible to penicillin. The patient was successfully managed with targeted intravenous ampicillin, achieving rapid and complete clinical recovery.
RESULTS: To contextualize this presentation, a 25-year literature review identified 41 confirmed cases of pneumococcal EOS. Overall, symptom onset was hyper-acute, with 63.4% (n = 26/41) of the cohort becoming symptomatic within the first 24 h of life. Among the 34 serotyped isolates, serotype 3 was the most prevalent (26.5%, n = 9/34). Serotype 3 infections were associated with an atypical clinical behavior and a higher mortality rate compared to non-serotype 3 cases (33.3% vs. 16%, p = 0.33). Remarkably, 88.8% of these serotype 3 isolates, including the index case, retained full susceptibility to penicillin.
CONCLUSIONS: S. pneumoniae serotype 3 may point to a challenging clinical profile in neonatal EOS, characterized by early and acute onset of respiratory failure, widespread systemic involvement, and a trend toward higher mortality within this cohort. This occurs despite preserved susceptibility to beta-lactam antibiotics, suggesting a potential interplay between capsular features and host vulnerability rather than antimicrobial resistance. Thus, the persistence of this vaccine-included serotype highlights the need for continued epidemiological surveillance.
43069377:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether domain-adaptive self-supervised pretraining of a convolutional neural network on musculoskeletal radiographs improves binary fracture classification and attribution faithfulness relative to ImageNet-pretrained baselines.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study (conducted June 2025 to May 2026) compared three initializations of a ResNet-50 convolutional neural network: supervised ImageNet (control), self-supervised ImageNet (DINO), and DINO further pretrained on 44,029 musculoskeletal radiographs (DINO-Ortho). Each was fine-tuned in three experiments: in-distribution (MURA and FracAtlas), out-of-distribution (5365 external calcaneal radiographs from 1775 patients acquired during 2015-2022), and initial weights (calcaneal fine-tuning). Attribution faithfulness was quantified using Remove and Debias (ROAD) scores from Grad-CAM saliency maps, with higher scores indicating greater faithfulness. AUROCs were compared using DeLong tests, and ROAD scores using Friedman tests with Bonferroni-adjusted post hoc pairwise comparisons.
RESULTS: DINO-Ortho AUROC did not differ significantly from either baseline in any experiment (0.82 [95% confidence interval, 0.79-0.84] in-distribution and 0.95 [0.93-0.96] with initial weights). DINO-Ortho ROAD scores were significantly higher than both baselines in-distribution (20.01 vs 3.70 and 9.35, respectively) and with initial weights (20.41 vs 12.15 and 1.67, respectively, P < 0.001 for all) and higher than control but not DINO out-of-distribution (15.47 vs 3.06 and 16.09, respectively). All models discriminated poorly out-of-distribution (AUROC 0.65 [0.63-0.67], 0.64 [0.63-0.66], and 0.64 [0.63-0.66] for control, DINO, and DINO-Ortho, respectively).
CONCLUSION: With no significant difference in AUROC from either baseline, domain-adapted self-supervised pretraining yielded more faithful attributions than supervised ImageNet pretraining in every experiment and than self-supervised ImageNet pretraining in two of three. No model generalized adequately to unfamiliar anatomy without fine-tuning. Groups fine-tuning on their own musculoskeletal data should therefore consider domain-adapted weights, whose saliency maps more reliably show what drove each prediction, making reliance on irrelevant features easier to detect.
43069469: PurposeLower-limb deformities caused by congenital conditions or unicompartmental knee osteoarthritis are commonly treated with corrective osteotomy. Accurate surgical planning depends on precise anatomical measurements, and three-dimensional (3D) alignment analysis is increasingly used. This study quantified how different landmark, axis, and coordinate system definitions influence 3D angular measurements for assessing lower-limb deformities.MethodsTwenty-four femora and tibiae from the prospective IMI-APPROACH cohort were segmented from low-dose whole-body computed tomography scans. Established definitions of coronal and sagittal planes, anatomical landmarks, and mechanical and anatomical axes were compared. Femoral and tibial deformity parameters were calculated, including the mechanical lateral distal femoral angle (mLDFA), femoral anteversion, mechanical medial proximal tibial angle (mMPTA), posterior proximal tibial angle (PPTA), and tibial torsion. Agreement between methods was evaluated using Bland-Altman analyses.ResultsVariation in coronal plane definitions had minimal influence on femoral measurements (mean 0°). In contrast, alternative landmark and axis definitions introduced systematic bias, particularly for mLDFA. For the tibia, both plane and axis definitions affected measurements, with the largest discrepancies observed for PPTA (mean 2.6°) and tibial torsion (mean 5.6°). Comparisons between whole-leg and bone-specific coordinate systems showed small differences (<1°) across all measurements.ConclusionAnatomical landmark and axis definitions are the main sources of variability in 3D lower-limb angular measurements, whereas plane definitions have limited impact. The substantial differences observed among commonly used femoral and tibial angle definitions underscore the need for standardized 3D measurement approaches in the assessment of lower-limb geometry.
43069486:
BACKGROUND: Heat-sensitive liposomal drug delivery systems (HSLDDS) have faced challenges in translation largely due to inadequate delivery of hyperthermia in early-stage hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). This study evaluates the feasibility of using remote heating implants (RHIs) as a controlled method to deliver hyperthermia ideally suited to improve the performance of HSLDDS.
METHODS: Transcriptomic profiling of HCC cell line SNU423 was performed after exposure to a range of hyperthermic temperatures to identify the heating window that minimized chemotherapy resistance gene expression. RHIs were built and their heating profiles assessed through numerical modeling and performance validated through a phantom model. RHIs were implanted into an in vivo subcutaneous mouse HCC model, and heat-sensitive liposomes loaded with the fluorescent dye DiI (DiI liposomes) were injected intratumorally. Heating was applied using the RHIs to facilitate dye release.
RESULTS: Bulk RNA sequencing revealed significant upregulation of chemotherapy resistance markers including HSP90, HSP27, HSP70, ABCB1, ABCC2, and ABCC5 at 47 °C (high-intensity hyperthermia) compared with 42 °C (low-intensity hyperthermia). RHIs maintained a stable temperature profile of 42.0 ± 0.5 °C at 1 mm and 40.3 ± 0.2 °C at 5 mm in phantoms and 42.0 ± 0.4 °C in vivo. DiI fluorescence intensity was significantly higher with 1-h heating (16.4 ± 2.3) compared with unheated controls (2.1 ± 0.9, p < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: RHIs are a novel heating platform that can be used to maintain a long-term low-intensity hyperthermic environment. This heating can synergize with HSLDDS to enhance drug release against HCC while potentially avoiding chemotherapy resistance pathways induced by high-intensity hyperthermia.
43070096:
OBJECTIVE: To systematically review the evidence on, update existing and create new recommendations for, and identify critical knowledge gaps regarding veterinary resuscitation team communication, composition, and training.
DESIGN: Standardized, systematic evaluation of literature pertinent to veterinary CPR team or "resuscitation team" communication, composition, and training, following the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation methodology. Identified evidence pertinent to prioritized topical questions posed in Population-Intervention-Comparator-Outcome (PICO) format was reviewed by Evidence Evaluators; findings were reconciled by Domain Chairs and Reassessment Campaign on Veterinary Resuscitation Initiative Co-Chairs to arrive at recommendations commensurate with the certainty of evidence, risk-benefit analysis, and perceived feasibility. This process was implemented using a standardized Evidence Profile Worksheet for each question that included an introduction, consensus on science, recommendations, justification of recommendations, and knowledge gaps sections. Recommendations underwent a 4-week comment period among international veterinary stakeholders prior to finalization.
SETTING: Transdisciplinary, international collaboration in university, specialty, and emergency practice.
RESULTS: Five PICO questions on resuscitation team composition, communication, and team training were addressed in this paper. Of the seven recommendations formulated, two took the form of recommendations ("strong" recommendations) and five were suggestions ("weak" recommendations), all supported by low-certainty (one recommendation) or very low-certainty (six recommendations) evidence. Taken together, recommendations pertain to optimal team composition, structured training, and communication.
CONCLUSION: The limited evidence supports a resuscitation team size of 4-8 rescuers led by an experienced veterinary rescuer. Standardized team training, as well as standardized communication among team members, is recommended. The absence of veterinary clinical outcome data for most PICOs revealed important knowledge gaps. Further research is needed to determine whether veterinary resuscitation team preparedness improves clinical CPR performance and outcomes in dogs and cats.
43070245:
PURPOSE: To develop an automatic dipole inversion method for quantitative susceptibility mapping (QSM) that preserves fine anatomical structures without the need for manual regularization-parameter tuning.
THEORY: The original approximate message passing with parameter estimation (AMP-PE) framework models image gradients with a single Laplace prior, which does not fully capture the heavy-tailed gradient distribution of brain susceptibility maps. To address this limitation, we propose a Laplace-Mixture Dipole Inversion (LAMDI) method by incorporating a two-component Laplace mixture prior into the AMP-PE framework with automatic regularization-parameter-estimation.
METHODS: LAMDI was evaluated on a public in vivo dataset and the simulated calcification dataset from QSM Challenge 2.0. Its performance was compared with FANSI, MEDI, and AMP-PE with a single-Laplace prior (AMP-PE-L1) under both standard default and reference-tuned settings. Reproducible code is available at: https://github.com/shuai-huang/lamdi.
RESULTS: On the public in vivo dataset, LAMDI achieved NRMSE and SSIM comparable to AMP-PE-L1 while substantially reducing HFEN. Under reference-based tuning, FANSI and MEDI achieved the best performance for some metrics, but LAMDI remained competitive without requiring reference maps or manual regularization tuning.
CONCLUSION: LAMDI provides an effective and automatic regularization-parameter-estimation alternative for QSM dipole inversion by combining competitive reconstruction accuracy with improved preservation of anatomical details.
43071003:
BACKGROUND: Reference values and validated measurement of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based total fetal lung volume (TFLV) in the late first and early second trimester are limited. Commonly used Meyers and Rypens prediction models were developed using later gestational ages and may not apply to pregnancies imaged at 12-19 weeks.
OBJECTIVE: To determine weekly reference values for TFLV between 12-week and 19-week gestation.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Retrospective study of fetal MRI examinations from 2009 to 2023. Of 311 examinations identified, 128 fetuses met inclusion criteria after exclusions for motion/technical limitations and conditions affecting lung development. Two radiologists manually segmented fetal lungs in two planes to obtain TFLV. Week-specific summary statistics and regression modeling were used to derive reference values and a predictive formula. Observed TFLV was compared with values predicted by the Meyers and Rypens models using t tests. Equivalence testing assessed one-plane versus two-plane average measurements, and interobserver/intraobserver agreement was evaluated using concordance correlation coefficients (CCC).
RESULTS: Mean TFLV increased nonlinearly from 12 weeks to 19 weeks; the best-fit formula was TFLV (mL)=0.000001810×(gestational age in weeks)5.196. Meyers and Rypens models significantly overestimated observed means at all gestational weeks (all P<0.001). One-plane and two-plane average measurements were equivalent (TOST P<0.001), and TFLV did not differ significantly by imaging plane. Agreement was high (interobserver CCC 0.96; intraobserver CCC 0.95).
CONCLUSION: Fetal MRI TFLV measurement in the late first and early second trimester is reproducible using either a one-plane approach or the average of two planes. Observed TFLV values at 12-19 weeks were significantly lower than those predicted by commonly used later-gestation models (Meyers and Rypens). These early-gestation reference values may be used cautiously in selected clinical settings, with prospective validation in independent cohorts warranted.
43071018:
OBJECTIVES: Sarcopenia and visceral fat obesity (VFO) are risk factors for adverse postoperative outcomes in colorectal cancer (CRC). This study investigated perioperative changes in skeletal muscle and adipose tissue in CRC patients and their predictive value for long-term survival.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This cohort study enrolled stage I-III CRC patients who received upfront curative resection. Pre- and postoperative CT scans were obtained to quantify the skeletal muscle index (SMI) for sarcopenia assessment and the visceral-to-subcutaneous fat ratio (VSR) for VFO assessment. Landmark analyses were performed at 3 and 12 months postoperatively. Overall survival (OS) was set as the primary survival endpoint.
RESULTS: A total of 266 patients (median [interquartile range, IQR] age, 55 [50-62] years; 156 males) were included. Landmark Cox regression analyses showed that sarcopenia at baseline and 3 months postoperatively was an independent risk factor for OS (hazard ratio [HR]: 3.408, p = 0.001; HR: 2.497, p = 0.016). VFO at baseline and 3 months postoperatively correlated with poorer OS in the univariable analysis (HR: 1.803, p = 0.026; HR: 1.905, p = 0.030). Integrated prediction models achieved area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.799 at baseline and 0.774 at 3 months postoperatively for OS.
CONCLUSION: Sarcopenia at baseline and 3 months postoperatively is an independent risk factor for inferior OS, whereas VFO is associated with poorer OS only at the univariable level. Combining perioperative sarcopenia and VFO with clinical factors could assist in the prognostic stratification for stage I-III CRC patients following surgical resection.
KEY POINTS: Question The prognostic influence of perioperative changes in CT-derived skeletal muscle and adipose tissues on colorectal cancer survival remains unclear. Findings Sarcopenia and VFO at baseline and the 3-month postoperative landmark are associated with worse overall survival and add incremental prognostic value to conventional clinical risk indicators. Critical relevance statement This work highlights the prognostic value of perioperative CT-derived sarcopenia and VFO for stage I-III CRC, suggesting that opportunistic body composition assessment on routine surveillance scans could provide valuable insights for future clinical risk stratification and management strategies.
43071111:
OBJECTIVE: Symptomatic minor instability of the lateral elbow (SMILE) has recently emerged as an explanation for atraumatic lateral elbow pain and has previously been described using arthroscopy and CT arthrography. This study evaluated the reader-detected frequency and reproducibility of MRI findings associated with the SMILE concept and investigated its applicability to routine elbow MRI.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this retrospective study, consecutive atraumatic elbow MRI examinations performed between January 2020 and May 2024 were independently evaluated by three readers. MRI findings associated with the SMILE concept were assessed together with extra-articular abnormalities of static and dynamic stabilizers. Agreement for individual MRI findings was assessed using Fleiss' κ, while agreement for the MRI-based SMILE sum score was evaluated using pairwise quadratically weighted Cohen's κ and a three-reader intraclass correlation coefficient.
RESULTS: Elbow MRI examinations from 122 patients with atraumatic lateral elbow pain were included (mean age 48.0 ± 14.1 years; 68 men). The MRI-based SMILE sum score demonstrated substantial-to-almost perfect pairwise agreement (weighted κ = 0.674-0.861) with good overall three-reader agreement (ICC = 0.772). Among the individual SMILE items, humeroradial asymmetry demonstrated the highest reproducibility, whereas trochlear ridge chondromalacia showed the lowest. Extra-articular abnormalities demonstrated substantial-to-almost perfect agreement, particularly epicondylitis and lateral ligament abnormalities.
CONCLUSION: MRI enables reproducible assessment of instability-associated abnormalities in patients with atraumatic lateral elbow pain, supporting the feasibility of an MRI-based SMILE concept in clinical routine. Besides intra-articular findings, MRI reproducibly depicts extra-articular pathologies, thereby broadening the imaging assessment of lateral elbow pain.
KEY POINTS: Question Can MRI reproducibly assess SMILE-associated abnormalities in atraumatic elbows? Findings MRI-based evaluation of SMILE-associated abnormalities and extra-articular stabilizer pathologies was highly reproducible across three readers. Clinical relevance MRI allows reproducible assessment of SMILE-associated and extra-articular abnormalities in atraumatic lateral elbow pain and may broaden the imaging assessment beyond CT arthrography.
43071112:
OBJECTIVES: We aimed to capture the current practice of intracranial and extracranial carotid Vessel Wall Imaging (VWI) across European institutions, and to identify practical, technical or educational obstacles to its successful implementation.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: An online survey on the use of VWI, endorsed by European Society of Neuroradiology (ESNR) in collaboration with American Society of Neuroradiology (ASNR) was performed between April and July 2023. The survey was anonymous and distributed via e-mail to ESNR members and associated National Societies. Only one member per institution could respond. Response data are summarized as frequencies and percentages.
RESULTS: There were 200 valid institutional respondents. The majority (84%) were neuroradiologists; 67.5% came from an academic hospital. Most respondents relied on vendor assistance for technical protocol development. Overall, 33% practiced only intracranial VWI, whereas 3% only extracranial; the majority (48.5%) did both. Both intracranial and extracranial-VWI were most commonly performed on average 1-2 times per month and for clinical use. Main intracranial and extracranial VWI indications were differentiation of vasculopathies (97.5%) and characterization/detection of dissection (76.5%), respectively. Interestingly, only 62.5% of intracranial VWI-users applied sequences with specific blood-flow suppression. A large proportion of intracranial (77.3%) and extra-cranial (72.4%) VWI-users indicated an interest in learning more about the technique.
CONCLUSION: VWI is regularly practiced on a clinical ground across European institutions, particularly in academic hospitals; however, the results of this survey stress the need for further education and harmonization to promote VWI successful use.
KEY POINTS: Question We explored the current state of VWI practice in Europe focusing on indications, frequency of use, adherence to technical recommendations and confidence in interpretation. Findings Our survey highlights VWI is often applied without appropriate technical requirements; users frequently express lack of confidence regarding technical aspects and interpretation of VWI studies. Clinical relevance Real-life data from VWI practice in Europe highlight important shortcomings (potentially causing clinical misdiagnosis of vessel-wall pathology), which need to be addressed with further education and call for a more widespread network of technical and clinical support.
43071113:
OBJECTIVES: To construct an imaging workflow using 4D DECT for the localization and characterization of parathyroid adenomas.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This IRB-approved, HIPAA-compliant retrospective study included patients who underwent DECT of the neck between June 1, 2023, and May 30, 2024, with pathology-confirmed parathyroid adenomas. A research fellow with 12 years of clinical radiology experience obtained attenuation of parathyroid adenoma, thyroid, lymph node on non-contrast, virtual non-contrast, 70 keV and 55 keV dual-energy CT, and iodine maps for arterial and venous phases. Two additional clinical fellows repeated the measurements to evaluate the interobserver variability. Conspicuity of the lesion was calculated by contrast-to-noise ratio of the parathyroid relative to the thyroid gland. Statistical analysis employed the Friedman test, Mann-Whitney U tests, one-way ANOVA, and ROC curves.
RESULTS: The study included 40 patients (31 females; mean age 57.7 ± 13.4 years) with 55 confirmed parathyroid adenomas. The highest contrast-to-noise ratio was seen in arterial-phase iodine concentration (5.7; IQR: 3.5-9.6). Non-contrast (AUC: 0.91), using cutoff value < 54 HU, achieved 81.8 (71.8-91.8)% sensitivity and 95 (88.6-100)% specificity for differentiation of parathyroid from thyroid, and 55 keV arterial (AUC: 0.97), using cutoff value of > 150 HU on 55 keV arterial phase achieved 94.5 (88.4-100) % sensitivity and 90 (80.8-99.2) % specificity for differentiation of parathyroid from lymph node. Combining cutoff values and within-patient pairwise comparison between the lesion, thyroid, and lymph node increased sensitivity to 98% for the characterization of parathyroid adenoma.
CONCLUSION: Workflow strategy using a combination of cutoff and within-patient pairwise analysis on non-contrast, 55 keV arterial and venous-phase DECT achieved high sensitivity for detection and characterization of parathyroid adenoma.
KEY POINTS: Question What is a systematic imaging approach for image review and measurement for identification and characterization of parathyroid adenoma on multiphasic dual-energy CT? Findings A systematic workflow combining arterial-phase iodine mapping, non-contrast, 55 keV arterial threshold cutoffs, and within-patient pairwise analysis achieved 98.2% sensitivity for parathyroid adenoma. Clinical relevance The proposed quantitative workflow for the identification and characterization of parathyroid adenoma in multiphasic dual-energy CT may enhance preoperative localization of suspected parathyroid adenomas. Its effects on surgical approach, procedure time, cost, and morbidity require prospective evaluation.
43071122:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the performance of a low-dose high-resolution photon-counting detector CT (PCD-CT) protocol for evaluating joint space width (JSW) and joint space narrowing (JSN) in peripheral arthritis, including inter-reader reliability and comparison with digital radiography (DR) and digital tomosynthesis (DT), using standard-dose PCD-CT as the reference standard.
METHODS: Twenty patients (forty hands) were examined using DR, DT, and low- and standard-dose ultra-high-resolution PCD-CT. JSW was measured, and JSN was subjectively scored in the radioulnar, radiocarpal, intercarpal, carpometacarpal, metacarpal, metacarpophalangeal, and interphalangeal joints. Two readers independently assessed all examinations, and inter-reader reliability was evaluated. DR, DT, and low-dose PCD-CT were compared with standard-dose PCD-CT. Effective doses were calculated from dose-length product and dose-area product values. Statistical analysis included linear mixed-effects models and one-way ANOVA.
RESULTS: Inter-reader reliability for JSW measurements was excellent across all modalities (ICC 0.988-0.995; 95% CI 0.987-0.995). Compared with standard-dose PCD-CT, DR significantly overestimated JSW (mean difference + 0.279 mm, p < 0.001) and underestimated JSN severity. No significant differences were observed between low- and standard-dose PCD-CT for JSW (mean difference - 0.016 mm, p = 0.302) or JSN scores (mean difference + 0.019, p = 0.533). DT and standard-dose PCD-CT had higher effective doses than DR and low-dose PCD-CT, with no significant dose difference between DR and low-dose PCD-CT (p = 0.993).
CONCLUSION: Low-dose PCD-CT demonstrated excellent inter-reader reliability and close agreement with standard-dose PCD-CT for JSW and JSN assessment. Compared with DR, it provided joint space measurements more consistent with standard-dose PCD-CT at a comparable effective radiation dose.
43071132:
PURPOSE: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA) is an aggressive malignancy associated with poor prognosis and limited treatment options. Selective internal radiation therapy (SIRT), also known as transarterial radioembolization (TARE), may improve locoregional tumor control and enhance antitumor immune response, increasing the efficacy of systemic treatment. This study evaluates the efficacy and safety of upfront TARE followed by cisplatin, gemcitabine and durvalumab in treatment-naïve patients with unresectable liver-predominant iCCA.
PROTOCOL: PM-CARE is a prospective, multicenter, single-arm phase II study. Treatment-naïve eligible patients with upfront unresectable liver-predominant iCCA preserved liver function (Child-Pugh A), Eastern Cooperative Oncology performance status 0-1. Following angiographic mapping and technetium-99 m macroaggregated albumin (99mTc-MAA) simulation, participants undergo personalized dosimetry-guided SIRT. Systemic treatment with cisplatin, gemcitabine and durvalumab will start 21 days after TARE and administered for six cycles. Co-primary endpoints are overall response rate (ORR) at 6 months according to modified Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (mRECIST) and safety. Secondary endpoints include ORR on target lesion and overall by RECIST 1.1, progression-free survival, overall survival, quality-of-life. Tissue and blood-based biomarkers including tumor mutational burden, circulating tumor DNA, immune profiling and cytokine characterization will be explored.
STATISTICS: A sample size of 22 achieves 90.9% power to detect a difference of 0.30 in response rate using a one-sided exact test with a significance level of 0.05 at the primary endpoint. The drop-out inflated enrollment sample size is 28 participants.
DISCUSSION: This study will provide prospective efficacy and safety data of upfront TARE combined with current first-line chemoimmunotherapy in patients with unresectable liver-predominant iCCA.
CLINICAL TRIALS REGISTRATION: Clinical Trials.gov NCT06375915.
43071202:
BACKGROUND: Epilepsy affects approximately 50 million people worldwide, with disproportionate burden in low- and middle-income countries where access to specialized care remains limited. Despite advances in neuroimaging and electrophysiology, accurate diagnosis, etiological classification, and timely identification of surgical candidates remain major clinical challenges. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising tool to integrate multimodal data and support clinical decision-making across the epilepsy care continuum.
OBJECTIVE: To systematically assess and meta-analytically quantify the evidence on AI applications for diagnosis, etiological classification, outcome prediction, surgical candidate selection, and workflow optimization in epilepsy.
METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, with protocol registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251117939). Searches were performed in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, Cochrane Library, and SciELO for studies published between January 2014 and March 2026. Eligible studies included original research in human subjects with epilepsy applying AI or machine learning models and reporting at least one quantitative performance metric with internal or external validation. Study quality was assessed using PROBAST. Pooled estimates of Area Under the Curve (AUC), sensitivity, and specificity were derived using DerSimonian-Laird random-effects models across four clinical task groups: diagnosis, classification, outcome prediction, and surgical referral.
RESULTS: From 423 identified records, 102 studies met inclusion criteria. Research output increased markedly after 2018, peaking in 2021 and 2024, with geographic concentration in China (n = 31) and the United States (n = 11). Electroencephalography and MRI were the dominant input modalities, and Support Vector Machines (n = 41) and Convolutional Neural Networks (n = 22) were the most frequently employed algorithms. Most studies relied exclusively on internal validation, and external validation remained scarce across all domains. PROBAST assessment revealed high risk of bias in the majority of studies, particularly in the participant and analysis domains. Meta-analysis demonstrated strong discriminative performance across all groups: the classification group achieved the highest pooled AUC (0.929; 95% CI: 0.837-0.971), followed by diagnosis (0.899; 95% CI: 0.859-0.929), surgical referral (0.895; 95% CI: 0.870-0.916), and outcome prediction (0.807; 95% CI: 0.740-0.861). Sensitivity was highest in the diagnosis group (0.885; 95% CI: 0.840-0.918) and lowest in surgical referral (0.729; 95% CI: 0.681-0.771), a clinically relevant asymmetry given the high cost of missing true surgical candidates in drug-resistant epilepsy. Substantial variability was observed across studies, reflecting differences in data modalities, AI architectures, and sample sizes, and indicating that pooled estimates should be interpreted with caution rather than as fixed, generalizable performance figures.
CONCLUSION: AI demonstrates robust and clinically meaningful performance across the spectrum of epilepsy care, particularly for diagnosis and surgical planning. However, uniformly high between-study heterogeneity, predominant reliance on internal validation, variable study quality, and underrepresentation of low- and middle-income country contexts limit the generalizability of current evidence and hinder clinical translation. Prospective multicenter studies, standardized reporting, and context-adapted implementation strategies are essential to realize the full clinical potential that this body of evidence consistently demonstrates.
43071284:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (MRONJ) is a potentially severe complication of antiresorptive therapy, but its epidemiology in male patients remains poorly characterized because most evidence derives from mixed-sex or predominantly female populations. This systematic review and meta-analysis estimated MRONJ prevalence in antiresorptive-treated men and evaluated differences by clinical setting and treatment class.
RECENT FINDINGS: Following PRISMA guidelines, we searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science through May 31, 2026 (PROSPERO: CRD420261433511). Forty-six studies involving 506,678 male patients were included, with 44 datasets contributing to the quantitative synthesis. The pooled MRONJ prevalence was 7.0% (95% CI 4.6-10.5%), with extreme heterogeneity (I² = 99.2%) and a wide prediction interval (0.5-54.9%). Prevalence was substantially higher in oncologic than osteoporotic populations (7.2% vs. 0.4%; p < 0.0001). Prostate cancer cohorts showed a numerically higher prevalence than other oncologic cohorts (13.8% vs. 7.4%), although the difference was not significant. No significant difference was observed between intravenous bisphosphonates and denosumab (14.2% vs. 10.7%; p = 0.19). Cumulative exposure and oral inflammatory burden were associated with MRONJ, whereas structured preventive dental care appeared protective. MRONJ prevalence in men is clinically relevant but highly context-dependent. Oncologic populations show substantially higher prevalence than osteoporotic populations, whereas current evidence does not demonstrate a significant difference between denosumab and intravenous bisphosphonates. MRONJ risk should therefore be interpreted according to treatment indication, cumulative exposure, and clinical setting rather than through a single global estimate. Standardized definitions and male-specific reporting are needed to improve risk stratification.
43071296:
Variability in periprosthetic DXA limits reproducibility and clinical translation. This multisociety RAND/UCLA consensus provides a standardized framework for ppDXA acquisition, analysis, ROI definition, longitudinal LSC-based interpretation, and structured reporting for hip and knee arthroplasty. The framework supports auditable measurement and reporting, does not advocate universal routine ppDXA screening, and is not intended to establish outcome-validated periprosthetic BMD thresholds.
PURPOSE: Periprosthetic dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (ppDXA) is increasingly used to measure areal bone mineral density (BMD) around hip and knee implants and to characterize longitudinal changes associated with periprosthetic bone remodeling. However, variability in acquisition, analysis, region-of-interest (ROI) definition, metal-artifact handling, and reporting limits reproducibility and hinders clinical and research implementation. This multisociety consensus aimed to develop a standardized methodological framework for ppDXA acquisition, analysis, reporting, and longitudinal interpretation in hip and knee arthroplasty.
METHODS: A multinational collaboration of scientific societies from Mexico, Colombia, Argentina, and Spain convened a 21-member multidisciplinary panel with expertise in orthopedic surgery, clinical densitometry, medical physics, bone biology, epidemiology, biostatistics, and consensus methodology. A targeted evidence review and narrative synthesis informed candidate statements on the ppDXA workflow. Statements were rated, discussed, and refined using the modified RAND/UCLA Appropriateness Method. Recommendations with high agreement were organized into six conceptual domains: quality assurance and precision; patient preparation and positioning; scan acquisition; ROI definition and analysis; longitudinal assessment; and reporting and clinical contextualization.
RESULTS: The consensus establishes minimum and optimal standards for site-level quality assurance, implant documentation, joint-specific positioning, scan parameters, metal-removal settings, implant-anchored ROI schemes, ROI-specific precision assessment, least significant change (LSC)-based longitudinal interpretation, structured reporting, and clinical contextualization. A Minimum Dataset for Reporting and practical ROI templates are provided. An exploratory therapy-aware Green-Amber-Red interpretive framework is proposed to support structured contextual interpretation and prospective evaluation of periprosthetic BMD trajectories, in conjunction with technical validity, clinical findings, imaging, systemic bone health, and treatment context.
CONCLUSIONS: These multisociety RAND/UCLA consensus recommendations provide a standardized framework to reduce avoidable technical variability, improve reproducibility, and support auditable use of ppDXA in research and selected clinical workflows. It does not advocate universal routine ppDXA screening for all patients undergoing hip or knee arthroplasty and is intended to standardize measurement and reporting rather than to establish outcome-validated diagnostic, prognostic, or therapeutic periprosthetic BMD thresholds.
43071370:
BACKGROUND: Differentiated thyroid carcinoma (DTC) is the most common endocrine malignancy in children, adolescents, and young adults (CAYA) with survival exceeding 98%. Real-world data on long-term nonmalignant chronic health conditions (CHCs) remain scarce.
OBJECTIVE: To characterize long-term nonmalignant CHCs in CAYA DTC survivors relative to cancer-free controls and explore associations with radioactive iodine (RAI) exposure.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used Clalit Health Services electronic health records (Israel, 1982-2022) comparing 5267 DTC survivors (diagnosed at age < 40) with 21,062 matched cancer-free controls. Incident CHCs occurring ≥2 years post-DTC diagnosis/index-date were assessed across metabolic, cardiovascular, renal, hepatic, gastrointestinal, pulmonary, skeletal, autoimmune/rheumatologic, and emotional domains and were evaluated using Cox proportional hazards models to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RAI subgroup analyses were exploratory.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 14.7 years (interquartile range 8.8-23.2), the risk of developing ≥1 CHC did not differ significantly between DTC survivors and cancer-free controls (54.4% vs. 52.0%; HR, 1.05; 95% CI, 1.00-1.11; p = 0.066). Survivors were more likely to experience multimorbidity (≥2 CHCs 35.7% vs. 32.0%) and had higher risks of several specific organ-system conditions: osteoporosis (HR 1.33; 95% CI: 1.14-1.56), chronic kidney disease (HR 1.61; 95% CI: 1.32-1.96), gastroesophageal disorders (HR 1.35; 95% CI: 1.26-1.45), dyslipidemia (HR 1.23; 95% CI: 1.16-1.32), and hypertension (HR 1.21; 95% CI: 1.13-1.29). Pulmonary, cardiovascular, autoimmune, hepatic, and clinically diagnosed emotional disorders did not differ significantly between groups. Exploratory analyses revealed a dose-dependent RAI risk gradient (1 course: HR 1.20; 95% CI: 1.06-1.35; ≥2 courses: HR 1.33; 95% CI: 1.16-1.52).
CONCLUSIONS: Despite excellent overall survival, CAYA DTC survivors face a modest overall increase in CHC risk alongside notably greater multisystem morbidity. RAI-associated risk trends are exploratory and need further research. These findings support risk-adapted therapy and structured long-term survivorship monitoring.
43071438:
BACKGROUND: Risk stratification systems are essential for individualized management of differentiated thyroid cancer. This study compared the 2015 and 2025 American Thyroid Association (ATA) guidelines in predicting long-term recurrence risk in patients with papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC).
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 2677 adult patients with PTC who underwent total thyroidectomy at a tertiary academic center between 2010 and 2015. Patients were stratified according to the 2015 and 2025 ATA guidelines. The primary outcome was structural persistent or recurrent disease (clinical event).
RESULTS: Risk distribution differed significantly between the two systems, with 526 patients (19.6%) upstaged under the 2025 ATA guidelines. Compared with the 2015 ATA system, the 2025 ATA system assigned fewer patients to the low-risk group (27.8% vs. 15.1%) and more to the high-risk group (9.9% vs. 16.8%). By the 2015 ATA, 1668 patients (62.3%) were classified as intermediate-risk. By the 2025 ATA, 882 (32.9%) and 940 patients (35.1%) were classified as low-intermediate- and intermediate-high-risk, respectively. Over a median follow-up of 9.6 years (interquartile range: 6.6-12.2 years), 132 (4.9%) patients experienced clinical events. Event rates among low-risk patients were 1.2% under the 2015 ATA system and 0.7% under the 2025 ATA system. Among intermediate-risk patients, the event rate was 4.4% with the 2015 ATA guidelines, compared with 0.9% and 5.3% in the low-intermediate and intermediate-high groups, respectively, under the 2025 ATA system. Among high-risk patients, event rates were 18.5% and 15.7% under the 2015 and 2025 ATA systems, respectively. Harrell's C-index was 0.711 ([confidence interval or CI, 0.672-0.750]) for the 2015 ATA classification and 0.781 ([CI, 0.748-0.814]) for the 2025 ATA classification, with a difference of 0.069 ([CI, 0.042-0.097]; p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: The 2025 ATA risk stratification system was more granular, showed improved discrimination, and more precisely identified patients at very low risk of recurrence. However, a substantial proportion of patients were reclassified into higher-risk categories, which may have implications for potential overtreatment and warrants careful consideration.
43071506:
OBJECTIVES: To assess the predictive performance of angiogenic factors and fetal Doppler, alone and in combination, for composite adverse perinatal outcome (CAPO) in late-onset small-for-gestational age (SGA) and fetal growth restriction (FGR), in both cases with and those without pre-eclampsia (PE), to determine whether these markers predict adverse outcomes beyond their established association with PE. As a secondary objective, we evaluated their performance for predicting subsequent PE.
METHODS: This was a retrospective observational cohort study conducted at Vall d'Hebron University Hospital, Barcelona, Spain, between January 2016 and January 2022. The study population comprised singleton pregnancies with an estimated fetal weight < 10th percentile, diagnosed with late-onset fetal smallness between 32 + 0 and 37 + 6 weeks' gestation, with available fetal Doppler ultrasound data and angiogenic factor measurements obtained at diagnosis. Placental growth factor (PlGF), soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1 (sFlt-1) and fetal Doppler indices were measured at initial assessment. CAPO was defined as the presence of at least one of the following: 5-min Apgar score < 7, umbilical cord arterial pH < 7.0, neonatal intensive care unit admission > 48 h, stillbirth, neonatal death, respiratory distress syndrome, bronchopulmonary dysplasia, neonatal sepsis, necrotizing enterocolitis, Stage-III-IV retinopathy of prematurity, Grade-III-IV intraventricular hemorrhage, periventricular leukomalacia or hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy. Predictive performance for CAPO was assessed using receiver-operating-characteristics (ROC)-curve analysis and area under the ROC curve (AUC) comparisons for fetal Doppler and angiogenic factors, alone and in combination, within logistic regression models. Prediction of subsequent PE after enrolment and before delivery was evaluated similarly as a prespecified secondary analysis. Sensitivity, false-positive rate, positive predictive value and negative predictive value were calculated. All analyses were stratified according to PE development at any time before delivery.
RESULTS: Overall, 754 pregnancies with late-onset fetal smallness were included. PE was present at diagnosis in 21/754 (2.8%) cases and developed later in 23 (3.1%) cases. CAPO occurred in 84 (11.1%) cases. In the overall cohort, the sFlt-1/PlGF ratio showed the highest predictive performance for CAPO (AUC, 0.791 (95% CI, 0.721-0.861)), outperforming fetal Doppler alone (AUC, 0.649 (95% CI, 0.566-0.732); P = 0.005).
