This was not significantly different from the performance of PlGF alone (AUC, 0.784 (95% CI, 0.711-0.856); P = 0.810). In pregnancies without PE, the predictive performance of individual angiogenic markers alone was lower compared with that in the overall cohort, and performance was similar across markers, with no significant differences between the sFlt-1/PlGF ratio, PlGF and fetal Doppler, alone or in combination. In pregnancies with PE at any time, the predictive performance of all markers was not significantly different from that observed in the overall cohort, and all markers showed comparable predictive performance for CAPO, with no clear superiority. In the prespecified secondary analysis for prediction of subsequent PE, the sFlt-1/PlGF ratio alone was the single marker that achieved the highest predictive performance (AUC, 0.884 (95% CI, 0.807-0.960)), outperforming both PlGF alone and fetal Doppler alone. Combining fetal Doppler with angiogenic factors reduced false-positive rates but did not improve sensitivity.
CONCLUSION: This study confirms the predictive value of angiogenic factors, particularly the sFlt-1/PlGF ratio, for identifying CAPO and subsequent PE in late-onset SGA/FGR. Compared with the overall cohort, the predictive performance of PlGF and the sFlt-1/PlGF ratio was significantly lower in pregnancies without PE, whereas no significant difference was observed for fetal Doppler. Nevertheless, in pregnancies without PE, angiogenic markers showed predictive performance comparable to that of fetal Doppler. These findings suggest that angiogenic factors reflect underlying placental insufficiency rather than PE alone, supporting their integration into the clinical assessment of late-onset SGA/FGR in both pregnancies with and those without PE. © 2026 International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology.
43071733:
BACKGROUND: Fresh frozen plasma (FFP) administered after severe isolated traumatic brain injury (TBI) has been shown to affect subsequent neurological recovery. One component of FFP, antithrombin III (AT3), demonstrates anti-inflammatory effects on the injured brain and may be a key FFP element that supports post-TBI recovery. We hypothesized that AT3 better improves cognition following severe, isolated TBI when compared with FFP.
METHODS: Male CD1 mice (n=29) underwent sham craniectomy (S) or craniectomy followed by severe TBI via controlled cortical impact. Mice received saline (placebo, P), FFP (10 mL/kg), or AT3 (250 IU/kg) 30 minutes after injury. Morris water maze exercises on days 6 to 14 characterized cued/spatial learning and memory. Decreased latency/distance and increased frequency/duration across four zones [zone 5 (escape platform), zone 6/zone 7 (concentric circular areas surrounding zone 5)], and zone 1 (quadrant containing zone 5) indicated superior learning and memory. The Garcia Neurological Test (GNT) allowed scoring of global animal neurological function following surgery on days 1 to 14.
RESULTS: Mice treated with FFP or AT3 had consistent improvements in GNT scores back to sham levels across all the post-TBI experimental period from day 1 through 14 (p<0.01). Cued learning was unaffected by FFP or AT3. Spatial learning was consistently worsened by FFP but not by AT3, which, in comparison, demonstrated reduced latency to zones 5, 6, and 7 (p<0.01). FFP had no effect on memory, but AT3 consistently improved memory, decreasing latency to zones 1, 5, 6, and 7 (p<0.01) and increasing frequency into zones 1, 6, and 7 (p<0.01). There were no differences in brain or lung edema between groups.
CONCLUSION: FFP after severe TBI improves global neurological recovery but appears to worsen spatial learning. Instead, AT3 confers better neurological recuperation, particularly through improved memory recovery. Further inquiry is warranted to identify beneficial and deleterious components of commonly transfused FFP to enhance recovery after severe blunt TBI.
43071802:
INTRODUCTION: Although increasingly recognized in young sport participants, epiphyseal stress injuries (epiphyseal PSIs) of the elbow and Panner's disease are rare and remain unclearly defined in etiopathogenetic, clinical and imaging terms. This review aimed to clarify their differences, characterize their extent and severity, and review their diagnostic and therapeutic management.
SOURCES OF DATA: Separate Scopus and PubMed searches identified studies involving athletes younger than 19 years, with no date or language restrictions. Two reviewers independently screened the records in Rayyan, each blinded to the other's decisions. Disagreements were resolved through discussion. The two searches yielded 27 condition-specific study entries: 20 on epiphyseal PSIs and 7 on Panner's disease. The epiphyseal PSI studies reported 688 participants, whereas the Panner's disease studies reported 15; one publication contributed to both review streams. Data were summarized descriptively.
AREAS OF CONTROVERSY: The exact pathogenesis of Panner's disease remains controversial, including the role of vascular injury and its relationship with osteochondritis dissecans.
AREAS OF AGREEMENT: Evidence is limited by heterogeneous study design, including many case reports, and scarce long-term prospective data.
GROWING POINTS: Repetitive mechanical loading is closely associated with epiphyseal PSIs and may also contribute to Panner's disease, although the two conditions appear to represent distinct entities. Panner's disease affects children and adolescents and is typically self-limiting, whereas epiphyseal PSIs occur during adolescence and may require surgery.
AREAS TIMELY FOR DEVELOPING RESEARCH: Further prospective studies with standardized criteria and long-term follow-up are needed to better define the natural history and optimize management strategies.
43071910:
BACKGROUND: Previous studies have shown that atrial fibrillation (AF) cardioversion may reverse atrial remodeling.
PURPOSE: To investigate whether LGE-MRI-assessed left atrial (LA) fibrosis regresses after persistent atrial fibrillation (PersAF) cardioversion to sinus rhythm, and to analyze the relationship between fibrosis change and traditional volume-based measures of LA reverse remodeling.
STUDY TYPE: Prospective.
POPULATION: Fifty-three patients following cardioversion for PersAF.
FIELD STRENGTH/SEQUENCE: 3 T, cine balanced steady-state free precession cine and 3D inversion recovery gradient-echo sequences.
ASSESSMENT: MRI was performed 1-3 days after AF-cardioversion (early follow-up), and again at 3 months (late follow-up). Image analysis was performed by two observers using CVI42 and ADAS software. Data were compared between early and late follow-up. LA fibrosis on LGE-MRI was categorized by the image intensity ratio (IIR): core zone (IIR > 1.61) and border zone (0.97 < IIR ≤ 1.61). Maximum LA volume (LAVmax), LA ejection fraction (LAEF), LA strain, and left ventricular mass were assessed from cine data. An LAVmax reduction ≥ 15% from early to late follow-up defined LA reverse remodeling.
STATISTICAL TESTS: Early and late follow-up data were compared using paired t-tests. Multivariable analysis was performed to assess the associations between changes in LA border and core zone and other LA parameters. A p-value < 0.05 was considered significant.
RESULTS: Seventeen patients had volume-based LA reverse. Compared with early follow-up, LA border zone (22.2 [11.8-37.0] vs. 18.1 [11.8-25.2] cm2) and core zone (0.9 ± 3.0 vs. 0.1 ± 0.6 cm2) were significantly decreased. LAVmax was significantly reduced (97.2 ± 26.3 vs. 109.4 ± 32.7 mL), and LAEF (44.1 ± 15.8 vs. 32.2% ± 13.1%) and LA strain (27.4 ± 14.1 vs. 18.2% ± 8.6%) improved. Volume-based LA reverse remodeling was unrelated to ΔLA border (p = 0.955) or Δcore zone (p = 0.301).
DATA CONCLUSION: PersAF conversion to sinus rhythm resulted in a reduction in LGE-defined atrial enhancement, LAV reduction, and improved function. Fibrosis regression was independent of volume-based LA reverse remodeling.
EVIDENCE LEVEL: 2.
TECHNICAL EFFICACY: Stage 4.
43072635:
PURPOSE: To develop imaging and consensus-based guidelines for the application of multimodal imaging in the diagnosis and management of ocular syphilis.
DESIGN: Consensus agreement guided by evidence-based literature and expert committee deliberation using nominal group technique (NGT).
PARTICIPANTS: International uveitis specialists and retina specialists participating in the Multimodal Imaging in Uveitis (MUV) taskforce.
METHODS: A subcommittee of experts formed by the MUV reviewed published literature on imaging in ocular syphilis and collected multimodal imaging datasets of serology-confirmed cases based on the Standardized Uveitis Nomenclature (SUN) criteria. Three clinical phenotypes of posterior uveitis were included: acute syphilitic posterior placoid chorioretinitis (ASPPC), syphilitic multifocal retinitis, and syphilitic necrotizing retinitis. Imaging modalities included color fundus photograph (CFP), optical coherence tomography (OCT), fundus autofluorescence (FAF), fundus fluorescein angiography (FFA), indocyanine green angiography (ICGA), and OCT angiography (OCTA). Through structured NGT sessions, the committee developed consensus-based descriptors of active and inactive syphilitic retinitis and imaging features associated with disease activity. The imaging guidelines were reviewed and voted upon by the full MUV taskforce.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Identification of globally acceptable multimodal imaging features of syphilitic retinitis; identification of modality-specific features of disease activity; consensus on the preferred imaging modalities for diagnosis and monitoring of disease activity and resolution.
RESULTS: The experts agreed that CFP, OCT and FAF were the most important diagnostic and follow-up imaging modalities for documenting pattern, extent, and borders of syphilitic lesions across all three disease phenotypes. CFP was helpful in identifying the characteristic morphological appearance of ASPPC, multifocal and necrotizing retinitis. In ASPPC, OCT demonstrates features of granular hyper-reflectivity of the retinal pigment epithelium with small nodular elevations, and a disrupted ellipsoid zone. FAF revealed more extensive hypo and hyper-autofluorescent areas of involvement than were clinically apparent on CFP, and these alterations regressed following initiation of treatment. FFA, ICGA and OCTA have limited role in diagnosing or assessing disease activity for all three phenotypes.
CONCLUSIONS: The MUV imaging guidelines for ocular syphilis extend existing diagnostic frameworks by systematically integrating multimodal imaging features for identification of specific phenotypes and for disease monitoring. CFP, FAF and OCT are important for detecting and monitoring of ASPPC, syphilitic multifocal retinitis, and syphilitic necrotizing retinitis.
43072712:
OBJECTIVE: Several outcome prediction tools exist to support decision making for patients undergoing major lower limb amputation (MLLA). However, most predict a single outcome, are derived from registry level data, and lack external validation. The present study aimed to develop clinically focussed, multi-outcome prediction tools using granular regional data with immediate external validation on an international database.
METHODS: This study involved development, and internal and external validation of multivariable binomial and multinomial regression prediction models. All patients undergoing MLLA for ischaemic or diabetic indications between 1 January 2013 and 1 July 2023 at a single regional vascular hub were used for model development. Clinically focussed logistic multivariable binomial and multinomial regression models were developed predicting 30 day and 1 year mortality and revision, 30 day major morbidity or mortality, and best mobility achieved (binary and 3 category). Model complexity, crossvalidated receiver operating curve (ROC) discrimination and calibration were assessed and optimised, with the best performing models undergoing external validation on PERCEIVE study data. External validity was assessed using discrimination and calibration statistics, with one revision attempt permitted.
RESULTS: The development dataset included 609 patients (75.2% men, median age 69 years). Internal crossvalidated ROC values were 0.774 for 30 day mortality, 0.752 for 1 year mortality, 0.679 for 30 day revision, 0.707 for 1 year revision, 0.699 for 30 day major morbidity or mortality, 0.876 for binary best ambulation, and 0.752 for 3 category best ambulation predictions. All models were well calibrated. On external validation the ROC values were 0.616, 0.722, 0.617, 0.488, 0.697, 0.643, and 0.602, respectively.
CONCLUSION: The prediction models performed well for internal "regional" patient outcomes, especially for mortality and ambulation. On external validation, like other models externally validated on the PERCEIVE data, they failed to generalise to the wider population undergoing MLLA, except for 1 year mortality. Predicting patient outcomes from pre-operative variables remains challenging; however, regional level modelling may provide better performance over more general prediction tools.
43072713:
OBJECTIVES: The aim of this review was to synthesise evidence on patient priorities, preferences for treatment, and shared decision making experiences in lower extremity peripheral artery disease (PAD) treatment decisions across intermittent claudication, chronic limb threatening ischaemia, and amputation level contexts.
DATA SOURCES: Key databases including MEDLINE and Embase.
REVIEW METHODS: This was a systematic review (PROSPERO ID: CRD420251106155). Key databases including MEDLINE and Embase were searched for English language studies published from 1 January 2000 to 17 December 2025. Eligible studies included adults with symptomatic PAD, reporting experiences, information needs, priorities, or decision making related to PAD treatment. Two reviewers independently screened studies, resolving disagreements by consensus with a third reviewer. Study quality was assessed using design appropriate tools. Qualitative and quantitative findings were integrated using a structured thematic narrative approach.
RESULTS: Thirty-four studies were included in the systematic review, comprising qualitative, mixed methods, observational registry or cohort, and stated preference studies, and one stepped wedge cluster randomised trial. Most qualitative and cohort studies were rated moderate to high quality. Participant reporting in the 34 studies was limited: seven studies (21%) did not report sex, two (6%) recruited men only, and most mixed sex studies recruited predominantly men; and 18 (53%) did not report ethnicity and, where reported, participants were predominantly White. Across heterogeneous studies, recurring patient valued domains included pain relief, walking ability, independence, emotional wellbeing, function, quality of life, treatment burden, risk, and uncertainty. Decision making processes were shaped by preferred involvement, trust, communication, clarity of options, and continuity of care. Studies identified a mismatch between patients' preferred and experienced decisional roles, with reported involvement lower than desired. Stated preference evidence showed heterogeneity in risk tolerance and treatment trade offs. Trial evidence reported improvements in shared decision making measures and patient knowledge after structured decision support and clinician training.
CONCLUSION: Patient valued outcomes and treatment trade offs vary across lower extremity PAD contexts and individuals. Shared decision making may help incorporate these priorities into treatment decisions, supported by tailored information, continuity of care, clinician training, and decision support tools.
43072896: Excimer laser coronary atherectomy (ELCA) was introduced over 4 decades ago for the modification and debulking of coronary atherosclerotic plaque. However, the adoption of ELCA has remained low, in part because of misperceptions around and limited understanding of its mechanism of action, the disappointing early experience with the device, and limited awareness of the significant body of safety and efficacy data generated after optimization of catheter design and procedural methods. The introduction of other techniques, such as rotational atherectomy, orbital atherectomy, and lately, intravascular lithotripsy, has further contributed to uncertainty regarding the optimal placement and value of ELCA within the percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) algorithm. This document clarifies the value and role of ELCA in contemporary PCI, with new insights on its mechanism of action as well as recommendations for settings and protocols for use to help cardiologists achieve successful procedural and clinical outcomes. ELCA is a valuable tool for uncrossable and undilatable thrombotic and stent-related lesions. Lesion composition, settings, and lasing medium affect the magnitude of ELCA's photoablative effects. This study contains recommendations for ELCA setup, settings, and protocols.
43073028:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Arterial spin-labeling (ASL) MR imaging is a noninvasive perfusion technique used in presurgical evaluation of focal epilepsy. A 2021 meta-analysis assessed its accuracy for identifying perfusion abnormalities concordant with the epileptogenic zone (EZ) but predated later studies and partly derived specificity from healthy-control true negatives. We re-estimated the diagnostic accuracy of ASL for EZ-concordant perfusion abnormalities with explicit handling of true negatives, and tested whether current data permit a quantitative estimate of the relationship between ASL findings and postsurgical seizure freedom.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Following PRISMA 2020 and PRISMA-DTA, we searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, and Scopus from inception to June 2026 for English-language primary studies (≥10 patients) of ASL for EZ localization or surgical-outcome evaluation in focal epilepsy. Random-effects models estimated pooled sensitivity (logit; primary), an exploratory specificity, a logit concordance/detection proportion, and a Freeman-Tukey seizure-free proportion. Because true negatives were absent by design, a joint bivariate/HSROC model was not estimable. Risk of bias used QUADAS-2 and QUIPS; certainty of evidence used a DTA-adapted GRADE approach.
RESULTS: Fifteen studies were included. The primary analysis (8 studies, 160 patients) yielded a pooled ASL sensitivity for EZ-concordant abnormalities of 0.73 (95% CI, 0.65-0.80; I2 = 0.0%). The concordance/detection proportion was 0.78 (95% CI, 0.62-0.89; 4 studies), and exploratory specificity 0.37 (95% CI, 0.13-0.71; 5 studies). In the surgical-outcome arm, the pooled seizure-free proportion (Engel I/ILAE 1) was 0.68 (95% CI, 0.58-0.77; 4 studies) and 0.71 (95% CI, 0.56-0.84) in a stricter analysis. Critically, a pooled odds ratio for seizure freedom in ASL-concordant versus ASL-discordant resections could not be computed: the required cross-tabulation was reported in no study.
CONCLUSIONS: ASL has moderate, stable sensitivity for identifying perfusion abnormalities concordant with the anatomo-electro-clinically defined EZ, whereas specificity is not estimable from current single-group designs. ASL-linked surgical cohorts achieve seizure freedom in two-thirds of operated patients, but whether ASL-resection concordance predicts seizure freedom is unquantifiable: a reporting gap, not a null result. Until outcome is reported stratified by ASL-resection concordance, ASL should be used as a localizing adjunct, not a prognostic marker.
43073385:
OBJECTIVES: Effective application of artificial intelligence (AI) in musculoskeletal (MSK) radiology depends on targeting unmet clinical needs rather than technical feasibility. This Society of Skeletal Radiology (SSR) position statement identifies and prioritizes the most impactful AI applications and value propositions for MSK radiologists.
METHODS: The SSR AI Committee (n = 18) used structured brainstorming to compile lists of AI-based applications and value propositions. After deduplication, standardization, and categorization using a 12-component MSK radiology value cycle, refined lists were distributed as electronic surveys to 122 SSR committee members; 103 (84.4%) and 102 (83.6%) completed the applications and value propositions surveys, respectively, scoring each item on a 5-point Likert scale. Top 10 lists were generated from summed scores.
RESULTS: Brainstorming generated 208 AI application and 126 value proposition ideas, condensed to 138 and 56 unique items, respectively. Fourteen AI applications and 13 value propositions shared the top 10 ranks (tied scores). Top-ranked AI applications were within dictation and reporting (5 items), archiving and presentation (2), diagnostic imaging (1), follow-up imaging (2), quality/safety (2), and protocoling (2). Top-ranked value propositions were within dictation and reporting (4), diagnostic imaging (3), ordering (3), protocoling (2), and quality/safety (1). The highest-ranked application was AI-assisted comparison study retrieval (mean 3.17/4.0) and the highest-ranked value proposition was increased reporting efficiency (mean 3.30/4.0).
CONCLUSIONS: This position statement provides a demand-driven roadmap for AI development in MSK radiology. Workflow and reporting tools were prioritized over disease detection algorithms, highlighting a gap between clinical needs and current commercial AI offerings.
43073496: Foundation models (FMs) offer a promising approach for electrocardiography (ECG) and photoplethysmography (PPG) analysis, enabling reusable representations across tasks without large labeled datasets or task-specific training. We review open ECG/PPG FMs and datasets, outlining cardiovascular applications. Advantages include data efficiency and generalizability, though challenges remain, particularly reliance on homogeneous pretraining datasets and the absence of standardized evaluation frameworks. This review guides clinicians in understanding and applying FMs in cardiovascular research.
43073561: The duration of reduced robotic operative exposure associated with deterioration in technical performance, and the minimum recent case frequency needed to preserve performance, remain uncertain. We systematically reviewed PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus through October 3, 2026. Eligible studies assessed robotic operators after proficiency, training, or established practice in relation to exposure gaps or recent case frequency. Study quality was appraised using MERSQI. Technical-quality (T_skill*) and efficiency (T_eff*) vulnerability thresholds were estimated using separate Bayesian interval-censored models. Twenty-four reports representing 22 study clusters were included (median standardized MERSQI, 11.8/18). In the primary analyses, the exploratory cross-study posterior median vulnerability thresholds were 41.6 days for technical quality (95% credible interval [CrI], 9.0-143.5) and 48.9 days for efficiency (95% CrI, 9.4-192.9). Model-implied probabilities of threshold onset by 90 days were 73.2% and 66.4%, respectively. Broad sensitivity analyses incorporating retention-favorable evidence shifted the medians to 110.8 and 89.4 days. A pooled recent-volume threshold was not identifiable; fewer than two versus at least two robotic cases monthly represented only an exploratory boundary. Measurable robotic performance vulnerability may emerge within weeks of reduced exposure, but timing varies substantially and broader retention-inclusive sensitivity analyses yield later estimates. No universal minimum-volume or credentialing cutoff is supported.
43073710:
PURPOSE: Ultra-high field MRI (7 Tesla) could potentially improve white matter (WM) perfusion imaging because of less severe loss of label thanks to longer T1-values. However, physiological noise increases, making background suppression (BGS) likely more important at this field strength. The aim of this study is first to assess the importance of background suppression at 7 Tesla compared to 3 Tesla, and secondly to use that knowledge to optimize flow-alternating-inversion-recovery (FAIR) ASL for WM perfusion imaging.
METHODS: A background suppressed FAIR ASL labeling scheme was implemented at both 7 and 3 Tesla scanners. Perfusion temporal SNR was compared over a wide range of BGS-levels by exploiting a 2D multi-slice readout. The knowledge gained from this was used to optimize a FAIR ASL scan with 3D readout scanned at several post label delays (PLD). The tSNR was compared across PLD for GM and several WM masks.
RESULTS: BGS was found to be more important at 7 Tesla compared to 3 Tesla. Therefore, a 3D FAIR ASL scan with homogeneous high BGS was used for WM perfusion imaging. Across PLD, we found a parabolic trend for significant voxels in the deep WM, both for a non-zero but slightly stronger for the ischemic perfusion threshold, peaking around a PLD of 2300 ms. However, this was not significantly higher than a PLD of 1800 and 2800 ms in this healthy population.
CONCLUSION: BGS becomes increasingly important for perfusion imaging at higher field strengths. Background suppressed WM perfusion imaging at 7 Tesla might benefit from a longer PLD than typically recommended for GM.
43073719:
PURPOSE: To develop a high-resolution multi-delay renal arterial spin labeling (ASL) technique for free-breathing imaging at 5T.
METHODS: A radial renal ASL (Radial-ASL) sequence was proposed using flow-sensitive alternating inversion recovery (FAIR) preparation followed by continuous golden-angle radial acquisition. The k-space data were firstly sorted by delay time and then reordered based on respiratory motion, with data grouped into four respiratory phases for Spatio-Temporal eXtra-Dimensional Golden-angle RAdial Sparse Parallel (ST-XD-GRASP) reconstruction. Both the Buxton kinetic model and a stepwise kinetic model were applied to perfusion quantification. The proposed method was evaluated against the saturated multi-delay ASL (SAMURAI) technique using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), and correlation analysis. Scan-rescan repeatability and interobserver reproducibility were assessed using ICC.
RESULTS: Twelve healthy volunteers (mean age: 27.4 ± 4.9 years old, 7 males) and one patient (55-year-old female) were included. Radial-ASL with ST-XD-GRASP provided high-quality images with 1.17 mm in-plane resolution. The stepwise model showed improved fitting performance (R2 ≥ 0.95) compared with the Buxton model (R2: 0.36-0.85). Cortical renal blood flow showed no significant difference between Radial-ASL and SAMURAI (363.7 ± 30.3 vs. 360.4 ± 30.0 mL/100 g/min, p = 0.216), with good agreement (ICC = 0.910) and strong correlation (r = 0.912). Radial-ASL demonstrated good scan-rescan repeatability (ICC = 0.884-0.911) and interobserver reproducibility (ICC = 0.943-0.985).
CONCLUSION: Radial-ASL at 5T enables free-breathing multi-delay renal perfusion quantification with high spatial resolution and demonstrates good agreement with SAMURAI technique as well as good repeatability.
43073723:
PURPOSE: To assess whether independently developed cardiac-damage staging systems identify concordant mortality associations in chronic aortic regurgitation (AR), without assuming equivalence of stage definitions.
METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL, and Web of Science were searched through September 16, 2026 for longitudinal cohorts of adults with native moderate or greater AR. Adjusted all-cause mortality hazard ratios (HRs) were summarized using exploratory random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood and modified Hartung-Knapp inference.
RESULTS: Five cohorts comprised 6043 patients; four used predominantly echocardiographic staging and one used a magnetic resonance-led multimodality framework. One cohort contributed 4026 patients, 78% of whom had moderate AR. The exploratory pooled HR per study-defined stage was 1.72 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.09-2.71; three cohorts, n = 1446; I2 = 62.7%). Restricting this analysis to two four-category frameworks yielded an HR of 1.90 (95% CI, 0.48-7.52; n = 827). For selected source-defined downstream categories versus no damage, the pooled HR was 2.89 (95% CI, 1.63-5.12; three cohorts, n = 4992; I2 = 0%). Three studies reported incremental prognostic performance. Staging definitions and valve-intervention handling differed across studies.
CONCLUSION: Independently developed frameworks identified adverse mortality associations in mixed moderate-to-severe AR populations. Pooled HRs are exploratory summaries of nonequivalent exposures and follow-up strategies; they do not validate a universal staging scale, severe AR-specific risk stratification, or an intervention threshold.
43073849:
OBJECTIVE: The association between the methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR) A1298C polymorphism and susceptibility to pregnancy-induced hypertension (PIH) has been widely investigated, but the results remain inconsistent. This meta-analysis aimed to systematically evaluate the relationship between the MTHFR A1298C polymorphism and PIH risk.
METHODS: This meta-analysis was reported in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. Eligible studies were identified through a comprehensive search of databases including PubMed, Web of Science, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), Wanfang, VIP Chinese Science and Technology Journal Full-text, and China Biomedical Literature (CBM), up to November 2025. Relevant data were extracted independently by two investigators. Pooled odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated to assess the association between the MTHFR A1298C polymorphism and PIH under six genetic models. The false discovery rate (FDR) was applied across the six genetic models and subgroup analyses. Subgroup analyses were performed to explore sources of heterogeneity, and publication bias was assessed using Begg's and Egger's tests.
RESULTS: A total of 31 studies involving 3,816 PIH patients and 17,303 controls were included. After adjusting for multiple comparisons using the FDR method, no statistically significant association was observed between the MTHFR A1298C polymorphism and PIH risk under any of the six genetic models, including the dominant model, allele, recessive, homozygous, heterozygous, or overdominant models.
CONCLUSION: This meta-analysis indicates no statistically significant association between the MTHFR A1298C polymorphism and PIH susceptibility after adjusting for multiple comparisons. The findings suggest that this variant may not be a major genetic risk factor for PIH. Given the limitations of current evidence, further large-scale, high-quality studies across diverse populations are required to provide a more definitive conclusion.
43074003:
BACKGROUND: Free liquid silicone injection (FLSI) cases are still sporadically encountered despite advances in breast augmentation techniques. The American College of Radiology (ACR) guidelines support the use of breast magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) for silicone complication mapping in conventional medical-grade implant cases. However, FLSI-related complications remain lesser-known in clinical practice. A limited familiarity with their imaging appearances hinders accurate image interpretation and timely clinical management. This case series illustrates uncommonly reported multimodal imaging variations of siliconomas with histopathologic correlation.
CASE PRESENTATION: Two 56-year-old women (one Malay and one Chinese) with histories of FLSI presented with a unilateral breast lump and nipple discharge, respectively. Both patients underwent mammography, ultrasonography and MRI. Mammography showed innumerable siliconomas, potentially obscuring malignant lesions. In both cases, ultrasonography had limited diagnostic value. Dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI provided superior visualization but remained challenging to interpret due to the multiplicity of lesions and overlapping imaging features between benign silicone-related complications and malignancy. Both patients had uneventful surgeries, and histopathology confirmed the final diagnoses.
CONCLUSION: This case series is a preliminary step toward larger longitudinal cohort studies, aimed at characterizing the full spectrum of FLSI imaging appearances. Improved understanding can reduce diagnostic uncertainty where silicone-related changes obscure or mimic malignancy. These case findings also highlight the need for standardized, evidence-based, FLSI-specific imaging protocols and clinical guidelines to support informed decision-making and optimize patient care.
43074056:
PURPOSE: Static magnetic field (B0) inhomogeneity degrades MRI quality near air-tissue interfaces in the brain and spine. Anatomically tailored shim coils can mitigate these effects, but their design requires knowledge of B0 distributions across diverse human anatomies and realistic posture differences. This study aimed to create an open-source database of simulated B0 field maps derived from segmented MRI to support brain and spine shimming development.
METHODS: Sixty volunteers were scanned at two 3T sites using T1-weighted MPRAGE protocols with head-to-torso coverage. Anatomical structures were segmented using three automated tools (Samseg, TotalSpineSeg, and a custom nnU-Net v2 model) to label the body, brain, skull, spine, vertebrae, discs, sinuses, trachea, and lungs. Segmentations were post-processed using a custom 3D Slicer pipeline for island removal, hole filling, and smoothing, then merged and assigned literature-based susceptibility values. ΔB0 maps were simulated via Fourier-domain convolution with the dipole kernel. Simulations were compared against measured field maps in two additional subjects. To illustrate an application, volume-wise and slice-wise shimming were performed on this simulated dataset.
RESULTS: Expected inhomogeneity patterns were observed in simulated ΔB0 maps near airways. The subject-averaged spatial standard deviation of ΔB0 within the brain was reduced by 66.7% with whole-volume second-order shimming and by 70.9% with subsequent first-order slice-wise shimming.
CONCLUSION: An open-source database of 60 anatomy-based simulated ΔB0 maps spanning the brain and spinal cord for shimming optimization is presented, with all data and code publicly available.
43074120:
PURPOSE: To improve deep learning-based QSM+qBOLD (QQ) oxygen extraction fraction (OEF) mapping by explicitly learning the temporal evolution of the multi-echo gradient-echo (mGRE) magnitude signal, whose decay encodes the tissue oxygenation that QQ-based OEF mapping depends on.
METHODS: 3D multi-echo gradient echo images were acquired in 34 ischemic stroke patients with arterial spin labeling (ASL) and diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI). We developed QQ-S, a deep learning method that estimates OEF by inverting the QQ model. QQ-S extends QQ-NET by adding convolutional long short-term memory (ConvLSTM) modules to the encoder to process the mGRE echoes sequentially. To isolate the effect of this architectural change, both networks were trained with the same simulated data and training scheme including the loss function. OEF maps from QQ-S and QQ-NET were compared in simulation and ischemic stroke patients.
RESULTS: In simulation, QQ-S provided more accurate OEF than QQ-NET, with lower mean absolute error (MAE) against the simulation ground truth: 3.43% vs. 5.03% in normal-appearing tissue and 4.88% vs. 10.60% in low-OEF lesions. In subacute stroke patients, where no ground truth is available, the lesion-to-contralateral OEF ratio was significantly lower with QQ-S than with QQ-NET (0.71 ± 0.26 vs. 0.81 ± 0.24; p < 0.001), suggesting more sensitive detection of lesion OEF, consistent with PET reports in the subacute phase. OEF in acute lesions and normal-appearing tissue was comparable between methods.
CONCLUSION: By explicitly learning inter-echo signal evolution with ConvLSTM, QQ-S improves OEF accuracy over QQ-NET, offering a promising tool for assessing tissue viability from conventional mGRE data.
43074584:
BACKGROUND: The 2023 international evidence-based guideline for polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) conditionally recommended serum anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH) as an alternative to ultrasound for diagnosing polycystic ovarian morphology (PCOM) in adults, marking a significant shift in diagnostic practice. However, the diagnostic accuracy of AMH remains debated, particularly regarding its utility as a standalone test, its application across diverse populations, and its use in adolescents.
METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted following PRISMA guidelines. Major electronic databases, including PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library, were searched for diagnostic accuracy studies published until November 2024, and studies evaluating serum AMH against the Rotterdam criteria for PCOS or ultrasound-defined PCOM were included. A bivariate random-effects model was used to pool sensitivity and specificity with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for three key questions: AMH for 1) PCOS diagnosis in adults, 2) PCOM diagnosis in adults, and 3) PCOS diagnosis in adolescents. The Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies-2 tool was used to assess the risk of bias.
RESULTS: For adult PCOS diagnosis, 83 studies (n = 33,376) were included, yielding a pooled sensitivity of 0.81 (95% CI, 0.78-0.83) and a specificity of 0.89 (95% CI, 0.86-0.91). For adult PCOM diagnosis, six studies (n = 11,436) provided a pooled sensitivity of 0.79 (95% CI, 0.70-0.86) and a specificity of 0.88 (95% CI, 0.77-0.94). In contrast, the analysis for adolescent PCOS (11 studies, n = 1,090) revealed a significantly lower accuracy, with a pooled sensitivity of 0.66 (95% CI, 0.58-0.73) and a specificity of 0.78 (95% CI, 0.71-0.83). Substantial heterogeneity was observed across all analyses.
CONCLUSION: The current, updated meta-analysis confirms that serum AMH is a highly specific and moderately sensitive biomarker for diagnosing PCOM and PCOS in adults, supporting its role as an adjunctive diagnostic tool. However, its utility as a standalone test is limited by significant heterogeneity; in addition, its diagnostic performance is further limited in adolescents, providing evidence against its use in such population. Future efforts must focus on the international standardization of AMH assays and the development of population-specific reference values to enhance its clinical utility.
43074746:
INTRODUCTION/AIMS: Parsonage-Turner syndrome (PTS), also known as neuralgic amyotrophy (NA), is an acute-onset peripheral neuropathy predominately affecting the upper extremity and causing substantial pain and disability. No formal international consensus-based diagnostic criteria exist, contributing to diagnostic delays, inconsistent terminology, and limited ability to collate and systematically analyze data. This study aimed to develop consensus-based diagnostic criteria and a diagnostic algorithm for PTS/NA.
METHODS: A modified Delphi study was conducted with an international, multidisciplinary panel of experts selected based on clinical and research experience with PTS/NA. A steering committee drafted preliminary statements informed by a literature review and panelist-derived diagnostic challenges across 9 domains. Two electronic survey rounds used Likert-scale and binary response formats, with consensus defined as ≥ 75% agreement or disagreement.
RESULTS: All 13 panelists completed both rounds (100% response rate). Of 86 items, 52 (60%) reached agreement. The panel endorsed "Parsonage-Turner syndrome" and "neuralgic amyotrophy" as interchangeable terms. Classic PTS/NA was defined by acute-onset severe pain (≥ 7/10) and severe weakness in a non-myotomal distribution. Non-classic presentations warranted confirmatory electrodiagnostic testing and/or nerve-focused imaging. Hourglass-like nerve constrictions were considered likely pathognomonic (100% agreement). If steroids were considered, early initiation was recommended in classic presentations, even before confirmatory testing.
DISCUSSION: These criteria may shorten time to diagnosis, standardize terminology, guide resource utilization, and facilitate clinical trials. Future research should prioritize validation of the criteria in patient cohorts.
43074911:
PURPOSE: To establish a risk-stratified management framework for cervical lymph node metastasis (LNM) in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) by integrating AJCC 9th edition staging, the 2024 HNCIG extranodal extension (ENE) consensus, AI radiomics, and modern immunotherapy, with critical appraisal of clinical utility and external validation.
METHODS: A PRISMA 2020-compliant systematic review of 49 high-quality studies identified through database search (January 2019-April 30, 2025), with 3 additional post-cutoff studies used for background context; stratified quality assessment was performed using RoB 2, NOS, AMSTAR 2, and QUADAS-2.
FINDING: Unified pathological-radiological ENE criteria were consolidated for HNSCC; AI radiomics showed promising but insufficiently externally validated performance for occult metastasis prediction; risk-adapted algorithms integrating selective neck dissection, adjuvant anti-PD-1 immunotherapy, and de-escalation were constructed for specific risk strata.
CONCLUSION: This review provides a risk-stratified evidence synthesis for LNM management in HNSCC, while highlighting that radiomics models require prospective multicenter validation before clinical deployment, and that management recommendations should be applied within appropriate risk and disease strata.
43075854: Post-traumatic osteoarthritis (PTOA) represents a significant health burden, particularly since it often affects young, athletic individuals. The concept of PTOA has evolved from early epidemiologic observations linking joint injury to osteoarthritis (OA) to a mechanistically grounded disease model supported by translational and preclinical research. Preclinical animal models have historically played a critical role in investigating mechanisms of OA pathophysiology, discovering diagnostic markers, and evaluating therapeutic interventions. As part of the 2026 International Consensus Meeting on Preclinical Models of Osteoarthritis, which culminated in an in-person meeting in Charlotte, NC, high-priority questions specific to the application of animal models to the study of PTOA (rather than primary OA) were identified to assess the current state of knowledge and identify key gaps for future research in the field. Consensus recommendations included (1) careful model selection with consideration of age, sex, and post-injury time point to maximize translational impact; (2) development of shared definitions of disease to facilitate cross-study comparisons; and (3) identification and/or refinement of novel molecular and imaging diagnostic biomarkers with cross-species applicability. These recommendations support the long-term goal of developing novel diagnostic tools and therapeutic interventions to prevent or reverse PTOA.
43076038:
BACKGROUND: Report the rate of epidural hematoma (EH) following lumbar interlaminar epidural steroid injections (ILESI) in patients prescribed anticoagulant or antiplatelet medications (ACAP).
METHODS: This analysis is a retrospective cohort study in a single private multispecialty practice reviewing 1787 unique patient encounters. Main outcome measures are to follow up patients after lumbar ILESI procedure by retrospective clinical chart review, outside clinical records review, and telephone follow up of consecutive patients over 8 years. Patients are stratified by whether ACAP medication was maintained or ceased prior to lumbar ILESI procedure.
RESULTS: There were zero clinically relevant EHs (0/1787, 0%, 95% CI 0.0-0.2%). In 310 patient encounters maintained on anticoagulation (either AC only or AC in conjunction with AP), the rate of clinically relevant EH was 0/310 (0%, 95% CI 0.0-1.2%). Patients who maintained AP medication alone, the rate of clinically relevant EH was 0/649 (0%, 95% CI 0.0-0.6%). Two patients without follow up data were not included in analysis.
CONCLUSIONS: Overall, the risk of EH following ILESI is low even in patients maintained on ACAP medication. At least 10 case reports of EH following lumbar ILESI have been published. Aggregating our data with other published cohorts, the rate of EH following lumbar ILESI, regardless of ACAP status, is 2/10,536 (0.02%, 95% CI 0.0-0.07%).
43076359:
BACKGROUND: Juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia (JMML) is an aggressive myeloproliferative neoplasm driven by Ras pathway alterations that occur in young children. Hematopoietic stem cell transplantation is the current standard of care for most patients, yet clinical outcomes remain suboptimal. Specifically, a subset of patients with JMML experience transformation to acute myeloid leukemia (AML) with ≥20% marrow involvement, but contemporary data detailing this phenomenon and its ontogeny are limited.
PROCEDURE: We identified 18 patients diagnosed with JMML who subsequently experienced transformation to AML and compared them against a contemporaneous control cohort of 81 previously reported patients who were diagnosed with JMML without progression to AML.
RESULTS: Patients with JMML-to-AML transformation had an increased incidence of high-risk JMML features at diagnosis, including older age, elevated fetal hemoglobin, two or more somatically mutated genes, and intermediate/high DNA methylation at diagnosis compared to controls. Eleven of 18 patients had acquisition of additional mutations or karyotypic abnormalities after diagnosis. Using RNA-sequencing analysis, we observed that JMML-to-AML samples clustered by cell composition more closely with de novo AML than with JMML samples. Patients with JMML-to-AML transformation had a significantly lower 5-year overall survival compared to control patients (13% vs. 61%, p = 0.004).
CONCLUSIONS: Although the 20% blast cutoff separating JMML from AML is seemingly arbitrary, RNA-sequencing data differentiated pre- and post-transformation samples, suggesting distinct molecular features. Given the very poor prognosis of children with JMML-to-AML transformation, novel therapies in the context of clinical trials should be considered.
43076382:
OBJECTIVES: To develop a Menopause Medical Eligibility Criteria (MenoMEC) tool to guide individualized, evidence-based care for the treatment of vasomotor symptoms due to menopause.
METHODS: We conducted a modified Delphi panel of 15 multidisciplinary experts to establish US-focused consensus recommendations for hormone and nonhormone therapy use in managing moderate-severe vasomotor symptoms, considering various comorbid conditions. An online survey assessed agreement with proposed recommendations using a nine-point Likert scale, with ≥70% agreement defining consensus. Items lacking consensus were discussed in a structured in-person meeting, leading to refined recommendations and final development of the tool.
RESULTS: Panelists affirmed hormone therapy as first-line for eligible women and nonhormone therapy for those with contraindications or who decline hormone therapy. Recommended first-line nonhormone therapy options were selective serotonin/serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors, gabapentin, and oxybutynin, after accounting for contraindications. Neurokinin therapies (eg, fezolinetant, elinzanetant) were supported as first-line but limited by access and cost. Clonidine and most herbal/over-the-counter products were not recommended due to potential adverse effects, drug-drug interactions, or lack of evidence of benefit or harm. Specific recommendations regarding the appropriateness of therapy addressed women with cardiovascular disease, metabolic syndrome, thrombosis, liver disease, smoking, and hormone-sensitive cancers. All panelists agreed that there was an urgent need to provide structured guidance to the clinical community regarding the selection and use of hormone versus nonhormone therapy.
CONCLUSIONS: This panel provided structured, symptom-based, and comorbidity-based recommendations to optimize therapy for the management of vasomotor symptoms and supported the development of a MenoMEC guideline for use in primary care clinical settings.
43076449:
BACKGROUND: Diverticulitis is among the most prevalent gastrointestinal conditions, with rising incidence in younger adults. Randomized trials have challenged long-standing principles of management, including routine antibiotic use and indications for elective surgery. Clinical practice guidelines aim to standardize care but differ in methodology and scope. This systematic review aimed to identify where contemporary international guidelines agree, where they diverge, and on what evidence each position rests.
METHODS: Clinical practice guidelines on acute diverticulitis were identified by a systematic PubMed search (last updated September 2026) and hand-searching of society websites and reference lists. Articles were independently screened against prespecified eligibility criteria (explicit evidence and recommendation grading; publication in English or German; comprehensive coverage), with disagreements resolved by consensus. Recommendations were extracted into five predefined domains (classification, diagnosis, therapy of acute diverticulitis, elective surgery, long-term management) and mapped onto unified evidence and recommendation scales for direct comparison across heterogeneous grading systems. The methodological quality of each guideline was appraised using AGREE II.
RESULTS: Of 148 records identified, 146 were screened and 142 were excluded; four guidelines met the eligibility criteria, namely those of the German Society of Gastroenterology, Digestive and Metabolic Diseases/German Society of General and Visceral Surgery (Germany, 2021), the European Society of Coloproctology (Europe, 2020), American Society of Colon and Rectal Surgeons (USA, 2020), and the World Society of Emergency Surgery (international, 2020). All four reached consensus on fundamental principles, including selective antibiotic omission in uncomplicated diverticulitis, size-based abscess management, and individualized indications for elective surgery. Substantial discrepancies were identified in classification, the role of ultrasound, criteria for outpatient management, abscess size thresholds, indications for primary anastomosis versus Hartmann's procedure, and long-term management. Disagreement was most pronounced in areas with limited evidence, including interventional abscess drainage, laparoscopic lavage in perforated diverticulitis, and pharmacological secondary prevention. The German guideline achieved the highest AGREE II scores in all six domains; applicability scored lowest throughout (6-19%).
CONCLUSION: Clinically relevant discrepancies persist where prospective evidence is most sparse. Heterogeneous evidence, grading, and classification systems limit cross-guideline comparison. Reducing practice variation will require harmonized definitions and prospective trials comparing divergent management strategies.
43076672: History A 31-year-old female patient with past medical history of uterine leiomyomas, hypertension, and migraines underwent CT for evaluation of an abdominal wall hernia, and lesions were incidentally discovered (Fig 1). The patient did not report any symptoms other than the bulge due to the hernia. Abdominal examination was negative for tenderness and palpable mass. Past surgical history included multiple myomectomies, cesarean section, and hysterectomy with bilateral salpingectomy. Laboratory results, including liver function tests, complete blood count, α-fetoprotein, carcinoembryonic antigen, and carbohydrate antigen 19-9, were within normal limits. The patient underwent MRI for further characterization (Figs 2-5).
43076673: Background Whether stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) is associated with lower hemorrhage risk for unruptured brain arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) during the latency period (ie, from SRS to complete AVM obliteration) remains controversial. Purpose To evaluate whether SRS is associated with lower hemorrhage risk in unruptured brain AVMs during the latency period when analyzed from the time of diagnosis. Materials and Methods This single-center retrospective study included 511 patients with unruptured brain AVMs at diagnosis treated with single-session SRS between June 1990 and May 2024. Hemorrhage rates before and after SRS were calculated using the person-year method. A time-dependent Cox proportional hazards model was used to assess the association between SRS and hemorrhage risk. The pre-SRS hemorrhage rate was calculated using the interval between diagnosis and SRS. Results For the 511 patients (median age, 39 years [IQR, 28-52 years]; 306 male patients), the total observation period from diagnosis to SRS or any prior treatment was 1009 person-years, and the pre-SRS hemorrhage rate was 3.4 per 100 person-years (34 hemorrhages). Among 477 patients who underwent SRS without a pre-SRS hemorrhage, 75 patients were lost to follow-up during the latency period, and the median latency period was 33 months, with a total of 1711 person-years. Hemorrhage occurred in 24 patients during the latency period, yielding an overall latency-period hemorrhage rate of 1.4 per 100 person-years. After adjustment for age, nidus volume, and venous drainage, time-dependent Cox proportional hazards analysis showed that SRS was associated with lower hemorrhage risk in the post-SRS latency period compared with the pre-SRS period, corresponding to a 53% lower hazard (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.47 [95% CI: 0.27, 0.83]; P = .009). SRS was also associated with lower hemorrhage risk in lesions treated with SRS following prior surgery or endovascular therapy (hazard ratio, 0.20; P = .01). Conclusion In patients with unruptured brain AVMs, SRS was associated with lower hemorrhage risk during the latency period when analyzed from the time of diagnosis. © RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article.
43076674: Background Type II endoleak (T2EL) is a common complication after endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) that may lead to aneurysm sac enlargement. Although guideline-based criteria are used to identify high-risk patients, their predictive accuracy remains limited. Purpose To evaluate the predictive value of preoperative total branch vessel ostial area at CT angiography (CTA) for T2EL after EVAR. Materials and Methods This single-center retrospective study included patients undergoing EVAR for infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) between January 2010 and December 2020. After exclusion of other endoleak types, CTA-derived anatomic parameters and outcomes were compared by isolated T2EL status. Total branch vessel ostial area was evaluated using prespecified Cox models and Cox-least absolute shrinkage and selection operator analysis. Discrimination and reproducibility were assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis, intraclass correlation coefficients, and Bland-Altman analysis. Results Of 216 patients in this study (mean age, 66 years ± 7.6 [SD]; 190 male; median follow-up, 4.7 years), 86 (39.8%) developed T2EL. Total branch vessel ostial area showed excellent reproducibility (intraclass correlation coefficients, 0.98-1.00) and was larger in patients with T2EL than in those without T2EL (median, 24.5 vs 11.7 mm2; P < .001). Sac enlargement was more frequent with T2EL (45.3% [39 of 86] vs 12.3% [16 of 130]; P < .001) and was associated with reintervention (hazard ratio [HR], 2.83; P = .003) but not overall survival (HR, 1.76; P = .28). In the fully adjusted Cox model, total branch vessel ostial area was associated with T2EL (HR, 1.06 per 1-mm2 increase [95% CI: 1.04, 1.08]; P < .001). Total branch ostial area showed better discrimination for T2EL than guideline-based criteria (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, 0.82 vs 0.64; P < .001), with a Youden index-derived cutoff of 15.55 mm2. Restricted cubic spline analysis showed a positive continuous association in T2EL risk with increasing ostial area (P < .001). Conclusion Preoperative CTA-derived total branch vessel ostial area outperformed conventional branch diameter and count criteria for predicting T2EL in patients after EVAR for infrarenal AAA. © RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article. See also the editorial by Liddell in this issue.
43076683: Background Mild hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) comprises approximately 30%-50% of neonatal encephalopathy cases, yet neurodevelopmental outcomes remain difficult to predict using clinical assessment alone. Purpose To develop and externally test a diffusion kurtosis imaging (DKI)-based machine learning model for predicting 24-month neurodevelopmental outcomes in neonates with mild HIE. Materials and Methods This prospective four-hospital study consecutively enrolled neonates from November 2019 through November 2023, with 24-month follow-up completed in November 2025. The primary outcome was adverse neurodevelopment at 24 months, defined as any Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, third edition, composite score below 85; cerebral palsy; or epilepsy requiring ongoing treatment. Clinical-only, imaging-only, and combined clinical-imaging models were developed from 49 DKI parameters and seven clinical variables. Model discrimination was assessed with the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), and curves were compared with paired DeLong tests and false discovery rate adjustment. Results Overall, 740 neonates were included (mean gestational age, 38.3 weeks ± 1.3 [SD]; 404 [54.6%] female). Adverse outcomes occurred in 182 of 510 development cohort participants (35.7%) and 80 of 230 external test set participants (34.8%). In the external test set, the combined model achieved an AUC of 0.92 (95% CI: 0.89, 0.95), with a sensitivity of 86% (69 of 80) and specificity of 85.3% (128 of 150). It exceeded the clinical-only model (AUC, 0.85; false discovery rate-adjusted P = .004) and imaging-only model (AUC, 0.86; false discovery rate-adjusted P = .005). Prespecified risk stratification yielded a negative predictive value of 100% (61 of 61) for low-risk infants and a positive predictive value of 88% (38 of 43) for high-risk infants. Conclusion In neonates with mild HIE, a combined clinical and DKI model demonstrated higher discrimination for predicting 24-month neurodevelopmental outcomes than did clinical-only or imaging-only models. © The Author(s) 2026. Published by the Radiological Society of North America under a CC BY 4.0 license. Supplemental material is available for this article.
43076917:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the utility of excess parenchymal water (EPW) partial volume, quantified from multi-dynamic multi-echo (MDME)-based relaxometry, in distinguishing brain tumors.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 95 patients (61 with grade 4 adult-type diffuse gliomas, 16 with primary CNS lymphomas (PCNSLs), and 18 with brain metastases) who underwent preoperative MRI including MDME-based sequences between October 2022 and May 2025. EPW partial volume maps were generated using dedicated software. Peritumoral T2 hyperintense regions of interest (ROIs) were defined by subtracting manually drawn ROIs of the enhancing tumor on contrast-enhanced T1-weighted images from the whole T2 hyperintense areas. EPW partial volumes were compared among groups using the Kruskal-Wallis test with post hoc Dunn's tests and Bonferroni correction. Diagnostic performance was assessed by ROC curve analysis.
RESULTS: The average EPW partial volume in the peritumoral T2 hyperintense area was significantly lower in grade 4 adult-type diffuse gliomas (median [IQR], 23.2% [14.6-30.5]) than in brain metastases (30.5% [21.7-37.3]) (p = 0.02). However, no significant differences in EPW partial volumes were observed between gliomas and PCNSLs (p = 0.85), or between PCNSLs and metastases (p = 0.65). The AUC was 0.71 (95% CI, 0.56-0.84) for differentiating gliomas from metastases. Using an EPW cutoff of 27.7%, the sensitivity and specificity were 67% and 71%, respectively.
CONCLUSION: EPW partial volume from MDME-based relaxometry was significantly lower in peritumoral areas of grade 4 adult-type diffuse gliomas than in brain metastases, suggesting its potential as a complementary quantitative biomarker for their differentiation.
KEY POINTS: Question Can excess parenchymal water partial volume derived from relaxometry distinguish different types of brain tumors? Findings In this pilot cohort, excess parenchymal water partial volume within peritumoral T2 hyperintense areas was significantly lower in grade 4 adult-type diffuse gliomas than in brain metastases, despite the modest diagnostic performance. Clinical relevance The average excess parenchymal water partial volume in the peritumoral T2 hyperintense area may complement conventional MRI by providing a quantitative measure that helps differentiate grade 4 adult-type diffuse gliomas from brain metastases.
43076934: The optimization of radiation dose in pediatric computed tomography (CT) is a critical imperative, driven by the heightened radiosensitivity of children. This review provides a critical analysis of the evolution of dose optimization, from foundational principles like As Low As Reasonably Achievable (ALARA) and conventional techniques to the transformative impact of artificial intelligence (AI). We trace the progression from iterative reconstruction (IR), which offered initial dose reduction but was limited by unnatural image textures and computational demands, to the new paradigm of deep learning reconstruction (DLR) and emerging detector technologies like photon-counting CT. Clinical evidence demonstrates that DLR significantly shifts the traditional compromise between dose and image quality, enabling substantial potential dose reductions while producing images with superior noise properties and diagnostic confidence. Beyond reconstruction, AI is also automating scan protocoling to enhance consistency and reduce errors. However, the clinical integration of these powerful tools is not seamless. Significant barriers remain, including the "black box" nature of algorithms, the need for new training curricula for radiographers, and complex ethical and regulatory challenges. This review synthesizes these issues and charts a path forward, advocating for a holistic approach involving complementary AI-specific reference levels, federated learning, and robust governance to realize the full potential of a safer, more efficient, and patient-specific dose optimization ecosystem.
43076935:
PURPOSE: To describe antithrombotic therapy in the first 24 h after endovascular treatment (EVT) and its determinants, and how far outcome comparisons depend on adjustment.
METHODS: Post hoc landmark analysis (24‑h assessment) of the prospective ANGEL-ACT registry (111 Chinese centers, 2017-2019) using mixed-effects logistic regression, sequential adjustment and quantitative bias analysis.
RESULTS: Of 1793 patients, 87 left hospital against medical advice within 24 h. Of the remaining 1706, 60.7% had antiplatelet therapy recorded by 24 h (mostly dual), 8.5% anticoagulants and 23.3% no antithrombotic agent; in atrial fibrillation, 3.4% received an oral anticoagulant and 31.7% no antithrombotic agent. Antiplatelet therapy was associated with stent placement (adjusted odds ratio 1.97, 95% CI 1.38-2.83) and inversely with symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH; 0.45, 0.28-0.72), intraprocedural complications and atrial fibrillation; the between-center median odds ratio was 2.65 (2.16-3.44). For 90-day death, standardized risk ratios were 0.60 (0.44-0.82) without and 0.69 (0.54-0.91) with adjustment for 24‑h NIHSS and sICH (E-values 2.70 and 2.26). If unmeasured, sICH could have biased the risk ratio by up to 1.52-fold, enough to explain the fully adjusted estimate (bias factor needed 1.45) but not the less adjusted one (1.66).
CONCLUSION: Antithrombotic therapy within 24 h after EVT was associated with stenting, bleeding and atrial fibrillation and varied between centers beyond measured case mix. Its association with lower mortality is likely to remain partly confounded, as confounding as strong as that observed for measured factors could account for most or all of it, and should not be read as a treatment effect.
43076941: Glioblastoma and other malignant brain tumors are difficult to treat due to the invasive behavior of the disease, resistance to conventional medicines, and the blood-brain barrier that limits delivery of therapeutics. This systematic review evaluates the potential of Sonodynamic Therapy (SDT), a non-invasive therapy that combines low-intensity ultrasound with tumor-selective sonosensitizers to produce fatal reactive oxygen species (ROS). A comprehensive literature search was conducted according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Analysis of 36 qualifying studies suggested that SDT could induce tumor-specific apoptosis and necrosis with little injury to healthy brain tissue by generating reactive oxygen species (ROS) and ultrasonic cavitation. Various sonosensitizers, such as 5-aminolevulinic acid, Photofrin II, and novel nanosonosensitizers, can improve their tumor targeting and efficacy. Early-phase clinical trials, including phase 0/1, phase 1 and phase 1/2 trials, have demonstrated encouraging safety, feasibility, and preliminary biological and clinical activity in high-grade gliomas and juvenile brain tumors. Optimization of the ultrasonic parameters (frequency, intensity, pulse patterns) is critical for therapeutic outcomes. Moreover, novel combination approaches with chemotherapy, radiation, and immunotherapy may synergistically improve the anti-tumor advantages of SDT. To summarize, SDT is a novel and minimally invasive therapy that has the potential to significantly improve the outcomes of patients with malignant brain tumors by selectively targeting tumor cells. Although the clinical application is enabled by improvements in sonosensitizer design and ultrasound technology, some problems with standardization of protocols and optimization of delivery still exist. Larger clinical trials are needed to confirm its efficacy and safety and its integration with multimodal therapy may delineate future neuro-oncological treatment paradigms.
43076965:
PURPOSE: To evaluate whether tumour contact length improves discrimination of muscle-invasive bladder cancer within Vesical Imaging-Reporting and Data System (VI-RADS) categories 2 and 3 on 3.0 T multiparametric MRI.
METHODS: This prospective single-centre study included 207 consecutive adults with a bladder mass who underwent 3.0 T multiparametric MRI before transurethral resection between February 2024 and January 2026. Two radiologists, blinded to histopathology, independently assigned VI-RADS categories and measured contact length. Histopathology of the resection specimen, or of re-resection when detrusor muscle was absent, was the reference standard. The primary analysis compared contact length ≥ 30 mm with VI-RADS 3 versus 2 within the VI-RADS 2-3 subgroup using McNemar's exact test.
RESULTS: Ninety-two patients (44.4%) had muscle-invasive disease. Within the VI-RADS 2-3 subgroup (n = 101; 24 muscle-invasive), contact length ≥ 30 mm yielded a sensitivity of 87.5% (95% CI 67.6-97.3) and a specificity of 76.6% (65.6-85.5), compared with 79.2% and 62.3% for VI-RADS 3 versus 2 (McNemar p = 0.69 and p = 0.043, respectively). Muscle invasion was present in 10.0% of VI-RADS 3 lesions below 30 mm and 60.7% at or above it; for VI-RADS 2 lesions, the proportions were 2.4% and 36.4%. Requiring both criteria increased specificity to 85.7% but missed 7 of 24 muscle-invasive tumours. Inter-reader agreement for contact length was excellent (intraclass correlation coefficient 0.906).
CONCLUSION: Within VI-RADS 2-3, a pre-specified 30 mm contact-length threshold improved specificity without a significant difference in sensitivity and was reproducible. Contact length complements the VI-RADS category and requires prospective multicentre validation.
43076966:
OBJECTIVE: Automated identification and extraction of recommendations for additional imaging (RAI) from radiology reports could facilitate closed-loop tracking and follow-up completion. We compare a prompt-engineered GPT-4.1 large language model (LLM) versus a validated encoder-only transformer deep learning model (bidirectional encoder representations from transformers [BERT]) for detection of RAI in abdominopelvic computed tomography (CTAP) reports, and evaluate GPT-4.1 for extraction of actionable RAI elements.
METHODS: This retrospective study included CTAP reports from a multi-institution system in 2023. LLM and BERT were used to identify RAI from radiology reports; LLM also extracted RAI actionable elements (modality, body part, time frame, rationale). Recall, precision, F1, and accuracy for RAI detection were determined using human-annotated reference standard. Paired comparison between each model's accuracy used McNemar's test. LLM recall, precision, F1, and accuracy for actionable element extraction were computed. Element prevalence was compared using chi-square test.
RESULTS: 2000 random reports for unique patients (58% women; mean age 58.5 ± 17.5) included 215 RAI within 206 reports. For RAI detection, GPT-4.1 recall, precision, F1 and accuracy were 95.6%, 98.5%, 97.0% and 99.4%, respectively; BERT recall, precision, F1 and accuracy were 93.7%, 96.5%, 95.1% and 99.0% (p = 0.16). Recommendation element recall were as follows: 100.0% for time frame, 93.9% for body part, 90.2% for rationale, and 94.2% for modality. Precision were 100.0%, 95.7%, 94.6% and 86.1%, respectively. 29/215 (13.5%) RAI were complete (specified all actionable elements). Prevalence of actionable elements varied (p < 0.001), highest for rationale (215/215, 100%), followed by body part (213/215, 99.1%), modality (191/215, 88.8%), and time frame (31/215, 14.4%).
CONCLUSION: GPT-4.1 demonstrated high accuracy for extraction of RAI and enabled accurate extraction of actionable elements. LLM integration into radiology workflows can facilitate automatic closed-loop communication and tracking of recommended imaging, which may reduce diagnostic delays.
43076967:
OBJECTIVE: To develop and temporally validate a bedside risk score (BTCH-AOMI) based exclusively on pre-CTA clinical variables to predict acute occlusive mesenteric ischemia (AOMI) in emergency CTA-selected patients.
METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated 285 adult patients (development cohort [2017-2022]: n = 187, 85 AOMI; temporal validation cohort [2023-2024]: n = 98, 42 AOMI). A 0-5-point score was constructed using four pre-CTA predictors: abdominal distension (1 point), AOMI risk conditions (1 point), peritonitis (2 points), and bedside inflammatory response (1 point). Score performance was evaluated and compared with an operationalized "pain-out-of-proportion" rule.
RESULTS: In temporal validation, the BTCH-AOMI score achieved moderate discrimination (AUC: 0.744, 95% CI: 0.651-0.834), significantly outperforming the pain-out-of-proportion rule (AUC: 0.521, 95% CI: 0.441-0.601; P = 0.002). Observed AOMI rates across validation strata (0-1, 2-3, and 4-5 points) were 25.0%, 45.5%, and 88.2%, respectively. A threshold of ≥ 2 points yielded a sensitivity of 71.4% and specificity of 64.3%; a threshold of ≥ 1 point yielded 95.2% sensitivity and 23.2% specificity.
CONCLUSIONS: The BTCH-AOMI score demonstrates moderate temporal discrimination and superior performance over traditional "pain-out-of-proportion" assessment. It is intended strictly as an adjunct for risk stratification and prioritization within emergency CTA pathways, not as a tool to exclude AOMI or replace CTA imaging.
43077095:
BACKGROUND: Superabsorbent polymer (SAP) beads are expandable hydrogel products increasingly recognized as pediatric foreign bodies capable of causing intestinal obstruction. Although infants and young children represent most reported cases, factors associated with serious outcomes remain unclear. This systematic review evaluated clinical features, diagnostic challenges, treatment strategies, and factors associated with serious outcomes after pediatric SAP bead ingestion.
METHODS: A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and CNKI were searched from the earliest indexed records through March 2026. Pediatric case reports and case series describing SAP bead ingestion were included. Demographic characteristics, clinical manifestations, imaging findings, anatomical involvement, interventions, and outcomes were extracted. Exploratory analyses assessed factors associated with serious outcomes.
RESULTS: The review included 58 reports describing 107 pediatric bead-related cases. The primary analysis comprised 62 known-age ingestion cases; 57/62 (91.9%) underwent at least one procedural intervention and 53/62 (85.5%) underwent surgery. Among the 62 cases, 49 (79.0%) involved children aged ≤ 18 months. Age ≤ 18 months was not associated with serious outcomes (OR 0.99, p = 1.000). Serious outcomes were associated with multiple-bead ingestion (OR 3.55, p = 0.044), multiple gastrointestinal-site involvement (OR 5.19, p = 0.007), duodenal involvement (OR 4.48, p = 0.022), and retained or missed beads documented during treatment (OR 299.67, p < 0.001). Imaging was performed in 50/62 (80.6%) cases; findings were discordant in 34/36 (94.4%) cases receiving multiple modalities. Ultrasonography had the highest positive-detection proportion (27/32, 84.4%), but an exploratory comparison did not show shorter time to intervention or fewer serious outcomes among children who underwent ultrasonography.
CONCLUSION: Published cases show that water-bead ingestion can cause intestinal obstruction requiring procedural treatment. In this selected case-report literature, young age alone was not associated with serious outcomes, whereas bead burden, anatomical extent, and retained or missed beads were associated with greater severity. These exploratory associations are vulnerable to selection bias, sparse data, and confounding and should not be interpreted as independent predictors.
43077138: Quantitative optical coherence tomography (OCT) measurements are essential for retinal disease monitoring, yet leading vendors store acquisition data in undocumented proprietary formats or encode measurements exclusively in private DICOM tags inaccessible to open systems, obstructing interoperability between devices and standards-based clinical imaging infrastructure. We present Transducin, an open-source Python library that reverse-engineers two undocumented proprietary OCT formats (the Optopol REVO FC130/REVO 60 .OPT binary format and the Zeiss Cirrus HD-OCT 500 private DICOM tags) through systematic binary analysis cross-referenced against DICOM-exported metadata from the same studies, and converts the recovered measurements into standard, vendor-neutral DICOM TID 1500 Structured Reports with SNOMED-CT coded findings. Format stability was validated across SOCT software versions 11.5.0-21.5.0, spanning approximately 8 years of development; a laterality-inference hypothesis derived from the device's scan-geometry parameters was tested against known eye assignment; and all generated DICOM objects were checked against pydicom's conformance validator and ingested into a clinical PACS. The validation corpus comprised 475 Optopol .OPT files across two clinical sites: 387 at Site A (Chihuahua; 73 patients) and 88 at Site B (Querétaro), spanning three device models and four SOCT software versions with 100% parse success across nine acquisition types. The Zeiss Cirrus pipeline generated TID 1500 SRs for all 41 applicable studies (100%), yielding CMT 203-630 µm and RNFL 53-123 µm across a clinically representative range. A scan-geometry parameter recorded by the device (OCTPARAMS tag 23, the horizontal position of the foveal or disc reflex relative to scan center) was found to encode ocular laterality through its arithmetic sign-an anatomical consequence of the fovea's nasal position relative to the optic disc-and this laterality-inference method was validated across 18 files from two device models and two software versions with 100% accuracy, requiring no operator data entry or filename convention. Transducin provides the first publicly documented specification of the Optopol .OPT format and the first open-source multivendor pipeline generating SNOMED-CT coded DICOM Structured Reports from both Optopol REVO and Zeiss Cirrus devices, closing a gap explicitly confirmed by both manufacturers' own documentation and final users experience. The code is available at https://github.com/oftalmos-org/transducin (Apache License 2.0).
43077139: Radiopharmaceutical information in imaging systems is typically recorded as free text or as flat code system entries that include little or no computable information about radionuclides' physical properties. This article introduces the Nuclide and Element Ontology (NUCLEON), a machine-processable knowledge resource that represents the 118 known chemical elements and 5408 nuclides, including 2019 metastable isomers, with computable nuclear properties. The ontology declares each element and nuclide as both a class and an individual: the class structure generates a taxonomy that aligns with vocabularies of chemistry and clinical medicine, and the individual entities support quantitative assertions, such as half-life. Each of 7691 decay branches is an individual specifying its mode of decay and branching ratio; 7399 branches have an explicit link to their decay product (daughter) nuclide, derived from the decay mode rather than transcribed. Ground-state data were taken from the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) LiveChart of Nuclides, isomer data from the NUBASE2020 evaluation, and the energies and yields of 3990 radiation emissions of clinically coded radionuclides and their decay chains from International Commission on Radiological Protection (ICRP) Publication 107; symbols and names were verified against standard chemical nomenclature. NUCLEON is linked to the Ontology of Chemical Elements, SNOMED Clinical Terms, and DICOM radiopharmaceutical isotope and PET radionuclide code sequences, allowing a nuclide to be resolved directly from a DICOM header. The ontology incorporates 215,862 triples across 5533 classes and 17,253 named individuals. Automated checks confirmed the arithmetic consistency of atomic, neutron, and mass numbers, and none of the derived decay products disagreed with ICRP Publication 107 or the Evaluated Nuclear Structure Data File. Element names are provided in seven languages. NUCLEON is available at https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/NUCLEON .
43077153: Cognitive training can strengthen executive functions, which are essential for adaptive behavior, yet evidence integrating cognitive and neural adaptations in healthy adults remains limited. This systematic review (PROSPERO: CRD420251107775), conducted according to PRISMA 2020, synthesized 26 publications examining executive function training and cognitive and neural outcomes in healthy adults. These comprised 24 randomized controlled trial publications and two quasi-experimental studies, representing 24 independent samples (N = 1,303; intervention = 667; control = 636).
