Cognitive improvements were most consistently reported for working memory and inhibitory control, although transfer varied across studies and several trials reported null findings. Neural evidence showed more consistent training-related changes in functional than structural measures, particularly involving electrophysiological dynamics and prefrontal or frontoparietal systems, whereas structural findings were more heterogeneous. Thirteen publications examined cognitive-neural associations across structural, functional, hemodynamic, metabolic, and electrophysiological measures; however, these relationships were heterogeneous and not consistently observed. Cognitive and neural changes were therefore not uniformly coupled, limiting mechanistic interpretations. Methodological constraints included small samples, short interventions, heterogeneous training and outcome measures, and limited availability of prespecified analysis plans. Overall, the evidence supports training-related cognitive and neural plasticity but indicates important limits to broad transfer and consistent brain-behavior convergence. Larger, longer, prospectively registered studies integrating cognitive and neural outcomes are needed to establish the durability, generalizability, and functional significance of these effects.
43077224:
BACKGROUND: AI is entering oncology workflows faster than evidence on stakeholder acceptance, trust, and sustained use. Existing syntheses rarely distinguish anticipated attitudes from actual use across oncology stakeholders.
OBJECTIVE: The aim of the study is to synthesize primary empirical evidence on stakeholder acceptance, trust, and implementation of AI in oncology and examine variation by stakeholder group, clinical task, AI exposure, and implementation maturity.
METHODS: We conducted a Joanna Briggs Institute-guided mixed methods systematic review with convergent integrated synthesis; the protocol was registered before formal eligibility screening. Eight databases were searched without date or language limits (August 6-9, 2026), yielding 46,206 records and 31,802 unique records. Title and abstract screening used 2 balanced primary allocations, joint bidirectional readjudication, and blinded verification of a stratified 10% (n=3182) sample. Full-text assessment, extraction, and critical appraisal were dual independent. Acceptance/Trust modes and F1-F8 coverage were independently coded across 309 studies and reconciled. Eight integrated findings were anchored to the nonadoption, abandonment, scale-up, spread, and sustainability framework; an emergent economic finding was reported separately. Adjusted stage models controlled for study design, publication format, and publication period; robustness analyses examined screening provenance and appraisal sensitivity.
RESULTS: We included 309 primary empirical studies; 187 (60.5%) were published in 2025 or 2026. Exposure ranged from hypothetical opinion to real-world implementation (n=82 studies), but only 6 described routine use. Acceptance was empirically assessed in 267 studies and Trust in 127. Relative to anticipatory stage 1, Acceptance assessment was less frequent in evaluated-interaction stage 2 (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.07, 95% CI 0.02-0.25; P<.001) and stages 3+4 (aOR 0.12, 95% CI 0.03-0.45; P=.001). Transparency/explainability coverage (F3) was lower in stages 3+4 (aOR 0.20, 95% CI 0.08-0.47; q<0.001). Workflow/interoperability coverage (F5) was higher and governance coverage (F7) lower in both later contrasts after false discovery rate correction. Trust declined descriptively across stages, but adjusted contrasts were nonsignificant. Eight integrated findings spanned clinical value, performance, transparency, oversight, workflow, readiness, governance, and implementation, plus an emergent stage 1 economic finding. The principal Acceptance, F3, F5, and F7 findings persisted in the 229-study original screening subset.
CONCLUSIONS: In oncology, the AI evidence profile appears to differ from anticipated use to implementation. Acceptance was empirically assessed most often before deployment; later-stage studies more often examined workflow and less often examined transparency and governance. The challenge is whether favorable attitudes and early deployment translate into calibrated, governed, and sustained routine use. An interpretive stage-specific model identifies assessment priorities across exposure and implementation contexts, but is not a validated causal or predictive model. Later-stage evaluations should retain measurement of Acceptance, trust calibration, governance, durability, and workflow outcomes.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: OSF Registries osf.io/nmep8; https://osf.io/nmep8.
43078081:
PURPOSE: Metachronous upper tract urothelial carcinoma after non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer is uncommon and attributable to high-risk disease. Intermediate-risk non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer is biologically heterogeneous. Whether this translates into differences in upper tract risk is unclear.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We performed a retrospective multicenter study of 2,094 patients with intermediate-risk non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer treated with transurethral resection between 2005 and 2025. Patients were stratified according to International Bladder Cancer Group criteria into low, intermediate, and high subgroups. The primary endpoint was upper tract urothelial carcinoma developing at least six months after diagnosis. Fine-Gray competing risks regression evaluated predictors.
RESULTS: 16 developed UTUC during follow-up. Cumulative incidence increased stepwise across subgroups, reaching 0.20%, 0.99%, and 3.5% at 10 years in low, intermediate, and high subgroups. Nine developed high-grade UTUC. UTUC was most commonly identified after abnormal upper tract imaging, with no cases diagnosed based on radiographic findings alone. Early bladder cancer recurrence within one year (sHR 7.38, 95% CI 2.86-19.02, p < 0.001) and ureteral stent placement (sHR 12.29, 95% CI 3.11-48.58, p < 0.001) were significantly associated with upper tract development on univariable analysis.
CONCLUSIONS: Upper tract urothelial carcinoma after intermediate-risk non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer is rare overall but occurs more frequently in patients with high-risk intermediate features. Early recurrence and ureteral stent placement were associated with increased upper tract risk. These findings highlight heterogeneity within intermediate-risk disease and may inform surveillance strategies.
43078326:
OBJECTIVE: Publication on physician-modified endografts (PMEGs) has grown rapidly. We examined whether this reflects an expanding evidence base or repeated publication from a limited number of clinical programs, and whether comparative studies support the comparisons they report.
METHODS: We systematically reviewed PMEG publications in Scopus, Web of Science, and MEDLINE/PubMed through August 20, 2026, following PRISMA 2020, PRISMA-S, and BIBLIO, with a supplementary ClinicalTrials.gov search. Studies with ≥20 PMEG patients were rated across five exploratory evidence-maturity domains, assigned to inferred cohort-overlap families, and, when comparative, assessed with ROBINS-I for perioperative mortality. Analyses added during peer review are labeled post hoc; no comparative meta-analysis was performed. The review was retrospectively registered in OSF (DOI: 10.17605/OSF.IO/A9YTB).
RESULTS: Of 340 publications, 88.8% appeared from 2020 onward. Of 100 full texts assessed, 72 studies were included; 52 belonged to 12 multi-report families. Summed cohorts comprised 8,885 patient counts. Retaining one record per family gave 4,524 (50.9%); alternative family definitions gave 3,980 to 4,694 (44.8%-52.8%), and additionally excluding the two largest multicenter aggregates gave 2,706 (30.5%). These are documentary estimates, not verified counts of unique patients. No study rated high across all five maturity domains. All 16 comparative studies were at serious (n = 11) or critical (n = 5) risk of bias, chiefly from confounding by urgency, anatomy, or treatment era.
CONCLUSIONS: About half of the summed PMEG patient count in the published literature is independently attributable, and no comparative study achieves better than serious risk of bias because PMEG use is closely tied to urgency and device availability. Observational comparisons between PMEGs and company-manufactured devices should be read as comparisons of different clinical contexts rather than evidence of device equivalence. These findings do not question the clinical role of PMEGs. Standardized reporting of cohort overlap, indication, and surveillance would make future series independently interpretable.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Clinicians, guideline writers, and regulators should read PMEG series as belonging to identifiable programs rather than as independent replications, and should not interpret observational comparisons of PMEGs with company-manufactured devices as simple device comparisons, because treatment allocation is frequently inseparable from urgency and device availability.
43078388:
PURPOSE: To evaluate embolization outcomes for congenital renal arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) and the impact of an evolving angiographic classification-guided strategy on renal parenchymal preservation.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 29 patients (33 sessions; 25 women; mean age, 52.0 ± 11.8 years) treated between 2010 and 2025. AVMs were categorized according to Do's angiographic classification. For type I AVMs, treatment transitioned from transarterial coils to through-and-through vascular plug embolization. For type IIIb AVMs, selective feeder angiography identified common venous targets for transvenous embolization.
RESULTS: AVMs comprised type I (n = 8), type II (n =10), and type IIIb (n =11). Complete devascularization was achieved in 25 patients (86.2%) after one session and all 29 after a second session, yielding 100% final technical success. Clinical success was achieved in all 28 patients with available clinical follow-up (100%), with no recurrence over a mean of 23.9 months. Renal parenchymal infarction occurred in 18 of 20 sessions (90.0%) involving transarterial access (TA alone or TA+TV; mean infarcted area, 22.7%; range, 5-50%) versus none after transvenous, direct percutaenous, or through-and-through approaches. All 4 type I AVMs treated with the through-and-through vascular plug embolization were occluded without infarction. Overall renal function remained stable. Mild adverse events (SIR grade 1) occurred in 5 patients (17.2%), with no adverse events of SIR grade 2 or higher.
CONCLUSIONS: Classification-guided selection of embolization strategies based on AVM architecture and venous anatomy may reduce renal parenchymal injury while preserving treatment efficacy.
43078389:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the safety and efficacy of variceal embolization (VE) combined with partial splenic embolization (PSE) for recurrent variceal bleeding in patients with cavernous transformation of the portal vein (CTPV) who were not candidates for transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS).
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included consecutive patients with CTPV and recurrent gastroesophageal variceal bleeding who underwent VE plus PSE between January 2020 and August 2024. The primary effectiveness endpoint was variceal rebleeding. Secondary endpoints included non-variceal rebleeding, new or worsening ascites, overt hepatic encephalopathy, changes in liver function, and survival time. Safety was assessed by procedure-related complications. Kaplan-Meier analysis was used to evaluate variceal rebleeding and survival.
RESULTS: Twenty-three patients were included, all had noncirrhotic CTPV (100%). Median follow-up was 825 days. Ten patients (43.5%) presented with acute bleeding; bleeding was controlled in all (immediate hemostasis rate, 100%). During follow-up, 11 patients (47.8%) experienced variceal rebleeding, with a median time to rebleeding of 217 days. New or worsening ascites occurred in 2 patients (8.7%). Two patients (8.7%) died. Liver function remained stable, with a significant increase in albumin levels at 1 year (P = .032). No major procedure-related complications were observed.
CONCLUSIONS: VE combined with PSE was feasible and demonstrated an acceptable safety profile in patients with CTPV and recurrent variceal bleeding who were not candidates for TIPS, and it may represent a treatment option in selected high-risk patients.
43078391:
PURPOSE: To develop and evaluate machine learning models integrating radiomic features from pre- and post-transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) CT and MRI with clinical variables to predict 6-month Milan criteria status, overall survival (OS), and time to progression (TTP) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 428 treatment-naive patients with biopsy-confirmed HCC who underwent conventional TACE (2010-2025) with post-TACE CT, pre- and post-TACE MRI, and 6-month imaging follow-up. nnU-Net segmented CT (liver, lipiodol, tumor) and MRI (liver, tumor) compartments, and radiomic features were extracted. Five feature configurations (shape and first-order features, alone and with clinical variables, and both combined with clinical variables) were evaluated. AutoGluon predicted 6-month Milan status, evaluated by repeated 5×5 cross-validation (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC]) and compared with clinical-only and baseline-Milan reference models; OS and TTP were assessed by concordance index (C-index) with leakage-corrected repeated cross-validation.
RESULTS: Cross-validated Milan AUCs were 0.766-0.791 for radiomic configurations, exceeding a clinical-only model (0.711) but not baseline Milan status alone (0.842); adding shape features to clinical variables and baseline Milan status did not improve discrimination (0.874 vs 0.865; P = .43). Shape features with clinical variables had the numerically highest C-index for OS (0.647) and TTP (0.571), without improvement over clinical-only models.
CONCLUSION: Shape descriptors carried most of the imaging signal for 6-month Milan status, adding discrimination beyond clinical variables but not beyond baseline Milan status; survival discrimination was modest (OS) to near chance (TTP).
43078912: Artificial intelligence (AI) represents a suite of tools that identify complex relationships in data to effectively emulate human reasoning. In this comment, we evaluate the clinical readiness of current work on injury prediction and recovery, and large language model-based applications for clinical decision making, sports psychology, and coaching. We further outline the ethical challenges of black-box predictions and bias, which precipitate the need for data governance.
43078962: Chemical risk assessment is undergoing a fundamental transition driven by the need for human-relevant, mechanistically informed, and animal-free approaches. Digital infrastructures that integrate New Approach Methodologies (NAMs), including computational models and emerging artificial intelligence (AI) tools, are increasingly considered drivers of this transition. However, their regulatory uptake depends on several factors, including trust, transparency, scientific validity, and the sustainability of the infrastructures.This paper summarises the outcomes from a multi-stakeholder expert workshop, jointly organised by the European Centre for Ecotoxicology and Toxicology of Chemicals (ECETOC), the VHP4Safety project, and the ONTOX project, focusing on the application of AI-supported digital infrastructures in human health risk assessment of chemicals. The workshop explored technical, regulatory, and governance challenges associated with the integration of AI-supported NAMs into regulatory workflows. This was achieved through demonstrations of two recently developed platforms, the Virtual Human Platform (VHP) and Ontology-driven Probabilistic Risk Assessment (OPRA).Key insights highlight that transparency, traceability and explainability tailored to user needs are necessary for adoption and regulatory acceptance, as well as sustained engagement with regulators. Participants emphasised the importance of platform interoperability, and the need for targeted training for end users. Furthermore, long-term sustainability of digital infrastructures emerged as a critical concern, requiring distinct governance beyond project-based funding.Based on these insights, actionable recommendations for the design, implementation, and governance of AI-supported digital infrastructures to enable regulatory uptake of NAMs are reported. These recommendations are intended to inform developers, regulators and stakeholders advancing next-generation chemical risk assessment across regulatory domains.
43078994:
PURPOSE: Detecting residual or recurrent pituitary adenoma (RPA) by MRI is challenging due to post-surgical or post-radiotherapy tissue remodeling. While [11C]Methionine ([11C]MET) PET demonstrates high diagnostic accuracy and sensitivity for RPA, its use is limited to centers with an on-site cyclotron. [18F]Fluorocholine ([18F]FCH) PET, which has shown incidental uptake in pituitary adenomas, may offer a viable alternative. This study compared dual-phase [18F]FCH with [11C]MET PET imaging for localizing suspected residual or recurrent pituitary adenoma (RPA) and characterizing uptake differences between suspected RPA and pituitary gland remnant (PGR) after surgery.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 23 patients addressed during the follow-up of an ablated pituitary adenoma (n = 23). The presence of suspected RPA was determined by multidisciplinary consensus integrating postoperative metabolic imaging, serial MRI follow-up, and biochemical data. Two patients underwent reoperation, in whom histopathological confirmation was available. All patients underwent a standard [11C]MET PET/MRI acquisition (mean activity = 397 ± 51 MBq) and subsequently a 20-min dynamic [18F]FCH PET/MRI acquisition, followed by an additional late static [18F]FCH PET/CT acquisition performed at 40-55 min post-FCH injection (mean activity = 334 ± 77 MBq). RPA and PGR uptake were compared visually and quantitatively using maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) for both tracers.
RESULTS: All lesions suspected of representing RPA were visually detected on both early and late [18F]FCH images. In suspected RPA, [18F]FCH uptake was comparable to [11C]MET uptake, with mean SUVmax values of 6.2 ± 2.3 for early (3-20 min post-injection) [18F]FCH PET, 5.1 ± 2.3 for late [18F]FCH PET, and 5.5 ± 1.9 for [11C]MET (p = 0.11 and 0.51, respectively). Both suspected RPA and PGR showed decreasing [18F]FCH uptake over time, with a significantly greater decline in PGR (early PET SUVmax: 5.7 ± 1.5; late PET SUVmax: 3.7 ± 1.1; time-by-region interaction, p < 0.0001). Accordingly, the RPA/PGR SUVmax ratio was significantly lower on early [18F]FCH images than on late [18F]FCH images (p = 0.0014) and [11C]MET images (p < 0.001), whereas it did not differ significantly between late [18F]FCH and [11C]MET images (p > 0.5).
CONCLUSION: [18F]FCH PET/MRI demonstrated uptake in lesions suspected of representing RPA, with uptake levels comparable to those observed with [11C]MET PET/MRI. The greater decline in PGR uptake on delayed imaging improved the quantitative RPA/PGR contrast, supporting dual-time-point [18F]FCH PET/MRI as a promising approach for postoperative tissue discrimination. These exploratory findings require prospective validation using an independent reference standard.
43079037:
PURPOSE: Neuromuscular choristoma (NMC) is a rare developmental peripheral nerve lesion characterized by muscle tissue within the affected nerve and a recognized association with NMC-associated desmoid-type fibromatosis (NMC-DTF). Its clinicoradiologic profile and comparison between published and institutional cases remain incompletely defined.
METHODS: A systematic review of the peripheral nerve NMC literature, excluding central nervous system cases, was performed in accordance with PRISMA principles using PubMed and Google Scholar. Published cases meeting imaging and/or biopsy-based diagnostic criteria were compared with retrospectively identified institutional cases. Demographic, clinical, imaging, pathologic, and molecular variables were extracted.
RESULTS: Twenty-nine articles reporting 48 literature cases and 30 institutional cases were included. In both cohorts, NMC most commonly involved large proximal nerves, particularly the sciatic nerve and brachial plexus, and was frequently associated with weakness, nerve-territory undergrowth, and NMC-DTF. Institutional cases were more likely to undergo MRI and PET imaging, and be managed without biopsy. MRI was performed in all institutional cases and in 35 literature cases, whereas PET was used in 12 and 2 cases, respectively. CTNNB1 alterations were identified in both NMC and NMC-DTF.
CONCLUSIONS: NMC is a rare but distinctive lesion with a recognizable clinicoradiologic phenotype, most commonly affecting the sciatic nerve. Contemporary diagnosis appears increasingly imaging-based, supporting a no-touch approach and reinforcing the biologic link between NMC and NMC-DTF.
43079060: Small and disseminated lesions within the bone marrow remain challenging to detect and eradicate in multiple myeloma (MM), highlighting the need for targeted approaches capable of both sensitive imaging and localized radiation delivery. CD38 is highly expressed on malignant plasma cells and represents an established target in MM, but CD38-directed radiopharmaceuticals with rapid tumor targeting and favorable pharmacokinetics remain limited. Here, we developed CP021, a high-affinity CD38-targeting cyclic peptide, and evaluated [⁶⁸Ga]Ga-DOTA-CP021 for PET imaging, together with [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-DOTA-CP021 and [²¹²Pb]Pb-DOTAM-CP021 for targeted radionuclide therapy in preclinical MM models.MethodsDOTA-CP021 was labeled with ⁶⁸Ga or ¹⁷⁷Lu and DOTAM-CP021 with ²¹²Pb. Radiochemical properties, PET imaging, biodistribution, pharmacokinetics, dosimetry, therapeutic efficacy, and safety were evaluated in MM xenograft models.ResultsAll radioconjugates showed > 95% radiochemical purity and good stability. [⁶⁸Ga]Ga-DOTA-CP021 demonstrated CD38-dependent tumor uptake; at 60 min, uptake in CD38-high MOLP-8 xenografts was 12.35 ± 1.37%ID/g, 1.8- and 3.1-fold higher than in MM.1 S and U266B1 tumors, respectively. [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-DOTA-CP021 produced activity-dependent tumor growth inhibition and prolonged survival. Repeated [²¹²Pb]Pb-DOTAM-CP021 further improved tumor control, extending median survival to 36.5 and 47 days at cumulative activities of 0.555 and 1.11 MBq, respectively, versus 16 days with PBS (P < 0.001). No overt treatment-related toxicity was observed.ConclusionCP021 provides a versatile CD38-targeted radiotheranostic platform combining rapid molecular imaging with β- and α-particle therapy. Its performance across radionuclides supports further development for detecting and treating CD38-positive MM lesions.
43079090:
PURPOSE: To develop and validate an integrated PET/CT‑based radiomic model that combines tumour characteristics and whole‑body composition features for predicting progression‑free survival (PFS) in patients with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC).
METHODS: This multicentre retrospective study included 477 patients with pathologically confirmed ESCC who underwent pretreatment [¹⁸F]FDG‑PET/CT. Patients were allocated to training (n = 294), internal validation (n = 74), and external validation (n = 109) cohorts. Primary tumours and whole‑body composition components, including skeletal muscle, subcutaneous adipose tissue, visceral adipose tissue, intermuscular adipose tissue and spine, were automatically segmented on PET/CT images. Radiomic features were extracted from both tumour and body‑composition regions. Feature selection and model development were performed using machine learning approaches. A composite clinical-tumour-body composition model was constructed and compared with clinical and tumour‑radiomic models.
RESULTS: The integrated model showed superior prognostic performance over individual models, achieving C‑indices of 0.802 (95% CI: 0.770-0.832), 0.716 (95% CI: 0.639-0.797), and 0.732 (95% CI: 0.660-0.796) in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts, respectively. The corresponding AUCs for 3‑year PFS prediction were 0.895 (95% CI: 0.858-0.930), 0.831 (95% CI: 0.727-0.923), and 0.772 (95% CI: 0.639-0.895). The model stratified patients into high‑ and low‑risk groups, with significantly different PFS between the two strata across all cohorts (log‑rank P < 0.05). Decision curve analysis supported the clinical utility of the integrated model.
CONCLUSIONS: A PET/CT‑based radiomic model integrating clinical, tumour, and whole‑body composition features provides robust, externally validated postoperative prognostic stratification for ESCC. This approach may facilitate individualised risk assessment and inform treatment decision‑making.
43079095: A 33-year-old woman presented with long-standing abdominal distension and unexplained ascites. Serum CA125 levels were significantly elevated. Abdominal CT revealed a cystic lesion in the left adnexal region with massive ascites. To determine the etiology, 18F-FDG PET/CT was performed after fasting for at least 6 h. The adnexal lesion showed no appreciable FDG uptake, favoring a benign cystic lesion. Unexpectedly,​ heterogeneous hypermetabolism was found along the right heart border. Because the interpretation of cardiac FDG findings may be confounded by physiological or nonspecific myocardial uptake, ¹⁸F-FAPI PET/CT was subsequently performed for further characterization, which revealed a more extensive and conspicuous tracer uptake within the cardiac lesion than FDG PET/CT, more clearly delineating its extent. The patient subsequently underwent partial surgical resection of the cardiac mass with biopsy. Histomorphological, immunohistochemical, and molecular findings supported the diagnosis of cardiac spindle cell sarcoma with partial myofibroblastic differentiation. This case reports a rare primary cardiac spindle cell sarcoma and highlights the complementary value of FDG and FAPI PET/CT in evaluating primary cardiac malignancies. It also underscores the importance of multimodal imaging in guiding differential diagnosis and clinical management.
43079102:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: [89Zr]Zr-girentuximab is a PET radiotracer targeting carbonic anhydrase IX (CAIX), a biomarker highly expressed in clear-cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC). Following the high diagnostic accuracy demonstrated in the phase III ZIRCON trial, this study evaluated the real-world clinical performance and management impact of [89Zr]Zr-girentuximab PET/CT in patients with indeterminate renal masses and advanced ccRCC.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: Within an early access program, patients with renal lesions of uncertain origin underwent [89Zr]Zr-girentuximab PET/CT for noninvasive lesion characterization, while patients with advanced ccRCC were imaged for postoperative assessment, recurrence evaluation, or metastatic restaging. Following intravenous administration of 37 MBq (± 10%) [89Zr]Zr-girentuximab, PET/CT was performed on day 5 post-injection. Findings were correlated with histopathology where available, and their impact on clinical management was assessed retrospectively.
RESULTS: Twenty-eight patients (22 men, 6 women; mean age, 71 ± 9 years) were included: 18 with indeterminate renal masses (Group A) and 10 undergoing postoperative, metastatic, or restaging evaluation (Group B). In Group A, PET/CT demonstrated CAIX-positive findings in 10/18 patients (56%) and CAIX-negative findings in 7/18 (39%); one patient showed heterogeneous tracer uptake. Histopathological confirmation was available in 11/18 patients (61%). Within this verified subset, patient-level PET/CT findings were concordant with histopathology, with all CAIX-positive patients (6/6) confirmed as ccRCC and all CAIX-negative patients (5/5) confirmed as non-ccRCC or benign. At the lesion level, however, concordance was incomplete in one patient: four CAIX-avid lesions were identified, two of which were confirmed as ccRCC, while the remaining two corresponded to an angiomyolipoma and normal renal parenchyma. PET/CT findings were associated with a subsequent change in the documented management plan in 11/18 patients (61%; 95% CI, 35.7-82.7%). In the exploratory Group B cohort, [89Zr]Zr-girentuximab PET/CT demonstrated the presence or absence of detectable CAIX-avid findings and contributed to therapeutic and surveillance decisions.
CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world cohort, [89Zr]Zr-girentuximab PET/CT showed concordance with histopathology in the limited verified subset and was associated with changes in clinical management, supporting further prospective evaluation in indeterminate renal masses and advanced ccRCC.
43079112:
PURPOSE: To evaluate "pseudoenhancement" in adnexal lesions on low kiloelectron volt (keV) virtual monoenergetic images (VMI) at photon-counting CT (PCCT) and to establish optimal attenuation change thresholds for distinguishing enhancing from nonenhancing lesions at each VMI.
METHODS: Adult women who underwent contrast-enhanced abdominopelvic PCCT and pelvic MRI or ultrasound (US) within 180 days were identified via retrospective PACS search. Adnexal lesions were classified as enhancing or nonenhancing using MRI or US as the reference standard. Quantitative attenuation measurements were obtained using regions-of-interest at VMI levels (70, 67, 60, 55, 50, 45, and 40 keV). "Pseudoenhancement" was defined as ≥ 20 Hounsfield units (HU) increase between the VMI and virtual unenhanced (VUE) images. The diagnostic performance of a 20HU change to define enhancement at each VMI level was assessed. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was used to determine optimal thresholds by maximizing the Youden index. Inter-reader agreement was evaluated with intraclass correlation coefficients.
RESULTS: Forty-five women (median [IQR] age 46 years [37, 54] ) with 30 nonenhancing and 15 enhancing adnexal lesions were included. No "pseudoenhancement" was observed at 70 or 67 keV; however, "pseudoenhancement" was observed in 3.3% of patients at 60 keV, increasing to 26.7% at 40 keV. Using a 20 HU change to indicate enhancement had 47% sensitivity with 100% specificity at 70 keV and 93% sensitivity with 73% specificity at 40 keV. Optimal attenuation thresholds increased with decreasing energy, from 10.0 HU at 70 keV to 36.3 HU at 40 keV. Notably, at 60 keV, the threshold was 19.1HU. Inter-reader agreement was near perfect (ICC = 0.858, 95%CI = 0.756-0.920).
CONCLUSION: "Pseudoenhancement" of adnexal lesions occurs with increasing frequency with decreasing keV below 60 keV, but there was no "pseudoenhancement" at 67 or 70 keV. Energy-specific attenuation thresholds improve adnexal lesion characterization.
43079113:
AIMS: To synthesize available evidence on the effectiveness of conservative rehabilitation strategies for piriformis syndrome, emphasizing pain reduction and functional improvement.
METHODS: Conducted per PRISMA 2020 guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251154880), this review searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science and PEDro for studies published between January 2015 and 2026. Eligible designs included randomized controlled trials (RCTs), non-randomized studies and case reports on rehabilitation interventions. Risk of bias and methodological quality were assessed using Cochrane RoB2, ROBINS-I, and the Downs and Black checklist. Evidence certainty was evaluated via the GRADE framework in accordance with SWiM guidelines. Due to heterogeneity, data were synthesized narratively.
RESULTS: Forty-two studies (1,971 participants) met the inclusion criteria. Multimodal rehabilitation programs generally yielded better outcomes than single-modality approaches. Manual therapies, specifically myofascial release and muscle energy techniques, were more effective than stretching alone for pain and functional recovery. Exercises emphasizing hip abductor and extensor strengthening were crucial for successful management. In refractory cases, adjuncts like extracorporeal shockwave therapy, ultrasound-guided dry needling, and botulinum toxin injections provided potential benefits for sustained pain reduction. However, overall evidence strength remained limited due to small, heterogeneous studies with high or unclear risk of bias.
CONCLUSION: Current evidence supports an active, multimodal rehabilitation approach for piriformis syndrome, prioritizing targeted manual therapy and strengthening exercises. While promising, the evidence base is limited by methodological shortcomings. High-quality, adequately powered RCTs with standardized protocols are required to establish definitive clinical recommendations.
43079160:
BACKGROUND: The association between primary hyperparathyroidism (PHPT) and cardiovascular (CV) risk remains unclear. Endothelial dysfunction and arterial wall thickening are early markers of CV risk. We performed a systematic review to evaluate (a) the association between PHPT and these vascular parameters, assessed by flow-mediated dilation (FMD) and carotid intima-media thickness (cIMT), and (b) the impact of parathyroidectomy on these outcomes.
METHODS: Studies assessing FMD and/or cIMT in PHPT were retrieved from Embase and MEDLINE up to November 2025 (PROSPERO: CRD420251076642). Risk of bias was evaluated using Cochrane criteria. Mean differences (MD) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated using random-effects models. Heterogeneity was assessed with the I² statistic. Analyses were conducted using Review Manager 5.4.1.
RESULTS: Twenty-nine observational studies (1,152 PHPT patients and 1,773 healthy controls) were included. PHPT patients had significantly lower FMD (MD -6.44, 95% CI: -9.80, -3.08; P = 0.0002; I2 = 98%) and higher cIMT (MD 0.07, 95% CI: 0.04, 0.11; P < 0.0001; I2 = 86%) than controls. Following parathyroidectomy, FMD improved (MD 5.88, 95% CI: 1.77, 9.99; P = 0.005; I2 = 97%), reaching values comparable with controls (MD -1.27, 95% CI: -3.48, 0.94; P = 0.26; I2 = 69%); cIMT decreased (MD -0.05, 95% CI: -0.08, -0.02; P = 0.004; I2 = 71%), with values not different from controls (MD 0.01, 95% CI: -0.02, 0.03; P = 0.62; I2 = 0%).
CONCLUSION: PHPT is associated with endothelial dysfunction and arterial wall thickening, suggesting increased CV risk. FMD and cIMT significantly improve after parathyroidectomy.
43079278:
BACKGROUND: Transmural inflammation is a hallmark of Crohn's disease (CD), a chronic inflammatory bowel disease that exposes patients to serious consequences such as fistulas and abscesses. Iliopsoas abscess (IPA) is an uncommon but potentially fatal penetrating (extra-luminal) complication of CD that frequently arises from the direct extension of transmural inflammation into the iliopsoas compartment. Because data on this entity are derived almost exclusively from isolated case reports and small case series, the current literature provides a fragmented understanding of its clinical behaviour, microbiology, and optimal management.
AIM OF THE STUDY: The aim of this study was to summarize the available data on the clinical presentation, diagnostic methods, microbiological profile, treatment plans, and results of IPA in patients with CD by methodically reviewing and analyzing published case reports and case series.
METHODS: This systematic review was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420251164473) and carried out in accordance with PRISMA 2020 principles. To find relevant studies, a thorough search of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar was conducted through February 2025. Case studies and case series describing CD patients who created an IPA were included. Data on demographics, clinical features, diagnostics, microbiology, management, and outcomes were extracted from 53 eligible studies. The Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) critical assessment methods for case reports and case series were used to evaluate the methodological quality of the included studies.
RESULTS: A total of 53 studies including information on 86 individuals were included, comprising 38 case reports and 15 case series. The mean patient age was 30.5 ± 12.9 years, and 55/86 (64.0%) were male. Fever (25/86; 29.1%), abdominal pain (18/86; 20.9%), and combined hip/flank/back pain (23/86; 26.7%) were the most frequently reported presenting features. Cross-sectional imaging was the cornerstone of diagnosis; CT was the most commonly utilised modality (56/86; 65.1%), followed by ultrasound (55/86; 64.0%) and MRI (52/86; 60.5%); most patients underwent more than one modality during workup. Microbiological data from abscess fluid culture were available in 72/86 patients (83.7%); the majority of isolates were polymicrobial enteric organisms, with Escherichia coli being most frequently identified. Management was typically combined: medical therapy (mainly antibiotics) was documented in 68/86 (79.1%) and surgical or interventional management in 78/86 (90.7%). The overall recovery rate was good, although recurrence was observed-particularly in patients treated with drainage alone without addressing the underlying intestinal disease.
CONCLUSION: IPA is a complication of CD that frequently presents with non-specific symptoms, leading to diagnostic delay. Cross-sectional imaging and a high index of suspicion are essential for early diagnosis. Improving clinical outcomes and preventing recurrence require a multidisciplinary approach that includes aggressive source control through drainage, appropriate antimicrobial therapy, and definitive management of the underlying CD, which frequently includes surgical resection and the subsequent consideration of biologic therapy.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.
43079284:
BACKGROUND: Endovascular revascularization is a cornerstone therapy for peripheral artery disease (PAD), typically guided by angiography, which may underestimate vessel size and lesion complexity. The clinical benefit of intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) guidance remains uncertain. This systemic review and meta-analysis compare clinical outcomes of IVUS-guided versus angiography-guided endovascular interventions in patients with PAD.
METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Cochrane, Scopus, Web of Science, EMBASE, and Google Scholar were searched from inception through January 30, 2026, for randomized and observational studies of adults with PAD undergoing endovascular interventions with IVUS versus angiography. Primary outcomes were primary patency, target lesion revascularization (TLR), and late lumen loss. Secondary outcomes included major adverse limb events, amputation, procedural success, and ankle-brachial index improvement. Random-effects meta-analysis was performed using R version 3.4.3.
RESULTS: Twenty-three studies encompassing 1,232,018 patients were included. There was no significant difference between IVUS-guided and angiography-guided interventions (RR 1.03; 95% CI 0.81-1.23; p = 0.75; i2 = 60.3%) or freedom from TLR (RR 1.21; 95% CI 0.96-1.54; p = 0.08; I2 = 58.6%).
CONCLUSION: IVUS-guided endovascular interventions in PAD were associated with reduced all-cause mortality, but similar limb-related outcomes compared with angiography guidance. However, these findings are based predominantly on observational evidence. Large-scale randomized trials are needed to confirm these findings and identify patient subgroups that would benefit from IVUS-guided strategies.
43079417:
BACKGROUND: Nivolumab-associated hypophysitis is a rare endocrine immune-related adverse event with incompletely defined clinical characteristics and management. This study aimed to synthesize patient-level evidence to clarify its presentation, treatment, and clinical outcomes, thereby facilitating earlier recognition and evidence-based management.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, case-based synthesis of nivolumab-induced hypophysitis. PubMed, EMBASE, Web of Science, WanFang Data, and CNKI were systematically searched for reports published up to Jan 31, 2026, using a combination of MeSH terms: ("nivolumab" OR "PD-1 inhibitor" OR "programmed death-1 inhibitor" OR "immune checkpoint inhibitor" OR "ICI") AND ("hypophysitis" OR "pituitary inflammation" OR "hypopituitarism") AND ("immune-related adverse event" OR "irAE" OR "endocrinopathy").
RESULTS: Among 2,264 records screened, 38 case reports and case series comprising 40 patients were included in the final analysis. Median age was 62 years (range 26-84), and 72.5% were male. Hypophysitis occurred most often in melanoma (42.5%) and renal cell carcinoma (30.0%), with a median onset of 20 weeks. Fatigue (82.5%), anorexia/nausea (65.0%), and hyponatremia (42.5%) were common; pituitary MRI abnormalities were reported in 46.2%. Endocrine testing mainly showed central adrenal insufficiency with central hypothyroidism; median cortisol and ACTH were 2.9 µg/dL and 38.0 pg/mL. All patients received corticosteroids, 35.0% received levothyroxine, and nivolumab was discontinued in 80.0%. Among 16 rechallenged patients, relapse occurred in 18.8%. Clinical improvement was frequent (92.5%), whereas full hormonal recovery was uncommon.
CONCLUSION: Nivolumab-induced hypophysitis primarily involves the corticotropic axis. Early hormonal evaluation and imaging are essential. Corticosteroids remain the mainstay of treatment, and long-term hormone replacement is often necessary. Rechallenge with nivolumab may be considered in selected patients, but requires careful risk-benefit assessment.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.
43079669:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) claims 18.6 million lives annually worldwide. Caribbean nations are particularly vulnerable to CVDs, as by Western standards they are largely comprised of racial/ethnic minorities and classified as Low-and Middle-Income Countries (LMICs); with race/ethnicity and socioeconomics affecting health outcomes. Cardiac pathology phenotypes (morphologic descriptions) can guide targeted diagnostics and therapeutics, yet despite this, there exists paucity of literature on Afro-Caribbean cardiac pathologies. This scoping review mapped existing cardiac pathology phenotyping literature across thirteen predominantly Black Caribbean nations and the diaspora; summarizing existing data, identifying gaps and setting the stage to prioritize future CVD cohort studies to reduce Afro-Caribbean under representation in the medical literature.
METHODS: This review was conducted following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) guidelines. Four academic databases (PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science and Bireme - Latin America and the Caribbean Literature on Health Sciences), and Google Scholar were queried with predefined search terms to obtain articles in English between 1990 - 2025, with Afro-Caribbeans from 13 nations or diaspora (United States of America (USA), Europe or Canada), with cardiac pathology phenotyping data derived from ECG, imaging or autopsy.
RESULTS: Forty studies featuring 17 cardiac foci across 9 countries were identified with the United Kingdom (UK) having the most (13). Seventeen were cross-sectional, 9 prospective cohorts, 6 retrospective cohorts, 5 retrospective case series, 1 prospective case series, and 2 case-control studies. Foci included left ventricular structure/function (9), heart failure (6), peripartum cardiomyopathy (4), ischemic heart disease (4), transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (3), valvulopathies (2), cardiorenal disorders (2), and miscellaneous (10). Sample sizes ranged from N = 15 to 5329, with N ≥ 100 in 22 of the 40 studies. Phenotyping utilized echocardiography (31), ECG (13), stress echocardiography (1), CT angiography (1), coronary angiography (2), cardiac MRI (1), and transesophageal echocardiography (2).
CONCLUSIONS: A review of literature on cardiac pathology phenotypes in Afro-Caribbean populations was performed, demonstrating paucity of large, prospective studies and use of advanced imaging, resulting in scarcity of data. Future work should prioritize multicenter cohorts, standardized multimodal imaging, and longitudinal follow-up to describe phenotypes and regional epidemiology and potentially guide resource allocation.
43079768:
PURPOSE: To develop and validate a region-adaptive tractography framework that integrates multi-scale diffusion metrics, specifically fractional anisotropy (FA), asymmetric index (ASI) from asymmetric fiber orientation distribution functions, and diffusion tensor distribution (DTD)-derived microscopic fractional anisotropy (μFA) to improve anatomical fidelity in complex white matter configurations.
METHODS: MS-Track, a rule-based region-adaptive tractography method, was proposed to classify local fiber configurations (parallel, crossing, bending, termination) using FA, ASI, and μFA. Streamline seeding, peak sampling, curvature tolerance, and termination were dynamically modulated according to configuration. Validation was performed on the ISMRM 2015 Tractography Challenge phantom and in vivo data acquired with the DTD protocol from 20 healthy subjects, 20 arteriovenous malformation (AVM) patients, and 2 glioma patients.
RESULTS: On the ISMRM 2015 Challenge dataset, a mean Dice coefficient of 0.700 was achieved by MS-Track, with the highest overlap (68.5%) and the lowest overreach (24.0%) among state-of-the-art methods. In AVM patients, reduced fiber density and elevated μFA and ASI were observed in affected tracts. In glioma cases, μFA increased with tumor grade, consistent with histological findings.
CONCLUSION: Tractography reliability in complex white matter was improved by MS-Track through the integration of complementary microstructural contrasts. DTD-derived μFA provided additional sensitivity to pathological tissue, supporting potential clinical translation in surgical planning and disease characterization.
43079827: Tuberculosis and lung cancer are major global health threats. China faces the dual burden of a prevalent tuberculosis epidemic and high incidence of lung cancer. These two diseases exhibit complex mutual reinforcement relationships, with both demonstrating high prevalence rates and clinical complexity in practice. Due to the similar clinical symptoms and easily confused imaging manifestations, diagnosis and treatment decision-making become more challenging. There is an urgent need for standardized imaging diagnostic consensus to guide clinical practice. To address this, Radiology Professional Committee on Infection and Inflammatory of the Chinese Research Hospital Association and the Beijing Image Diagnosis and Treatment Technology Innovation Alliance organized multidisciplinary experts to develop the Expert consensus on imaging diagnosis of comorbid pulmonary tuberculosis and lung cancer (2026 edition), which outlines 11 recommended guidelines. The consensus emphasizes the central role of integrated diagnosis combining clinical data, imaging findings, etiology, and pathology, recommends low-dose spiral CT for lung cancer screening in tuberculosis patients, and preliminarily defines the value and application scenarios of multimodal imaging (CT, MRI, PET-CT) and artificial intelligence in coexisting disease diagnosis, aiming to enhance the level of imaging diagnosis for tuberculosis-lung cancer comorbidity in clinical practice.
43079866:
PURPOSE: To develop a redundancy-aware frequency offset selection framework for accelerated chemical exchange saturation transfer (CEST) MRI that reduces acquired saturation frequency offsets while preserving quantitative and classification performance.
METHODS: FOCUS, a Frequency Offset selection framework for accelerated CEST MRI Using adaptive Subset-level optimization, was developed to account for inter-offset redundancy beyond individual offset importance. Frequency offset selection was formulated as subset-level optimization, in which candidate subsets were encoded as binary individuals and evaluated by final task performance. An artificial protozoa optimizer-based search scheme was used to explore the subset space, and a deep Q-network adaptively guided the search strategy. FOCUS was evaluated in numerical simulations, in vivo human skeletal muscle phosphocreatine quantification, and glioma molecular subtype classification, and compared with permutation importance analysis, random forest, and channel pruning.
RESULTS: Under reduced frequency-offset sampling, FOCUS outperformed existing methods in both CEST quantification and glioma molecular subtype classification. For CEST quantification, FOCUS achieved the lowest root mean square error in simulations and in vivo skeletal muscle experiments, with the highest structural similarity index and peak signal-to-noise ratio in vivo. For glioma classification, FOCUS achieved the best overall performance in predicting isocitrate dehydrogenase mutation and O6-methylguanine-DNA methyltransferase promoter methylation status.
CONCLUSION: FOCUS enables redundancy-aware frequency offset selection for accelerated CEST MRI, reducing acquired saturation frequency offsets while preserving quantitative accuracy and classification performance.
43080088:
OBJECTIVE: To report the outcomes of fetuses undergoing vesicoamniotic shunting for lower urinary tract obstruction (LUTO).
METHODS: MEDLINE and EMBASE databases were searched electronically from inception to 15 January 2025. The inclusion criteria were studies reporting the outcome of fetuses with isolated LUTO, defined as LUTO with no additional structural anomalies detected at the time of diagnosis, that underwent vesicoamniotic shunt placement. The outcomes observed included: overall fetal loss, defined as miscarriage or intrauterine fetal demise; neonatal death (NND); oligohydramnios at the time of diagnosis; additional structural anomaly detected on follow-up ultrasound assessment after shunt insertion; oligohydramnios at follow-up ultrasound assessment; preterm birth (PTB) < 37, < 32 and < 28 weeks' gestation; preterm prelabor rupture of membranes; shunt dislocation; shunt occlusion; need for shunt reinsertion; pulmonary hypoplasia at birth; abnormal renal function at birth and at pediatric follow-up assessment; need for dialysis; and need for renal transplant. All outcomes were explored in the overall population of fetuses with isolated LUTO. Furthermore, we performed subgroup analyses of fetuses that presented with a normal amniotic fluid volume before shunt placement, those that underwent shunting in the first trimester and analysis according to the type of vesicoamniotic shunt (double pigtail or double basket) used. Random-effects meta-analysis of proportions was used to combine data, and results are reported as pooled proportions with 95% CI.
RESULTS: Overall, 17 studies were included in the systematic review and 15 in the meta-analysis. Overall fetal loss occurred in 10.0% (95% CI, 5.1-16.3%) of fetuses with a prenatal diagnosis of LUTO, and NND occurred in 15.8% (95% CI, 9.5-23.4%). PTB < 37, < 32 and < 28 weeks occurred in 63.3% (95% CI, 43.2-78.1%), 24.8% (95% CI, 12.3-40.0%) and 6.0% (95% CI, 0.4-17.1%) of cases, respectively. Shunt dislocation was reported in 37.2% (95% CI, 24.5-48.5%) of cases. At the follow-up ultrasound scan after shunt insertion, oligohydramnios was reported in 46.4% (95% CI, 27.6-65.7%) of cases. Abnormal renal function at birth and at pediatric follow-up were reported in 53.9% (95% CI, 35.6-71.6%) and 56.0% (95% CI, 39.0-72.4%) of cases, respectively. When considering studies reporting the outcome of fetuses that underwent shunt insertion for LUTO with normal amniotic fluid volume at the time of diagnosis, overall fetal loss occurred in 6.4% (95% CI, 2.6-11.7%) and NND occurred in 10.2% (95% CI, 4.6-17.8%) of cases, while abnormal renal function at birth and at pediatric follow-up assessment were reported in 26.9% (95% CI, 10.4-47.7%) and 28.9% (95% CI, 17.8-41.4%) of cases, respectively. In fetuses that underwent vesicoamniotic shunting in the first trimester (< 14 weeks), the incidence of abnormal renal function at birth was 18.6% (95% CI, 0.5-54.0%). When considering different types of shunt, shunt dislocation was reported in 41.4% (95% CI, 25.7-58.1%) of fetuses with a double-pigtail shunt and 30.3% (95% CI, 19.7-42.0%) of fetuses with a double-basket shunt.
CONCLUSIONS: There is limited evidence on the role of vesicoamniotic shunting in fetuses with LUTO. There was a high observed rate of shunt dislocation and abnormal renal function after birth. Further evidence is needed to elucidate whether the risk of adverse outcome is lower in fetuses presenting with normal amniotic fluid volume before shunt insertion and in those undergoing placement of a double-basket shunt compared with a double-pigtail shunt, as the design of the included studies did not allow us to perform a direct comparison. © 2026 The Author(s).
